item.title: pod — Sat, Nov 14
item.description:
School

Start with what slipped. The Prokaryotic Cell extra credit assignment was due last night at midnight and shows as missing. It was worth zero points, so there's no grade damage, but it's marked missing.

Tonight at midnight, your Physics homework eleven is due. It's worth ten points and isn't submitted yet. Monday night at midnight, you have two things. The Prokaryotic Cell Quiz twelve is worth fifteen points. Your Linear Algebra Homework ten is worth thirty, and it's the one your professor pushed to Monday. Then Wednesday at seven in the morning, the physics lab prelab on standing waves and resonance is due. It's worth five points.

The deadline watcher only sent warnings since yesterday. It flagged the extra credit with about twelve hours left, and it flagged Physics homework eleven around midnight with about twenty-four hours left. It didn't submit the extra credit, and the homework is still open. The watcher's automatic work kicks in at six hours left, so that's about six tonight. Don't count on it. Do the homework yourself.

Two new grades in Physics. Exam two came back at nine out of twenty. Your professor posted that question seven, the hand grenade problem, was ambiguous, so everyone gets one point. Your iClicker grade is twenty-nine out of fifty-eight. Your Physics score rose from about sixty-six and a half to sixty-eight and a half, still a B minus.

Two other classes are below a B. Linear Algebra sits at seventy-five and a half, a C, unchanged. Abstract Algebra is at fifty-four percent with no letter grade yet, also unchanged. Prokaryotic Cell is an A minus, and the physics lab is an A.

On email, there are fresh replies from Friday afternoon and evening about your research assistant setup with Professor AitSahlia. Those include the WRDS account request and the onboarding for an unpaid undergrad assistant. You've read them all. Separately, a reminder from the college says Monday at eleven fifty-nine at night is the last day to drop a course without penalty.

On registration, Spring twenty twenty-seven is open now. You have no holds and nothing on your to-do list.

The one thing today is Physics homework eleven, due tonight at midnight.

Projects

You have several things waiting today, mostly in AlphaThread.

First, AlphaThread. Two scheduled jobs failed again last night. The evening research shadow run timed out downloading volatility data, and the afternoon snapshot job failed on its futures step. Both have now failed three days running, and neither has a later successful run. Two questions are also holding up the work queue. The filings study needs a contact string for the SEC's EDGAR user agent, and you already chose to run it. The other question is how the worker should get forward daily profit and loss for each sleeve. The proposal is to extend the afternoon snapshot, which is an interactive change.

Next, the Discord feed. The health step failed again, and the listener still reports eight unfilled gaps. It's the same problem as yesterday, and deletes inside those gaps are invisible.

Last, calculators. You need to decide whether to move the lo-fi content kit to Ready. The recommendation is yes, next run. The other options are to wait until samples arrive, or drop it. You also have two reminders. Send the US quote request to LegalZoom and Jaburg Wilk if you haven't yet, and pick a time for the pre-order admin session.

Now the projects, starting with AlphaThread development. The research queue moved well overnight. The study of a fresh twenty-day volatility low came back dead. SPY was weaker over the next five days, not stronger, and the result did not survive the multiple-test correction. The sleeve correlation study also finished. Every link in the tree was significant, and the tree formed one connected group. That is probably over-powered given more than eleven hundred days of data. The two index futures sleeves are correlated at about point nine five. A follow-up with a fixed null model has also run. The screen farm leaderboard was refreshed, and a new reel note on the first thirty minutes of the Nasdaq futures session was filed. It predicts range, not direction, and hasn't been tested against trailing average range. The broker bridge dropped and recovered four times in the last day, up from once yesterday. No detail is available on why. On specification twenty-seven, the open work is the deploy-gate dry run, then your merge to main, and then going live on Lucid. Your checkout is still on the signal sleeve branch with uncommitted changes. The runner process is up. The sleeve correlation re-run waits on your answer about forward profit and loss.

Calculators had a clean overnight run. The check on the FCC ruling came back negative again. It is still not in the Federal Register or on public inspection, and the negative check is dated in the notes. Reel triage handled three notes. Two went to the playbook, and one was discarded. The overnight report sits on its own branch, and nothing was pushed, sent, published or paid. Tomorrow's task is the next FCC recheck. Still blocked are the admin session, which needs you, and the video editor spike, which waits for real product footage. You are also waiting on the US attorneys and on the written quote from Li Changgen via Nathan.

On the Discord feed, curation itself ran. It now watches one hundred seventy-six channels across eighteen servers, with eleven channels added and none removed. Odd Lots, TPE's School and Quanted had nothing worth watching.

The research ideas watcher ran fine. It looked at forty-eight items, five from Instagram and forty-three from Reddit. One new idea came out of it. It says bear call spreads on stocks stretched above their two-hundred-day average underperform random entry. It is defined risk and could be run live. It scored three and was not queued. The support is one commenter's view, so treat it as an untested hypothesis. The inbox now holds eighty-seven ideas, thirty-nine of them queued.

The kalq server hunt and the extra AlphaThread worktrees are idle, with nothing new in either.

Most of today comes down to the failed jobs and the two blocked questions.

Markets

Stocks slipped on Friday, with Nvidia's turmoil pulling tech lower, but the S&P 500 still finished a strong week.

The regime is mixed. The S&P 500 trend has been mixed for seven sessions, sitting above its two-hundred-day average but below its fifty-day. Volatility is high, with the VIX at about nineteen, and that label has held for two sessions. The VIX curve is in contango, four sessions running, which is the calmer shape. And implied volatility is below realized, a negative gap, for five sessions now. Options are pricing less movement than stocks have actually delivered.

On the day, the S&P 500 fell about a third of a percent, and the Nasdaq 100 dropped about one point two percent. Small caps slipped about a third of a percent, while the Dow edged up about a tenth. Volume was light across all four, roughly three quarters to four fifths of normal, so these were gentle moves that could reverse easily.

Under the surface, tech fell about two percent, the worst sector. Consumer staples rose about one and a half percent, the best, and energy gained about one percent. The ten-year yield rose to about five point one five percent, and the dollar index closed at a one-year high. Bitcoin fell about four percent on heavier volume, about one and two thirds times normal, and is down roughly eight and a half percent over five days. That is more conviction than the stock moves had.

Now the unusual stuff. Nvidia fell about two percent on nearly double its normal volume, after gapping up at the open and then selling off. A gap that fades like that often means early buyers were overwhelmed by sellers. AMD fell almost nine percent, after opening only about three percent lower, so it kept sliding through the day. Defensive names like Coca-Cola, Procter and Gamble, and Johnson and Johnson hit new one-year highs while tech weakened. That can mean money rotating toward safety, though one day is not a trend.

Sentiment shifted too. StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so changes against a ticker's own history matter more than its level. The bullish share on the S&P 500 ETF was about thirty-one percent, far below its recent average near fifty-six.

As for why, Yahoo Finance reports the major indexes ended lower amid Nvidia turmoil, but still posted their best week since August. CNBC reports that Nvidia is done with Jensen Huang, and that the fallout in Washington is just beginning. MarketWatch says Nvidia's stock is on a losing streak not seen in fourteen years. The causes of the bitcoin drop and the yield rise are unclear from today's headlines.

Concept of the day: Breadth confirms a trend. Breadth measures how many stocks join a move, not how far the index moves. About seventy-two percent of S&P 500 stocks are above their fifty-day average, up from about sixty-three percent five days ago. Advancers beat decliners, three hundred seventeen to one hundred eighty-three, even as the index dipped. That suggests the rally is broad, not carried by a few big names. For options, strong breadth means an index view and single-stock views agree, so an index position is less hostage to a handful of names. Watch for that share falling out of the strong band while the index holds up.

AlphaThread

Quiet morning. No trades opened or closed, no halts, and no reconciliation breaks. The one health note is that your flow levels futures snapshot is still stale, so its numbers may be old. Your other sleeves have no restarts since yesterday.

Three research studies are flagged as updated. The question of whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is still open, and the one creator tested so far does not predict direction. The study on low relative volatility in mega caps says it needs a better test. The follow-up asking whether implied volatility underprices what comes after that flag also needs a better test, and with fifty-six flags it can't be told apart from chance.

Two new ideas landed in your inbox. One says bear call spreads on stocks stretched above their two-hundred-day average do worse than random entry. The other says large caps bounce after a record weekly down-streak. The inbox is up to eighty-seven ideas.

The R eleven score did not move. Your real trades are six closed, averaging down about a quarter of a risk unit. The placebo trades are ten closed, averaging up about two-thirds of a unit. The bar needs thirty closed real trades and a positive edge over placebo, so you're well short.

On to the roll call. Nothing is live yet. Your broker account is only approved for the most basic options level, so it can't trade your strategies.

On paper, the main store runs the demo put spread. It has twelve closed trades, down seventy dollars, with one SPY put spread still open. That's twelve of twenty trades toward going live, and twenty-seven of ninety days.

Copy Mordy has no closed trades yet. It's at zero of twenty trades and nineteen of ninety days.

Flow levels is running cleanly. It has two closed trades, up eleven dollars. That's two of twenty trades and eighteen of ninety days.

Flow levels futures is running, with no closed trades. It's at zero of twenty trades and eight of ninety days. It's also a research session, so it can't be promoted to live as configured.

Paper profit and loss uses mid-price fills, so treat it as an upper bound on what real trading would have done.

On research, a few studies are waiting on you. The calendar and gap findings from R three want your review, and R four needs your approval for one probe to close out its cause. R five, the data request budget plan, is still a proposal. R ten, the Discord caller copy test, is collecting data, with nine calls against the forty it needs. R eleven is being scored, as above. R thirteen and R eighteen are pre-registered and blocked on data. R twenty-three is logging forward calls, with no result yet. The remaining studies are closed or parked.

item.title: pod — Fri, Nov 13
item.description:
School

Good morning. Here's school for Friday.

Due tonight at midnight is the extra credit assignment for Prokaryotic Cell. It's worth zero points, but it hasn't been submitted. Tomorrow night, Saturday at midnight, your Physics homework eleven is due. It's worth ten points.

Monday night at midnight you have two things. Linear Algebra homework ten is worth thirty points, and Dr. Kim extended it from today because there's no lecture or office hours this morning. Also Monday night is Prokaryotic Cell Quiz twelve, worth fifteen points. Wednesday at seven in the morning, the physics lab prelab on standing waves and resonance is due. It's worth five points. Nothing is overdue.

The deadline watcher flagged two items just after midnight. The Prokaryotic Cell extra credit and Physics homework eleven were both still unsubmitted. It starts doing them itself at six hours left, so nothing has been submitted yet. It had no login problems.

For grades, Physics Quiz nine came back at seven and a half out of ten. Your Physics grade is sixty-six and a half, a B minus, down slightly from sixty-seven since your last briefing. Abstract Algebra dropped from about sixty-five to fifty-four, with no new grade posted that explains it. Check that gradebook. Linear Algebra holds at seventy-five and a half, a C. Prokaryotic Cell is steady at an A minus, and the physics lab is an A.

Two Physics office hours changed. Today's session is by Zoom because the teaching assistant is sick. Another one moves from Tuesday to Wednesday, periods four and five.

In email, Professor AitSahlia asked to meet this afternoon at two about the data sponsorship for your study. Also, Monday at eleven fifty-nine at night is the last day to drop a course without penalty. Two Perusall reminders are still unread for modules ten and eleven in Prokaryotic Cell. Both are labeled for the graduate section only, so they may not apply to you.

On registration, Spring registration is open and you're eligible. You have no holds and no to-dos.

The most important thing today is finishing the Prokaryotic Cell extra credit before midnight and making your two o'clock meeting.

Projects

Here's what needs you today.

AlphaThread first. The paper runner still looks doubtful. The paper database was last written about a hundred and four hours ago, and the newest runner log is from Tuesday night. Yet seven runner processes have been up since yesterday morning. Markets are closed, so it isn't flagged stale, but it didn't move through yesterday's session. Check it before the open.

Two scheduled jobs are also still failing. The volatility shadow job timed out downloading from FRED last night, and the afternoon snapshot job failed on one futures step. Both failed the day before as well, with no success since.

Two worker tasks are blocked on you. On the filings sector signal, decide whether to drop it now or run the first baseline. If you run it, the worker needs a contact string for the EDGAR user agent. The other task, the multi-strategy test, needs four answers. Which profit and loss streams to use? The suggestion is replayed backtests over one common in-sample window. Should the afternoon snapshot be extended to write daily profit and loss rows? Which sleeves are in scope? And should the underlyings-only page run now or wait? Waiting is suggested.

On Discord feed, the health check failed again. The listener is connected but reports eight unfilled gaps, and deletes inside them are invisible. That's the same as yesterday.

For calculators, you have three founder items. You're waiting on the written quote from Li Changgen via Nathan, covering scope and unit prices at five hundred and a thousand. The trademark quote requests still need to go out. And you need to pick a time for the admin session before the first real listing.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread development moved well. Four queue tasks finished: the last-half-hour momentum test on ES and NQ, the option signals replication, the Congress buy-cluster test, and the scoping page for the filings agent. There were thirteen commits across research branches. The fix stack merge that was blocked yesterday no longer appears as a question, and there's now a fresh scratch merge branch for it. One new task was queued from the idea watcher. Your checkout is on the signal sleeve branch with two uncommitted files. On the open specification, the deploy-gate dry run is waiting, and the merge and go-live on Lucid is for you as operator. The broker bridge connected, dropped and recovered once each, far quieter than yesterday's nine drops. Health is a warning, down from a problem.

Calculators had an ok overnight run. The FCC rule is still not in the Federal Register, and the recheck repeats tomorrow. A new task was queued for a zero-skill lo-fi content kit, and three more reel notes were filed. The admin session remains the blocker, and the editor spike waits on product footage.

IG ideas ran fine this morning. It found five new ideas, and the top-scoring one, about VIX closing at a multi-week low, was queued for AlphaThread. The inbox holds eighty-five ideas, thirty-nine of them queued. Creator and Reddit claims are still untested hypotheses.

Discord feed's watch list was refreshed this morning at one hundred sixty-five channels in fifteen servers, with one added and one removed. There were no commits.

Two projects are idle. The server hunt has no news, and its status file hasn't been updated since the first, so its current state is unclear. The AlphaThread worktrees just mirror the shared commits.

The runner check before the open is the one that can't wait.

Markets

Stocks slipped yesterday, with small caps taking the worst of it, as the ten-year yield pushed above five percent and Nvidia's leadership turmoil kept weighing on tech.

The big regime news is volatility. The VIX rose to about nineteen, and its one-year rank moved the label from normal to high, a change that is one day old. The trend is mixed, six sessions running: the S&P 500 sits below its fifty-day average but above its two-hundred-day. The VIX curve is in contango, three sessions now, meaning markets expect calm to resume. And implied versus realized volatility is negative, four sessions in a row. Realized volatility, about twenty-three percent, is running above the VIX.

Now the moves. The S&P 500 fell about a third of a percent, and the Nasdaq 100 dropped about the same. The Dow was down about four tenths. Small caps were the weak spot, down about one and a half percent. Volume on the indexes was well below normal, roughly three quarters of average for the S&P 500, so these were quiet drops, easier to reverse than conviction selling.

Rates and commodities moved more. The ten-year yield rose to about five point one percent, up about two percent on the day. The dollar edged up to a one-year high. Gold fell nearly three percent to a one-year low. Oil rose about two and a half percent, and energy was the best sector, up about one and a half. Bitcoin dropped about three and a half percent.

Three things stand out. First, breadth. Only about one hundred twenty-five S&P 500 stocks rose, against about three hundred seventy-six that fell, a much worse picture than the small index drop suggests. Often that means the weakness was widespread while a few large names held the index up. Still, about seventy percent of stocks sit above their fifty-day average, so the underlying trend is intact.

Second, Nvidia. It gapped down about thirteen percent at the open on volume about four and a half times normal, then recovered to close down about four percent, and it hit a new one-year low. A big gap that gets partly bought back can show dip buyers stepping in, though one day proves little. Supermicro fell about eleven percent, and Dell, Sandisk and other AI hardware names gapped lower too. Yet AMD and Broadcom rose more than five percent, so the AI trade split rather than moved as one.

Third, defensive and quality names. Apple, Berkshire, Johnson and Johnson, Coca-Cola and Eli Lilly made new one-year highs while the indexes slipped. That can signal money rotating toward steadier companies.

On sentiment, StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so shifts against a ticker's own history matter more than levels. Bullish share on small caps fell to about twenty-nine percent, far below its recent average of about seventy-one. That fits the day's small cap drop.

As for why, Investing.com reports that Nasdaq futures are dipping as Nvidia's tumult keeps investors on edge, and CNBC reports a scandal over Chinese chip sales has drawn in Commerce Secretary Lutnick, who reportedly agreed to testify. CNBC also reported earlier that the ten-year yield jumped back above five percent as oil gained and more Fed rate hikes were expected. The cause of gold's slide is unclear from the data.

Concept of the day: when realized beats implied. A delta-hedged long option profits when the underlying moves more than the option was priced for, and a hedged short option loses. Today the VIX is about nineteen while realized volatility is about twenty-three, so the market has moved more than options imply. That usually happens right after a shock, and Nvidia's turmoil fits. In this regime, being long gamma has historically been more favorable, while short premium has faced bigger moves than it was paid for. Defined-risk structures limit the damage if the swings continue. Watch for the spread turning positive again, usually as the twenty-day realized volatility rolls off the shock days.

AlphaThread

Nothing traded overnight, and no profit or loss moved on any sleeve. Two things need a look. Your flow levels and flow levels futures processes each restarted once in the last day, both yesterday morning, and both are running now. The flow levels futures snapshot is also stale. Its numbers are from last week, so treat them as old.

On research, three studies changed status. The question about Instagram creators' stock calls stays open, and the one creator tested so far still does not predict direction. The study on low relative volatility in mega-caps still needs a better test. The follow-up on whether implied volatility underprices what comes next also needs a better test, because the result looks like chance.

Five new ideas landed in the inbox. The top one asks whether a VIX close at a fresh multi-week low leads to SPY continuing up. The inbox holds eighty-five ideas in all, and thirty-nine are queued.

The R eleven score did not move. Your real trades are six closed, averaging down about a quarter of a risk unit. The placebo trades are ten closed, averaging up about two thirds of a unit. The bar needs thirty closed real trades and a clear edge over placebo, so it is nowhere near met.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. IBKR is your primary broker, but the account is only at options Level 1.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve has twelve of twenty trades toward going live and twenty-six of ninety days. It is down seventy dollars realized, with one position still open. Your copy Mordy sleeve has no closed trades, zero of twenty, and eighteen of ninety days.

Flow levels has two of twenty trades and seventeen of ninety days. It is up eleven dollars realized. Flow levels futures has no trades, zero of twenty, and eight of ninety days. item.content:encoded:
School

Good morning. Here's school for Friday.

Due tonight at midnight is the extra credit assignment for Prokaryotic Cell. It's worth zero points, but it hasn't been submitted. Tomorrow night, Saturday at midnight, your Physics homework eleven is due. It's worth ten points.

Monday night at midnight you have two things. Linear Algebra homework ten is worth thirty points, and Dr. Kim extended it from today because there's no lecture or office hours this morning. Also Monday night is Prokaryotic Cell Quiz twelve, worth fifteen points. Wednesday at seven in the morning, the physics lab prelab on standing waves and resonance is due. It's worth five points. Nothing is overdue.

The deadline watcher flagged two items just after midnight. The Prokaryotic Cell extra credit and Physics homework eleven were both still unsubmitted. It starts doing them itself at six hours left, so nothing has been submitted yet. It had no login problems.

For grades, Physics Quiz nine came back at seven and a half out of ten. Your Physics grade is sixty-six and a half, a B minus, down slightly from sixty-seven since your last briefing. Abstract Algebra dropped from about sixty-five to fifty-four, with no new grade posted that explains it. Check that gradebook. Linear Algebra holds at seventy-five and a half, a C. Prokaryotic Cell is steady at an A minus, and the physics lab is an A.

Two Physics office hours changed. Today's session is by Zoom because the teaching assistant is sick. Another one moves from Tuesday to Wednesday, periods four and five.

In email, Professor AitSahlia asked to meet this afternoon at two about the data sponsorship for your study. Also, Monday at eleven fifty-nine at night is the last day to drop a course without penalty. Two Perusall reminders are still unread for modules ten and eleven in Prokaryotic Cell. Both are labeled for the graduate section only, so they may not apply to you.

On registration, Spring registration is open and you're eligible. You have no holds and no to-dos.

The most important thing today is finishing the Prokaryotic Cell extra credit before midnight and making your two o'clock meeting.

Projects

Here's what needs you today.

AlphaThread first. The paper runner still looks doubtful. The paper database was last written about a hundred and four hours ago, and the newest runner log is from Tuesday night. Yet seven runner processes have been up since yesterday morning. Markets are closed, so it isn't flagged stale, but it didn't move through yesterday's session. Check it before the open.

Two scheduled jobs are also still failing. The volatility shadow job timed out downloading from FRED last night, and the afternoon snapshot job failed on one futures step. Both failed the day before as well, with no success since.

Two worker tasks are blocked on you. On the filings sector signal, decide whether to drop it now or run the first baseline. If you run it, the worker needs a contact string for the EDGAR user agent. The other task, the multi-strategy test, needs four answers. Which profit and loss streams to use? The suggestion is replayed backtests over one common in-sample window. Should the afternoon snapshot be extended to write daily profit and loss rows? Which sleeves are in scope? And should the underlyings-only page run now or wait? Waiting is suggested.

On Discord feed, the health check failed again. The listener is connected but reports eight unfilled gaps, and deletes inside them are invisible. That's the same as yesterday.

For calculators, you have three founder items. You're waiting on the written quote from Li Changgen via Nathan, covering scope and unit prices at five hundred and a thousand. The trademark quote requests still need to go out. And you need to pick a time for the admin session before the first real listing.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread development moved well. Four queue tasks finished: the last-half-hour momentum test on ES and NQ, the option signals replication, the Congress buy-cluster test, and the scoping page for the filings agent. There were thirteen commits across research branches. The fix stack merge that was blocked yesterday no longer appears as a question, and there's now a fresh scratch merge branch for it. One new task was queued from the idea watcher. Your checkout is on the signal sleeve branch with two uncommitted files. On the open specification, the deploy-gate dry run is waiting, and the merge and go-live on Lucid is for you as operator. The broker bridge connected, dropped and recovered once each, far quieter than yesterday's nine drops. Health is a warning, down from a problem.

Calculators had an ok overnight run. The FCC rule is still not in the Federal Register, and the recheck repeats tomorrow. A new task was queued for a zero-skill lo-fi content kit, and three more reel notes were filed. The admin session remains the blocker, and the editor spike waits on product footage.

IG ideas ran fine this morning. It found five new ideas, and the top-scoring one, about VIX closing at a multi-week low, was queued for AlphaThread. The inbox holds eighty-five ideas, thirty-nine of them queued. Creator and Reddit claims are still untested hypotheses.

Discord feed's watch list was refreshed this morning at one hundred sixty-five channels in fifteen servers, with one added and one removed. There were no commits.

Two projects are idle. The server hunt has no news, and its status file hasn't been updated since the first, so its current state is unclear. The AlphaThread worktrees just mirror the shared commits.

The runner check before the open is the one that can't wait.

Markets

Stocks slipped yesterday, with small caps taking the worst of it, as the ten-year yield pushed above five percent and Nvidia's leadership turmoil kept weighing on tech.

The big regime news is volatility. The VIX rose to about nineteen, and its one-year rank moved the label from normal to high, a change that is one day old. The trend is mixed, six sessions running: the S&P 500 sits below its fifty-day average but above its two-hundred-day. The VIX curve is in contango, three sessions now, meaning markets expect calm to resume. And implied versus realized volatility is negative, four sessions in a row. Realized volatility, about twenty-three percent, is running above the VIX.

Now the moves. The S&P 500 fell about a third of a percent, and the Nasdaq 100 dropped about the same. The Dow was down about four tenths. Small caps were the weak spot, down about one and a half percent. Volume on the indexes was well below normal, roughly three quarters of average for the S&P 500, so these were quiet drops, easier to reverse than conviction selling.

Rates and commodities moved more. The ten-year yield rose to about five point one percent, up about two percent on the day. The dollar edged up to a one-year high. Gold fell nearly three percent to a one-year low. Oil rose about two and a half percent, and energy was the best sector, up about one and a half. Bitcoin dropped about three and a half percent.

Three things stand out. First, breadth. Only about one hundred twenty-five S&P 500 stocks rose, against about three hundred seventy-six that fell, a much worse picture than the small index drop suggests. Often that means the weakness was widespread while a few large names held the index up. Still, about seventy percent of stocks sit above their fifty-day average, so the underlying trend is intact.

Second, Nvidia. It gapped down about thirteen percent at the open on volume about four and a half times normal, then recovered to close down about four percent, and it hit a new one-year low. A big gap that gets partly bought back can show dip buyers stepping in, though one day proves little. Supermicro fell about eleven percent, and Dell, Sandisk and other AI hardware names gapped lower too. Yet AMD and Broadcom rose more than five percent, so the AI trade split rather than moved as one.

Third, defensive and quality names. Apple, Berkshire, Johnson and Johnson, Coca-Cola and Eli Lilly made new one-year highs while the indexes slipped. That can signal money rotating toward steadier companies.

On sentiment, StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so shifts against a ticker's own history matter more than levels. Bullish share on small caps fell to about twenty-nine percent, far below its recent average of about seventy-one. That fits the day's small cap drop.

As for why, Investing.com reports that Nasdaq futures are dipping as Nvidia's tumult keeps investors on edge, and CNBC reports a scandal over Chinese chip sales has drawn in Commerce Secretary Lutnick, who reportedly agreed to testify. CNBC also reported earlier that the ten-year yield jumped back above five percent as oil gained and more Fed rate hikes were expected. The cause of gold's slide is unclear from the data.

Concept of the day: when realized beats implied. A delta-hedged long option profits when the underlying moves more than the option was priced for, and a hedged short option loses. Today the VIX is about nineteen while realized volatility is about twenty-three, so the market has moved more than options imply. That usually happens right after a shock, and Nvidia's turmoil fits. In this regime, being long gamma has historically been more favorable, while short premium has faced bigger moves than it was paid for. Defined-risk structures limit the damage if the swings continue. Watch for the spread turning positive again, usually as the twenty-day realized volatility rolls off the shock days.

AlphaThread

Nothing traded overnight, and no profit or loss moved on any sleeve. Two things need a look. Your flow levels and flow levels futures processes each restarted once in the last day, both yesterday morning, and both are running now. The flow levels futures snapshot is also stale. Its numbers are from last week, so treat them as old.

On research, three studies changed status. The question about Instagram creators' stock calls stays open, and the one creator tested so far still does not predict direction. The study on low relative volatility in mega-caps still needs a better test. The follow-up on whether implied volatility underprices what comes next also needs a better test, because the result looks like chance.

Five new ideas landed in the inbox. The top one asks whether a VIX close at a fresh multi-week low leads to SPY continuing up. The inbox holds eighty-five ideas in all, and thirty-nine are queued.

The R eleven score did not move. Your real trades are six closed, averaging down about a quarter of a risk unit. The placebo trades are ten closed, averaging up about two thirds of a unit. The bar needs thirty closed real trades and a clear edge over placebo, so it is nowhere near met.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. IBKR is your primary broker, but the account is only at options Level 1.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve has twelve of twenty trades toward going live and twenty-six of ninety days. It is down seventy dollars realized, with one position still open. Your copy Mordy sleeve has no closed trades, zero of twenty, and eighteen of ninety days.

Flow levels has two of twenty trades and seventeen of ninety days. It is up eleven dollars realized. Flow levels futures has no trades, zero of twenty, and eight of ninety days. It is also flagged as a research session that cannot go live. Remember that paper fills happen at the mid price, so these profit and loss figures are an upper bound.

Among open research, the R eleven study on Vin's reversal levels is pre-registered and being scored. The R ten study on copying a Discord caller is waiting on more data. Studies thirteen and eighteen are pre-registered and blocked on data. R twenty-three is logging forward calls. The R four timestamp question is waiting on your approval of one probe, and the R three findings are waiting on your review. The other studies are closed or parked.

item.title: pod — Thu, Nov 12
item.description:
School

This briefing is built from school data collected yesterday morning, because today's early check had not finished, so treat it as possibly out of date.

As of that check, nothing was overdue. Two things are due tomorrow, Friday, at midnight. Linear Algebra Homework ten is worth thirty points. There is also the Prokaryotic Cell extra credit assignment, which is worth no points but is still open. Physics homework eleven is due Saturday night at midnight, worth ten points. Next up is Prokaryotic Cell Quiz twelve, due Monday night at midnight, worth fifteen points.

The deadline watcher had no activity to report.

For grades, your Physics Exam two came back at eight out of twenty. The class median was thirteen, so you landed below the middle. Your Physics score sits at about sixty-seven percent, a B minus. Linear Algebra is at seventy-five and a half, a C. Abstract Algebra is at about sixty-five percent, with no letter grade posted yet. Prokaryotic Cell is a solid A minus, and the physics lab is an A.

In email, Professor AitSahlia moved your meeting about the data sponsorship because UF was closed for Veterans Day. He proposed Friday at two in the afternoon, at his office in Stuzin Hall. The data I have does not show whether you confirmed, so it is worth checking your reply. Also, the college reminded students that Monday at midnight is the last day to drop a course without penalty.

Two Perusall reminders for Prokaryotic Cell are still unread, for modules ten and eleven. Both are labeled for the graduate section only, so they may not apply to you.

Registration and records could not be checked, because the ONE.UF login failed.

The most important thing today is getting Linear Algebra Homework ten done before it is due tomorrow night.

Projects

Five things need you today, mostly on AlphaThread.

First, the most urgent. Your AlphaThread paper runner may not be doing its job. The paper database was last written Sunday night, about eighty-two hours ago. Seven runner processes started this morning, but it is unclear whether they are writing anywhere. The newest runner log is from Tuesday night. Check this before the market opens.

Second, the merge of the fix stack into main is blocked, with four questions for you. Merging the last two fixes back gives one conflict in the runner's startup file, and the worker guard blocks the merge command. You need to decide who does the re-merge. The suggestion is an interactive session that keeps both blocks of code, runs the full test suite, merges fast-forward only, and does not push. You also need to decide whether the worker may fast-forward after a green suite, and whether the guard should allow merges on scratch merge branches only.

Third, three runs failed in the last day with no later success. Signals ingest crashed at five this morning. Last night's shadow run timed out downloading the FRED volatility series. Yesterday afternoon's snapshot job failed on futures flow levels.

Fourth, the Discord feed health check failed again. The listener is connected, but it has eight unfilled gaps, up from two yesterday. Deletes inside those gaps are invisible.

Fifth, for kalq. If you have not yet, send the US trademark quote request to LegalZoom and Jaburg Wilk. Pick a time for the pre-order admin session. The written quote from Li Changgen, via Nathan, is still awaited.

Now the projects. On AlphaThread, development moved fast. Spec twenty-nine, the rule sleeves work, merged to main last night, so yesterday's wait on that looks resolved. The schedule identity fix is also on main. The regime engine spec merged too, with one performance task still open. The screen farm leaderboard refreshed, and the overnight worker ran fine. Fourteen commits landed, far fewer than yesterday's big batch. Next in the queue is a test of last-thirty-minutes momentum on ES and NQ, ready to go. Spec twenty-seven still has eight open tasks. The reel bot also filed six new notes.

On kalq, the overnight run finished fine with six commits, nothing pushed. The FCC rule is still not in the Federal Register, and the recheck repeats tomorrow. The US trademark drafts were updated, and the plan now totals about nineteen hundred fifty dollars at filing, or twenty-two fifty with statements of use. The China lines are dropped. Four new reel notes are saved but uncommitted. Still blocked: the pre-order admin session, product footage for the editing spike, and the two attorney replies.

On IG ideas, the watcher ran fine. Seven new ideas came in, none queued yet, and the inbox is at eighty. Five scored three, including long-dated SPY tail hedges, a QQQ rebound after a bad day, and a zero-day SPX butterfly. A post from vince.quant produced a new work item, and that creator is now watched. The watcher also found seven Instagram posts and fifty Reddit posts. One post is waiting for a transcript.

On the Discord feed, the curate step ran and now watches one hundred sixty-five channels, down two after removing the investor alerts and alert setup channels. The health failure is covered above.

On redditscrape, one fix landed: request addresses are now encoded properly, so posts with non-English characters in their titles can fetch their comments.

The kalq server hunt is still idle, with no update since November first, and the extra AlphaThread worktrees show nothing separate.

That is everything, and the health problems are the ones to start with.

Markets

The S&P 500 rallied about one point three percent on Wednesday, led by a burst in tech, but it happened on lighter than normal volume.

The news in the regime is volatility. The VIX fell to about seventeen and a half, which moved it from the high band to normal for the first time after four sessions in high. The trend is still mixed, now five sessions running. The VIX curve is in contango, meaning near-term fear sits below three-month fear, for two sessions. And implied volatility is below realized: the VIX at seventeen and a half against realized volatility around twenty-three. That has held three sessions. Options are priced cheaper than the market has actually been moving.

Now the moves. The S&P 500 rose about one point three percent, but on roughly eighty percent of normal volume. Light volume makes a rally easier to reverse. The Nasdaq 100 jumped about two point three percent. Tech led every sector, up about three point two percent, and that came on about one point two times normal volume, which shows more conviction. Small caps gained about nine tenths of a percent and the Dow about half a percent. Energy rose nearly two percent. The ten-year yield sat just under five percent, and the dollar index closed at a one-year high. Gold slipped about seven tenths of a percent.

On the unusual side, three things stand out. First, the opening gaps were concentrated in one theme. Coherent, Lumentum, Seagate, Ciena and Marvell all gapped up roughly eight to ten percent and held it. Optical, networking and storage names moving together often suggests money rotating into one theme, here AI hardware, and not a stock-by-stock story. Second, breadth backed the index. About three hundred thirty stocks rose against about one hundred seventy that fell, and over seventy-two percent of the S&P 500 sits above its fifty-day average. A rally with wide participation tends to be sturdier than one carried by a few names. Third, the put to call ratio dropped to about point five nine from point seven seven. Fewer people were buying protection. That can mean confidence, or complacency.

Sentiment moved the other way. On StockTwits, which skews bullish and retail, the bullish share for the S&P 500 fund fell to about twenty-six percent, against a normal near fifty-seven. The Nasdaq 100 fund fell to about twenty-nine percent. Message volume was nearly ten times normal. Retail got sharply bearish into a strong up day. Contrarians sometimes read that as fuel for more upside, but it's one reading.

For why, the data doesn't offer a clean cause for Wednesday's tech surge. What it does show is what's hanging over this morning. Investing.com reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down, and that Wall Street futures are lower. CNBC reports the ten-year yield is back above five percent, with more Fed rate hikes expected. Nvidia traded at about two times normal volume yesterday, up nearly three percent, so Wednesday's gains may be given back.

Concept of the day: a volatility regime shift. Volatility clusters, so a move into a new band tends to persist. Turbulent days follow turbulent days, and quiet follows quiet. Yesterday the VIX stepped down from nineteen and a half to about seventeen and a half, moving from high to normal. That raises the odds the next stretch looks calmer than the last. For options, premium sellers collect less after a step down, and position size usually follows the new band. Watch whether the normal label holds for several sessions, and whether the term structure keeps moving the same way.

AlphaThread

Two health items first. Flow levels and flow levels futures each restarted once in the last day, the same as yesterday. The flow levels futures snapshot is also stale. It was last updated last Friday, so treat its numbers as old.

Nothing else moved in trading. No trades opened or closed, profit and loss is unchanged, and there were no gate milestones or version changes.

Three studies changed status. These are the one on whether I G creators' stock calls predict anything, the one on whether low relative volatility in a mega-cap reverts upward, and the one on whether implied vol underprices the realized vol after that flag. Seven new ideas landed in the inbox, all scored two or three. They include long-dated SPY tail-hedge puts, a QQQ rebound after a bad day, and a QQQ lift after a VIX collapse.

R eleven moved too. Your real trades now stand at six closed, averaging minus zero point two three R. The placebo trades stand at ten closed, averaging plus zero point six six. The placebo is still ahead. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, an average of at least plus zero point one five R, and a beat over placebo by the same margin.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. Your IBKR account is still at options level one.

On paper, the demo put spread sleeve has twelve closed trades and is down seventy dollars, with one spread still open. It is twelve of twenty trades and twenty-five of ninety days toward going live. Copy Mordy has no trades yet. It is zero of twenty trades and seventeen of ninety days. Flow levels has two closed trades and is up eleven dollars, at two of twenty trades and sixteen of ninety days. Flow levels futures has no trades, at zero of twenty trades and eight of ninety days. Its latest research session also can't be promoted live, because it allowed uncovered short legs. Paper results use mid-price fills, so profit and loss is an upper bound.

On research, the I G creators study is still open, kept active at your request. The low relative volatility study and its implied vol follow-up both need a better test. R ten, copying a Discord caller, needs more data, and the paper forward test is how it gets answered. R thirteen and R eighteen, the two intraday studies, are blocked on data. R five, the capture universe budget, needs a better test. R four is waiting on your approval of one probe, and R three is waiting on your review. R twenty-three is logging calls with no result yet. The other studies are closed, parked or built.

In the inbox, eighty ideas total, thirty-eight queued. Discord had sixty-two new alerts from seventeen callers. They are unscored.

item.title: pod — Wed, Nov 11
item.description:
School

Good morning. No classes today for Veterans Day, and nothing is overdue.

Next up is Friday night at midnight. Your Linear Algebra Homework 10 is due, worth thirty points, and it isn't submitted yet. The Prokaryotic Cell extra credit assignment is also due then. It's worth no points, but it's extra credit. Saturday night at midnight, your Physics homework 11 is due, worth ten points. Then Monday night at midnight, Prokaryotic Cell Quiz 12 closes, worth fifteen points.

The deadline watcher had nothing to report since yesterday.

For grades, Physics Exam 2 was posted: you got eight out of twenty. Your professor said the median was thirteen, so this one came in below the middle. It pulled your Physics score down from about seventy-eight to about sixty-seven, which moves you from a B plus to a B minus. Your professor also says the solutions are in the Old Exams area of Resources, if you want to see where the points went.

Your other classes didn't move. Prokaryotic Cell is at an A minus, the physics lab is an A, Linear Algebra is a C at about seventy-five and a half, and Abstract Algebra is at about sixty-five with no letter grade showing yet.

On email, Professor AitSahlia wrote that UF is closed today, so your eleven forty-five meeting about the data sponsorship is off. He asked if you can meet Friday at two in the afternoon instead. Nothing in today's data shows a reply from you yet.

Also, the college reminded students that Monday is the last day to drop a course without penalty. Changes have to be made in ONE.UF before eleven fifty-nine that night.

Registration and records could not be checked today, because the ONE.UF login failed. Nothing there is flagged, but it's worth a look later.

The most important thing today is to answer Professor AitSahlia about Friday at two, and to get a start on Linear Algebra Homework 10 before it's due Friday night.

Projects

Here is what needs you today.

On AlphaThread, two jobs failed. The continuous signals ingest crashed last night just before eleven. The four-thirty sleeve snapshot also failed again on the futures flow-levels part, the same one that failed the day before. Neither has a later good run recorded.

You also have three decisions. First, the merge-fix stack is built and tested. Main needs to be moved up to it with a fast-forward only and no push. Main has moved since the early hours, so check that it is still a clean fast-forward. Second, you're asked whether the overnight worker may do those fast-forward merges itself after a green test suite. The recommended answer is no. Third, the rule farm work is complete, and its operator steps wait on your merge approval.

For Discord feed, the daily health step failed again at four. The listener has two gaps it hasn't filled, and deleted messages inside them can't be seen.

For kalq, the pre-order launch setup still needs an admin session with you, covering Shopify admin and the pre-order app settings. You're also waiting on the two American attorney replies. The report says you send that request. The written design quote from Li Changgen, via Nathan, is also still outstanding.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread moved a lot. Yesterday you had five separate fix branches waiting. They are now merged into one tested stack. That is the item waiting on your fast-forward. The rule sleeves spec finished all sixty-six tasks. The minimum viable version and its kill rule are already on main. A new branch adds a long-only fifteen-minute opening range breakout for micro Nasdaq futures, with paper launcher templates. A new architecture decision record is proposed. Cash adjustment work for the signal sleeve spec also landed. A separate research task, a backtest overfitting check, finished on its own branch and is not merged. Commit volume across branches jumped to two hundred forty-seven. Next up are the remaining open tasks on the Nasdaq bridge spec. The one thing blocked is that main's ref move is left to an interactive session. On health, the runner is up with seven processes. The database write log hasn't changed since Sunday night, about fifty-five hours. The market is closed, so it isn't counted as stale. The bridge also recorded six reconciliation breaks and two broker connections. No phone alerts fired.

IG ideas is healthy. The watcher ran at about five this morning and produced seven new ideas, after none yesterday. Four scored three. They cover short premium paying only when implied volatility beats realized, mechanical exits on credit spreads, post-earnings drift with strong momentum, and thin overnight gaps in volatile tech stocks reversing. None are queued. The inbox is at seventy-three ideas, thirty-eight queued. The scrape found three new Instagram posts and four Reddit posts, and one Instagram post is still waiting on a transcript.

Discord feed is the same failure as yesterday. The watch list refreshed to one hundred sixty-seven channels across fifteen servers, adding one retail channel and dropping one personal finance channel. The listener is connected. The only next step is fixing those two gaps.

Kalq had a clean overnight run with five commits, and nothing pushed or sent. The federal rule recheck found it is still not in the Federal Register, so the next recheck is tomorrow. The attorney quote comparison sheet is done. One reel note went into the tactics file. The editing spike still waits on product footage.

Redditscrape got its first commit overnight, a receive-only scraper over the public Reddit feeds.

Everything else is quiet. Kalq server hunt hasn't been updated since November first. Its follow-ups were due on the third and fourth, and their state is unclear. Sixty-three other AlphaThread checkouts show the same commits as the main project.

That's the picture. The two failed jobs and the merge decision are the places to start.

Markets

Stocks slipped on Tuesday, giving back a bit of Monday's big rally, while the ten-year yield jumped and tech took the hit.

On the regime, the news is the term structure. Volatility futures moved into contango, meaning near-term fear sits below three-month fear, but that label is only one day old. The S&P 500 trend is mixed, held for four sessions. Volatility is high against its own past year, also four sessions. And implied volatility sits below realized, the VIX at about nineteen and a half against realized near twenty-two, for the second session in a row.

Now the moves. The S&P 500 fell about four tenths of a percent. The Nasdaq 100 lost about seven tenths, and small caps matched that. The Dow was the strongest, down about three tenths. Volume was light everywhere, around eighty percent of normal or lower, so this was a drift, not a conviction sell-off, and light-volume moves are easier to reverse.

Tech was the weak spot, down about one point one percent, and about four percent over five days. Financials rose about half a percent. The ten-year yield rose to about five percent, up two and a half percent in relative terms. Higher yields tend to pressure growth stocks, which fits tech lagging. The dollar rose about half a percent. Gold fell about two percent, on slightly heavy volume, and bitcoin dropped about two percent.

Now the unusual. Nvidia fell about five and a half percent on more than three times normal volume. That is real conviction, and with the stock heavy in the indexes it explains much of tech's drop. Second, breadth held up better than the index. Advancers and decliners were nearly even, and the share of stocks above their fifty-day average rose to about seventy percent. One read is that the damage was concentrated in a few big names, not broad selling. Third, Take-Two jumped over eight percent on nearly three times normal volume, a sign of company-specific news, probably earnings.

On sentiment, StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so only changes against its own norm matter. Bullish share on the S&P 500 ETF was around ninety percent, far above its thirty-day average near fifty-five. Extreme retail optimism often shows up before pauses, though one day is not a trend.

On why, CNBC reports Nvidia shares rebounded five percent Wednesday morning as Jensen Huang faces scrutiny ahead of earnings, which is the overhang behind Tuesday's drop. MarketWatch says Goldman Sachs is changing its Federal Reserve rate forecast, and yesterday's headlines had Fed Governor Waller opening the door to a December hike, which fits the higher yield. Oil moves are unclear from today's data alone.

Concept of the day: after a shock, realized runs ahead. The VIX is about nineteen and a half, yet realized volatility is near twenty-two, because the last twenty days include big swings like Monday's rally of over two percent. The VIX looks thirty days forward and already assumes some calming. That means short premium has recently been paid less than the market delivered. Defined-risk structures and smaller size are the usual response. Watch for the gap turning positive as the shock days roll out of the window.

AlphaThread

Quiet on the trading side. Nothing opened or closed, and profit and loss didn't move for any sleeve.

The one health note is restarts. Flow levels and flow levels futures each restarted once overnight, shortly after eleven. Both are running now. That's down from three restarts each the day before. Also, the flow levels futures snapshot is stale. It's still from Friday, so treat its numbers as old. No halts and no reconciliation breaks anywhere.

On research, three studies changed status. The one on whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is still open, with no direction signal from the one creator tested. The low relative volatility study and its implied volatility follow-up both changed too. Both say they need a better test. The follow-up found a small gap that can't be told apart from chance. Seven new ideas also landed in the inbox, mostly about short premium, mechanical exits on credit spreads, post-earnings drift, and overnight gaps. The R eleven score didn't move.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. Your broker account is only approved for the most basic options level.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve has twelve closed trades and is down seventy dollars overall. It still holds one SPY put spread. It sits at twelve of twenty trades toward going live and twenty-four of ninety days.

Copy Mordy has no closed trades yet. It's at zero of twenty trades and sixteen of ninety days.

Flow levels has two closed trades and is up eleven dollars. It's at two of twenty trades and fifteen of ninety days.

Flow levels futures has no trades yet, at zero of twenty and eight of ninety days. It's also marked as a research session, so it can't be promoted to live as configured.

All paper results use mid-price fills, so profit and loss is an upper bound on real trading.

For research, the three studies above are the ones that moved. R ten, copying a Discord caller, is still waiting on more data. R eleven, the reversal levels study, has five real closed trades averaging a loss of about four hundredths of an R, against eight placebo trades averaging a gain of about one point one R. The bar needs thirty closed trades and an average of at least fifteen hundredths of an R, so it's far from passing. The other studies are unchanged.

The ideas inbox holds seventy-three ideas, with thirty-eight queued. Discord had seventy-five new caller alerts from twelve callers, none of them scored.

item.title: pod — Tue, Nov 10
item.description:
School

Good morning. Nothing is due today or tomorrow, but one item is still overdue. Your Physics Exam 2 was due Friday at eight twenty p.m. It's worth twenty points and still shows as not submitted.

Coming up this week, Prokaryotic Cell has an extra credit assignment due Friday at midnight. It's worth no points, so it's purely optional. Your Physics homework eleven is due Saturday at midnight and is worth ten points. Then Prokaryotic Cell Quiz twelve is due Monday at midnight, worth fifteen points.

On the deadline watcher, it sent reminders yesterday about Prokaryotic Cell Quiz eleven. It also flagged that quiz as proctored, so it left it for you to do yourself. That worked out. The quiz posted last night at fifteen out of fifteen, and your Prokaryotic Cell grade rose from ninety-three point six to ninety-four point three, still an A minus.

Two classes are below a B, and neither changed since yesterday. Linear Algebra sits at seventy-five point five, a C. Abstract Algebra is at sixty-four point six, with no letter grade assigned yet. Physics is at seventy-eight point two, a B plus. The physics lab is an A at about ninety-six.

On email, the most important item is Professor AitSahlia, who confirmed a meeting with you tomorrow, Wednesday, at eleven forty-five a.m. It's about sponsorship for your data study. Stop by his office in Stuzin Hall, room three oh one F.

Also, Monday is the last day to drop a course without penalty. Changes have to be made in ONE.UF before eleven fifty-nine p.m.

You also have unread Perusall reminders for assignments ten and eleven in Prokaryotic Cell. Both are marked for the graduate section only, so they may not apply to you. And there's still an unread Physics email about Exam 2 reviews.

For registration, Spring registration is open now and stays open until late April. You have no holds and no to-dos, and your cumulative GPA is three point six eight.

The most important thing today is the overdue Physics Exam 2. Check whether it can still be turned in, and get it sorted before the rest of the week fills up.

Projects

You have a busy list this morning, mostly on AlphaThread.

Starting with AlphaThread. Yesterday afternoon's snapshot job failed. Three of its four outputs were written, the futures one failed, and no later run is recorded. Separately, the runner's paper database has not been written since Sunday night, about thirty-one hours ago. Nothing was recorded during Monday's session. The runner processes are running and it isn't flagged stale outside market hours, but the cause is unclear, so it's worth a look. The Guru relay blocker is also still open. It skips every Guru post because the relay repeats the text. A fix branch exists, but it's unclear whether it waits on you. And five stacked fix branches are finished and waiting for your review and merge.

Next, the Discord feed. The health check failed again, this time on two unfilled gaps. Deletes inside them are invisible. The listener itself is running and connected.

For calculators, two things. The pre-order launch setup needs your admin session, covering the product and notification screens and the Shopify order confirmation. And two quote requests were drafted overnight and are ready to send. One goes to the US attorneys, LegalZoom and Jaburg Wilk. The other is the written-quote request for Li Changgen, which goes through Nathan. Nathan should check the machine-drafted Chinese.

Now the projects. AlphaThread development first. The overnight worker finished seven tasks, and none are merged. Yesterday's blocked question about old freeze checks is gone. The freeze checks for the older specs are now done, including the newest, which accepts the dividend event. The dividend chain was also reconciled onto main in a branch of eight commits. Across all branches there were twenty-one commits in the last day. They include a gold heading fix for flow levels, a buying-power fix for the prop-firm setup, and scripts for the NVIDIA study. Next up are eight open tasks on the broker bridge spec. They include the deploy-gate dry run and your own merge to go live on Lucid. One more merge is pre-approved once a final check passes. The runner is up and no alerts fired in the last day.

On calculators, the overnight run was clean. The FCC rule is still not in the Federal Register or on public inspection. It gets rechecked tomorrow. The do-it-yourself trademark figure is now US-only, about one thousand dollars. The Li Changgen request includes a comparison against Wonderful PCB and CalcAI. Still blocked are the video editor spike, which waits on product footage, and Wonderful's revised quote, which hasn't arrived since your reply on November fifth.

IG ideas ran fine at five. Seven new posts were analysed, with no new ideas. Nothing is queued and nothing awaits a transcript.

On the Discord feed, the watch list was rebuilt. It now covers one hundred sixty-seven channels in fifteen servers, one more than yesterday, a links channel. Four servers still have nothing worth watching. Listeners now start without a console window. Yesterday's gap warning has grown from one to two.

The kalq server hunt is idle, with no movement since November first. The EpicNPC account still needs claiming, and the follow-up dates from the status file have passed with no update. The many AlphaThread worktrees show no separate activity, only the shared commits already covered.

The most time-sensitive items this morning are the runner database question and the two quote requests.

Markets

Stocks surged on Monday, with the Nasdaq 100 up about three and a half percent, as oil fell and fear drained out of the market.

The regime shifted in two ways. The volatility curve went from backwardation to flat, with the VIX at nineteen and change against the three-month VIX at about twenty-one. And implied versus realized volatility flipped to negative after fifty-two days of being rich. Realized volatility, about twenty-two, now exceeds the VIX. Options are no longer priced richer than the actual swings. Trend is still mixed and volatility still high, both for three days.

The S&P 500 rose about two point four percent, the Nasdaq 100 about three and a half, small caps about three point two, and the Dow about two point two. Volume was only slightly above normal on the S&P and Nasdaq, around one point one times, and below normal on the Dow. So this was a broad rally, but not a stampede, and it is easier to reverse than a heavy-volume move. Industrials led, up nearly four percent, and tech rose about three and three-quarters percent on one and a quarter times normal volume. Oil fell about four and a half percent to just under eighty-seven dollars, and the dollar slipped.

Breadth is the standout. Four hundred twenty-three S&P 500 stocks advanced against seventy-eight decliners. On Friday it was one eighty-five against three seventeen. About seventy percent of the index now sits above its fifty-day average, up from about sixty-three. When a rally lifts nearly everything, it often reflects a macro driver rather than a few stocks.

Nvidia went the other way. It gapped down about seven percent, finished down about four, on nearly four times normal volume. Heavy volume on a drop suggests real selling pressure. Yahoo Finance reports Nvidia's board is investigating its CEO's relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. AMD jumped about thirteen percent.

The put to call ratio fell to about point five six, which means few traders were buying protection. That can mean calm, or complacency after one good day.

On sentiment, StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so shifts against a ticker's own norm matter more than levels. The bullish share on the S&P 500 fund was about seventy-eight percent, roughly twenty-five points above its thirty-day average. But message volume was well below normal, so a thin crowd was loud.

For the cause, CNBC reports Brent crude fell below ninety dollars for the first time since August on hopes the Iran war is de-escalating, and that Trump says the war will end fairly soon. Lower oil eases cost pressure, which fits the rally in industrials and tech. Separately, CNBC reports Fed Governor Waller sees a December rate hike as likely and is open to a half-point move. That is a risk the rally has not answered.

Concept of the day: the volatility curve normalizes. The VIX over the three-month VIX fell to about point nine five five, from above one on Friday, as near-term fear faded faster than longer-term uncertainty. The VIX itself dropped nearly six points. Volatility tends to mean revert, so the curve usually slopes upward again after stress. For options, front-month premium loses its richness relative to later expiries, and the roll begins to cost long volatility holders. Watch whether the ratio stays below its contango threshold for several sessions.

AlphaThread

Two things to flag first. Your flow levels and flow levels futures processes each restarted three times in the last day. Both were clean yesterday. Flow levels futures also has an old snapshot, last updated Friday, so its numbers may be behind.

Flow levels also moved to version zero point three point one. No sleeve opened or closed a trade since yesterday, and no sleeve has a halt or a reconciliation break.

On research, three studies changed status. The one on whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything stays active, with the single creator tested so far showing no directional edge. The low relative volatility study now says it needs a better test, because the effect looks like ordinary mean reversion. Its follow-up on implied volatility says the same, since the result can't be told apart from chance.

Your R eleven score moved too. One more real trade closed, and the real average slipped from about plus a quarter of a risk unit to about zero, slightly negative. Placebo trades closed two more and still average above one risk unit. So placebo is ahead of real. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, and you have five.

Nothing is live yet. IBKR is your primary broker, but the account is still at options Level one, which is too restrictive to go live.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve has twelve of twenty trades toward going live, and twenty-three of ninety days. It is down seventy dollars realized, with one put spread still open from last Thursday. Its open profit isn't available, because that needs a live quote.

Copy Mordy has no trades yet. It stands at zero of twenty trades and fifteen of ninety days.

Flow levels has two closed trades, up eleven dollars, with fourteen of ninety days. Apart from the restarts, it is running.

Flow levels futures has no trades, zero of twenty, and eight of ninety days. It is also flagged as a research session that can't be promoted live, because it allows uncovered short legs.

All of that paper profit and loss uses mid-price fills, so treat it as an upper bound on real trading.
