item.content:encoded:
School

Good morning. Nothing is due today or tomorrow, but one item is still overdue. Your Physics Exam 2 was due Friday at eight twenty p.m. It's worth twenty points and still shows as not submitted.

Coming up this week, Prokaryotic Cell has an extra credit assignment due Friday at midnight. It's worth no points, so it's purely optional. Your Physics homework eleven is due Saturday at midnight and is worth ten points. Then Prokaryotic Cell Quiz twelve is due Monday at midnight, worth fifteen points.

On the deadline watcher, it sent reminders yesterday about Prokaryotic Cell Quiz eleven. It also flagged that quiz as proctored, so it left it for you to do yourself. That worked out. The quiz posted last night at fifteen out of fifteen, and your Prokaryotic Cell grade rose from ninety-three point six to ninety-four point three, still an A minus.

Two classes are below a B, and neither changed since yesterday. Linear Algebra sits at seventy-five point five, a C. Abstract Algebra is at sixty-four point six, with no letter grade assigned yet. Physics is at seventy-eight point two, a B plus. The physics lab is an A at about ninety-six.

On email, the most important item is Professor AitSahlia, who confirmed a meeting with you tomorrow, Wednesday, at eleven forty-five a.m. It's about sponsorship for your data study. Stop by his office in Stuzin Hall, room three oh one F.

Also, Monday is the last day to drop a course without penalty. Changes have to be made in ONE.UF before eleven fifty-nine p.m.

You also have unread Perusall reminders for assignments ten and eleven in Prokaryotic Cell. Both are marked for the graduate section only, so they may not apply to you. And there's still an unread Physics email about Exam 2 reviews.

For registration, Spring registration is open now and stays open until late April. You have no holds and no to-dos, and your cumulative GPA is three point six eight.

The most important thing today is the overdue Physics Exam 2. Check whether it can still be turned in, and get it sorted before the rest of the week fills up.

Projects

You have a busy list this morning, mostly on AlphaThread.

Starting with AlphaThread. Yesterday afternoon's snapshot job failed. Three of its four outputs were written, the futures one failed, and no later run is recorded. Separately, the runner's paper database has not been written since Sunday night, about thirty-one hours ago. Nothing was recorded during Monday's session. The runner processes are running and it isn't flagged stale outside market hours, but the cause is unclear, so it's worth a look. The Guru relay blocker is also still open. It skips every Guru post because the relay repeats the text. A fix branch exists, but it's unclear whether it waits on you. And five stacked fix branches are finished and waiting for your review and merge.

Next, the Discord feed. The health check failed again, this time on two unfilled gaps. Deletes inside them are invisible. The listener itself is running and connected.

For calculators, two things. The pre-order launch setup needs your admin session, covering the product and notification screens and the Shopify order confirmation. And two quote requests were drafted overnight and are ready to send. One goes to the US attorneys, LegalZoom and Jaburg Wilk. The other is the written-quote request for Li Changgen, which goes through Nathan. Nathan should check the machine-drafted Chinese.

Now the projects. AlphaThread development first. The overnight worker finished seven tasks, and none are merged. Yesterday's blocked question about old freeze checks is gone. The freeze checks for the older specs are now done, including the newest, which accepts the dividend event. The dividend chain was also reconciled onto main in a branch of eight commits. Across all branches there were twenty-one commits in the last day. They include a gold heading fix for flow levels, a buying-power fix for the prop-firm setup, and scripts for the NVIDIA study. Next up are eight open tasks on the broker bridge spec. They include the deploy-gate dry run and your own merge to go live on Lucid. One more merge is pre-approved once a final check passes. The runner is up and no alerts fired in the last day.

On calculators, the overnight run was clean. The FCC rule is still not in the Federal Register or on public inspection. It gets rechecked tomorrow. The do-it-yourself trademark figure is now US-only, about one thousand dollars. The Li Changgen request includes a comparison against Wonderful PCB and CalcAI. Still blocked are the video editor spike, which waits on product footage, and Wonderful's revised quote, which hasn't arrived since your reply on November fifth.

IG ideas ran fine at five. Seven new posts were analysed, with no new ideas. Nothing is queued and nothing awaits a transcript.

On the Discord feed, the watch list was rebuilt. It now covers one hundred sixty-seven channels in fifteen servers, one more than yesterday, a links channel. Four servers still have nothing worth watching. Listeners now start without a console window. Yesterday's gap warning has grown from one to two.

The kalq server hunt is idle, with no movement since November first. The EpicNPC account still needs claiming, and the follow-up dates from the status file have passed with no update. The many AlphaThread worktrees show no separate activity, only the shared commits already covered.

The most time-sensitive items this morning are the runner database question and the two quote requests.

Markets

Stocks surged on Monday, with the Nasdaq 100 up about three and a half percent, as oil fell and fear drained out of the market.

The regime shifted in two ways. The volatility curve went from backwardation to flat, with the VIX at nineteen and change against the three-month VIX at about twenty-one. And implied versus realized volatility flipped to negative after fifty-two days of being rich. Realized volatility, about twenty-two, now exceeds the VIX. Options are no longer priced richer than the actual swings. Trend is still mixed and volatility still high, both for three days.

The S&P 500 rose about two point four percent, the Nasdaq 100 about three and a half, small caps about three point two, and the Dow about two point two. Volume was only slightly above normal on the S&P and Nasdaq, around one point one times, and below normal on the Dow. So this was a broad rally, but not a stampede, and it is easier to reverse than a heavy-volume move. Industrials led, up nearly four percent, and tech rose about three and three-quarters percent on one and a quarter times normal volume. Oil fell about four and a half percent to just under eighty-seven dollars, and the dollar slipped.

Breadth is the standout. Four hundred twenty-three S&P 500 stocks advanced against seventy-eight decliners. On Friday it was one eighty-five against three seventeen. About seventy percent of the index now sits above its fifty-day average, up from about sixty-three. When a rally lifts nearly everything, it often reflects a macro driver rather than a few stocks.

Nvidia went the other way. It gapped down about seven percent, finished down about four, on nearly four times normal volume. Heavy volume on a drop suggests real selling pressure. Yahoo Finance reports Nvidia's board is investigating its CEO's relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. AMD jumped about thirteen percent.

The put to call ratio fell to about point five six, which means few traders were buying protection. That can mean calm, or complacency after one good day.

On sentiment, StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so shifts against a ticker's own norm matter more than levels. The bullish share on the S&P 500 fund was about seventy-eight percent, roughly twenty-five points above its thirty-day average. But message volume was well below normal, so a thin crowd was loud.

For the cause, CNBC reports Brent crude fell below ninety dollars for the first time since August on hopes the Iran war is de-escalating, and that Trump says the war will end fairly soon. Lower oil eases cost pressure, which fits the rally in industrials and tech. Separately, CNBC reports Fed Governor Waller sees a December rate hike as likely and is open to a half-point move. That is a risk the rally has not answered.

Concept of the day: the volatility curve normalizes. The VIX over the three-month VIX fell to about point nine five five, from above one on Friday, as near-term fear faded faster than longer-term uncertainty. The VIX itself dropped nearly six points. Volatility tends to mean revert, so the curve usually slopes upward again after stress. For options, front-month premium loses its richness relative to later expiries, and the roll begins to cost long volatility holders. Watch whether the ratio stays below its contango threshold for several sessions.

AlphaThread

Two things to flag first. Your flow levels and flow levels futures processes each restarted three times in the last day. Both were clean yesterday. Flow levels futures also has an old snapshot, last updated Friday, so its numbers may be behind.

Flow levels also moved to version zero point three point one. No sleeve opened or closed a trade since yesterday, and no sleeve has a halt or a reconciliation break.

On research, three studies changed status. The one on whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything stays active, with the single creator tested so far showing no directional edge. The low relative volatility study now says it needs a better test, because the effect looks like ordinary mean reversion. Its follow-up on implied volatility says the same, since the result can't be told apart from chance.

Your R eleven score moved too. One more real trade closed, and the real average slipped from about plus a quarter of a risk unit to about zero, slightly negative. Placebo trades closed two more and still average above one risk unit. So placebo is ahead of real. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, and you have five.

Nothing is live yet. IBKR is your primary broker, but the account is still at options Level one, which is too restrictive to go live.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve has twelve of twenty trades toward going live, and twenty-three of ninety days. It is down seventy dollars realized, with one put spread still open from last Thursday. Its open profit isn't available, because that needs a live quote.

Copy Mordy has no trades yet. It stands at zero of twenty trades and fifteen of ninety days.

Flow levels has two closed trades, up eleven dollars, with fourteen of ninety days. Apart from the restarts, it is running.

Flow levels futures has no trades, zero of twenty, and eight of ninety days. It is also flagged as a research session that can't be promoted live, because it allows uncovered short legs.

All of that paper profit and loss uses mid-price fills, so treat it as an upper bound on real trading.

For the other studies, the rest are closed or waiting on data, review, or pre-registered scoring. The pair of Discord caller studies and the intraday momentum and opening range tests are in that group.

Discord was busy overnight. There were ninety-two new alerts from twelve callers, mostly from Emilin, compared with sixteen yesterday. They're unscored caller calls, not signal.

Your ideas inbox holds sixty-six ideas, thirty-eight of them queued, and none are new.

item.title: pod — Mon, Nov 9
item.description:
School

Start with the one that's overdue. Your physics Exam 2 was due Friday at eight twenty p.m., and it still shows as not submitted. It's worth twenty points, so check on it first.

Tonight at midnight, your Prokaryotic Cell Quiz 11 is due. It's fifteen points, and you have about eighteen hours. Later this week, the Prokaryotic Cell extra credit is due Friday night, though it carries no points. Physics Homework 11 is due Saturday night, ten points.

The deadline watcher finished your physics Homework 10 yesterday evening. It submitted it and WileyPLUS scored it ten out of ten. The watcher also flagged the Prokaryotic Cell quiz just after midnight as not submitted. It starts completing work on its own when six hours are left, so that would kick in this evening.

That Homework 10 grade nudged your physics score up a hair, to about seventy-eight percent, still a B plus. Two classes are worth a look. Linear Algebra sits at seventy-five and a half percent, a C, and Abstract Algebra is at about sixty-five percent with no letter grade yet. Neither moved since yesterday. Prokaryotic Cell is an A minus, and the physics lab is an A.

In email, Perusall sent a reminder last night that Perusall Assignment 11 for Prokaryotic Cell is due in about a day. It's labeled for the graduate section only, so it may not apply to you. The reminder for Assignment 10 is also still unread, along with an unread physics message about Exam 2 reviews from last Thursday. That review message might be worth opening, given the exam situation.

On registration, Spring registration has been open since October thirtieth and stays open until late April. You're eligible, you have no holds, and there's no automatic registration plan set up. Fall registration closes December second, and there are no to-dos on your record.

The most important thing today is the physics Exam 2 that's past due, then the Prokaryotic Cell quiz before midnight.

Projects

You have three things waiting today.

First, AlphaThread. The overnight worker is blocked on two questions about the validation scripts. The first is how the older specs' freeze checks should treat later approved specs. The proposal is to mark the freeze sections of the older validation scripts as historical, skipped with a reason pointing to the later spec, and keep the newest one as the live freeze gate. The second is whether the task is then finished as it stands. The proposal is yes, close it once the first is answered. The work queue has nothing else ready, so this answer unblocks the next run.

Second, calculators. The trademark quote requests are ready to go out. Forward the China agent request to Nathan now. Send the US attorney request to two flat-fee firms now, with LegalZoom and Jaburg Wilk recommended. Also run the two-minute U S P T O search and send the hits. The U S P T O declaration and the China agent power of attorney still wait for the LLC.

Third, Discord feed. The listener has an unfilled gap again, and the four o'clock health step failed again. This is the same problem as yesterday. Deletes inside the gap are invisible. The listener is running and connected, so check the Discord feed log for today.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread had a big night. The work queue finished eleven tasks, and every one sits on its own unmerged branch. Forty-four commits landed across branches in total. The finished work includes a fix for early assignment of short in-the-money calls around ex-dividend dates, which yesterday was only a question. It also includes a plausibility flag for overfit or leaked backtest results, a point-in-time dividend source, the stress engine now using dividend yield, and a fix for paying a dividend declared before its ex-date. There was also a proposal for a lane-grid heatmap screen, with no code, plus one-minute data work for the pairs short list, including a backfill of holes in the NinjaTrader history. On the spec side, the rule sleeves spec moved into implementation, and the regime engine spec now has a plan and ninety-six tasks. Spec twenty-seven still has eight open tasks, including your Sim run, the deploy gate, and the decision to merge and go live. Many branches now wait for your review or merge. The runner has been up about thirty-eight hours, and there were no alerts. The bridge logged one broker outage and one recovery, but the times are unclear.

Calculators finished its overnight run cleanly, with six commits. It produced the China agent quote request, now without the camera group, and the US attorney request with a price shortlist. It also rechecked the F C C rule, which is still not in the Federal Register. Next in line are the pre-order launch configuration, which needs your admin access, and a test of the video editor once there is product footage.

Discord feed now watches one hundred sixty-six channels across fifteen servers, up two. Four servers have nothing worth watching: Gold Squad, Odd Lots, T P E's School, and Quanted. There are uncommitted config changes in the repo.

IG ideas ran fine this morning. Three new posts were analyzed, and none produced a new idea. Nothing is waiting for a transcript.

The rest is quiet. Content bench has one new commit, research on a faceless video reel flow for pre-launch warm-up. The kalq server hunt is idle. Its status file was last updated on the first, and the follow-up dates in it have passed, so current lead stages are unclear. Two leads there still need the EpicNPC account claimed. The AlphaThread worktrees show only the same shared commits.

That is everything. One answer for AlphaThread and three sends for trademarks would clear most of the board.

Markets

Stocks bounced on Friday, but only a narrow slice of the market did the bouncing, and it came at the end of the worst week since the April 2025 tariff crash.

On the backdrop: the trend is mixed, with the S&P 500 between its fifty- and two-hundred-day averages, a state that has held two sessions. Volatility is high, with the VIX at about twenty-six, higher than on roughly ninety-five percent of days this past year, also for two sessions. The VIX curve is in backwardation, two sessions running. And implied volatility has sat well above realized for fifty-two sessions, with the VIX about five points over what stocks actually delivered.

Now the moves. The S&P 500 rose about a third of a percent. The Nasdaq 100 gained about one point four percent on one and a half times normal volume, which shows some conviction. Small caps rose about one percent. The Dow slipped four tenths of a percent. Over five days, though, the S&P is down about two point seven percent and the Nasdaq 100 nearly five.

Technology led, up about one and a half percent on nearly one and three-quarters times normal volume. That's heavy trading, so buyers did show up. But the sector is still down more than eight percent on the week and almost nineteen percent below its high. Consumer staples were the weakest sector, down about one point three percent.

Outside stocks, the ten-year yield rose to about four point eight six percent and the dollar gained about three quarters of a percent. Gold fell nearly one percent. Oil closed near ninety-one dollars, down almost thirteen percent on the week.

Here is the part worth noticing. The index rose, yet only one hundred eighty-five S&P 500 stocks advanced, while three hundred seventeen declined. When an index rises on fewer winners, the gains are often concentrated in a few big names. That can mean a bounce is fragile, though a single day proves little.

Single stocks moved hard. Axon fell about eighteen percent on five times normal volume and hit a new one-year low. That kind of volume on a drop often means holders repriced the company, not just a pause. On the other side, AMD rose about eleven percent and Lam Research about eight, so the chip rebound was selective.

As for why, Yahoo Finance reports the odds of a December rate hike jumped to seventy-seven percent after a blowout jobs report. That fits a higher yield and stronger dollar. Yahoo Finance also reports this was the S&P 500's worst week since the April 2025 tariff crash. The reason for Friday's tech bounce itself is unclear from the headlines.

Concept of the day: Inside a stress regime. A high VIX together with an inverted volatility curve means the market is paying the most for protection over the next few weeks. Today the VIX is about twenty-six and its ratio to the three-month VIX is just above one. Volatility tends to cluster, so storms often last for a while, but mean reversion says they do end. For options, front-month premium is at its richest relative to later months and moves are large, so size and defined risk matter more than your direction view. Watch for the ratio to fall back under one first, then for the VIX percentile to ease out of the high band.

AlphaThread

Nothing changed in your trading books since yesterday. No trades opened or closed, no gate milestones, and no halts or reconciliation breaks. The flow levels and flow levels futures processes had one restart each yesterday, and none in the last day.

The movement is in research and Discord. The study on whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything changed status. It stays open, and the one creator tested so far does not predict direction. The two relative volatility studies also changed. Both say they need a better test. Discord had sixteen new alerts overnight, up from seven yesterday, mostly from itsnighthawk338 and Ironheart Capital. They are unscored caller calls, not signal. No new ideas landed in the inbox, and the R eleven score did not move.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. Your Interactive Brokers account is still at options Level 1, which limits what it can trade.

On paper, the demo put spread sleeve has twelve closed trades and is down seventy dollars. That is twelve of twenty trades and twenty of ninety days toward going live. It holds one open SPY put spread expiring in December, with no live quote on it yet. Paper results fill at mid prices, so treat any profit as an upper bound.

Copy Mordy has no closed trades, so zero of twenty trades and twelve of ninety days.

Flow levels has two closed trades and is up eleven dollars. That is two of twenty trades and eleven of ninety days.

Flow levels futures has no closed trades, zero of twenty and eight of ninety days. It is flagged as a research session and cannot go live, because its setup allows uncovered short legs.

On research, the volatility work is the live thread. One study asks whether low relative volatility in a mega-cap reverts upward. It holds at sixty-three sessions but not at twenty-one, and the next test needs implied volatility. The follow-up on whether implied volatility underprices what follows a low flag found a gap of under one volatility point. With fifty-six flags, that cannot be told apart from chance.

Still open beyond those: the Discord caller copy study has nine calls against the forty it needs. The Ironheart copy-trade study found that the guru's futures calls clear the bar, but on caller-reported prices, so it is an upper bound. The headline second-order options study is logging with no result yet. Two other studies are pre-registered and blocked on data. The rest are closed or parked.

On R eleven, the reversal levels study, your real trades have four closed with a mean of plus zero point two five R. The placebo has six closed with a mean of plus one point three nine. The bar needs thirty closed real trades and a real edge over placebo of at least zero point one five R. For now, the placebo is ahead.

The ideas inbox holds sixty-six ideas, thirty-eight of them queued.

item.title: pod — Sun, Nov 8
item.description:
School

Your physics Exam 2 is still showing as overdue, but that was an in-person exam. There was nothing to submit online, so that is not a missed assignment. It is just sitting there in Canvas.

Tonight at midnight, your Physics homework ten is due. It is worth ten points, and it is not submitted yet. About eighteen hours are left.

Tomorrow night at midnight, your Prokaryotic Cell Quiz eleven is due. It is worth fifteen points, and it is also not submitted.

Later this week, the Prokaryotic Cell extra credit assignment is due Friday night. It is worth no points in the gradebook. Physics homework eleven is due Saturday night, and it is worth ten points.

The deadline watcher has nothing new since yesterday. Its last pings were early this morning, flagging physics homework ten and the Prokaryotic Cell quiz as not submitted. It starts completing work on its own when six hours are left. Yesterday, it submitted your Linear Algebra homework nine. It also could not log in to Canvas for about four and a half hours on Friday afternoon and evening, so deadlines were not watched during that stretch.

No new grades posted overnight, and your scores are unchanged. Prokaryotic Cell is an A minus. The physics lab is an A. Physics is a B plus. Linear Algebra is a C at seventy five and a half percent, and Abstract Algebra is at sixty four and a half percent. Those two are your weak spots.

In email, nothing new needs a reply. You have unread Perusall reminders for Prokaryotic Cell assignments nine and ten, both for the graduate section. You also have an unread physics message about Exam 2 reviews. Two dates are coming up. On Tuesday at ten in the morning, UF's board meets about tuition increases for some graduate programs, which take effect in Fall 2027. On Friday afternoon, there is a reminder about the graduate travel scholarship.

Spring registration is open now, with no holds and no to-dos. Your cumulative GPA is three point six eight.

The most important thing today is Physics homework ten, due tonight at midnight.

Projects

Five things need you today.

Discord feed first. The listener has one unfilled gap, which means deletes inside it are invisible. The early morning curate run also logged a health failure. The listener itself is running and connected. You need to look at why the health step failed and fill the gap.

AlphaThread has three decisions waiting. First, whether to deploy the new Schwab pre-close price mark. The suggestion is yes. Merge it to main and the live branch, rebuild and restart at the next planned stop, bring the research worktree up to date, and reinstall the shadow tasks. Do all of that the same day, and follow up only if the three fifty-five hit rate comes in under about seventy percent. Second, the gamma exposure volatility flag. The suggestion is shadow logging only, with a review next November. Hand it to the regime engine spec only after a forward test, and don't ask SqueezeMetrics for permission yet. Third, early assignment around ex-dividend dates. The suggestion is to park it. When it's built, handle only the second of the two cases, on a fix branch, leave the existing requirement alone, and keep the dividend charge in the core only.

For kalq, the trademark work needs four things from you. Forward the China agent quote request draft to Nathan. Get one US trademark attorney quote, sending that request once the LLC lawyer names the applicant contact. Run the trademark office search and send back the hits. Then e-sign the declaration and the China agent power of attorney once the LLC exists.

Now the projects. AlphaThread development is blocked on those three answers, but the runner is up and healthy. Yesterday's warning about the signals ingest crashing is gone. There are no alert lines in the last day, and the runner is writing normally. Seven research tasks finished overnight, including the pre-close mark build, which is built and tested but not deployed. There were sixteen new commits across the queue worker and two feature branches. Your main checkout sits on the signal sleeve branch with two uncommitted files. In the ready queue, the most important item is the fix for copy guru futures skipping Guru posts, which is marked as a live blocker. The network reconnect add-on for NinjaTrader and the pointer for the regime engine spec are also ready. Spec twenty-seven still has eight open tasks. The Sim101 reconnect check and the Lucid go-live confirmation from yesterday no longer appear as asks, so their current state is unclear.

Kalq finished its overnight run cleanly. Both trademark quote request drafts are done, and nothing has been sent. The recheck of the FCC rule found it still isn't in the Federal Register. Seven commits sit on the overnight branch, not pushed, and the tree is clean. Next up is the pre-order launch configuration, which still needs you in an admin browser session. After that comes the spike on the cooked video editor, which waits on product footage. Trademarks remain blocked on your steps.

Discord feed again has no commits. The watch list now covers one hundred sixty-four channels across fifteen servers, one channel fewer than yesterday. Seven configuration files are uncommitted on master. This is the second day running with the same health failure and gap.

IG ideas is fine. The daily watcher ran at five and analysed three new posts, but produced no new ideas. Nothing is waiting for a transcript.

The kalq server hunt, the other AlphaThread worktrees and the pod project are idle with nothing new. The server hunt status file is still from November first, so the outcome of its follow-ups remains unknown. It no longer appears as an ask.

Overall, the decisions are quick if you accept the suggestions, and the Discord gap is the only item with a live problem.

Markets

The S&P 500 bounced Friday, but only a little, and it still ended its worst week since the April 2025 tariff crash.

On the regime: the trend is mixed, meaning the S&P 500 sits between its fifty-day and two-hundred-day averages, for two sessions now. Volatility is high. The VIX at about twenty-six sits in the top five percent of its past year, also for two sessions. The VIX curve is in backwardation, so near-term fear is priced above three-month fear, for two sessions. Implied volatility is still rich compared with realized, and that has held for fifty-two sessions.

Now the moves. The S&P 500 rose about a third of a percent on about one and a third times normal volume, but it is down about two point seven percent on the week. The Nasdaq 100 gained about one point four percent on one and a half times normal volume, yet it is still down nearly five percent for the week and about fourteen percent below its high. Tech rose about one and a half percent on nearly one and three-quarters times normal volume, after losing more than eight percent over the week. Heavy volume on a bounce can mean real buying, or it can mean shorts covering. One day can't tell you which. The Dow slipped about four tenths of a percent. Consumer staples fell about one point three percent, the weakest sector, which fits money rotating back toward risk. The dollar rose about three quarters of a percent. Oil sits near ninety-one dollars, down almost thirteen percent on the week, and energy stocks are down twelve percent over the same stretch.

Now the unusual stuff. Breadth disagreed with the index. The S&P 500 was up, but only one hundred eighty-five stocks advanced against three hundred seventeen decliners. A rally carried by a few big names, here tech, often proves less durable than one that lifts most stocks. Second, single-stock violence. AMD jumped about eleven percent. Axon fell about eighteen percent on roughly five times normal volume and hit a one-year low. Moves that large on that much volume usually mean an earnings reaction or a repricing of the whole story, not noise.

On sentiment: StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so shifts against a ticker's own normal matter more than the level. Bullishness on the S&P 500 ETF fell to about thirty-eight percent, well under its thirty-day average near fifty-one. Small caps dropped from about seventy percent to fifty. Retail got more cautious while the index ticked up.

As for why, Yahoo Finance reports the S&P 500 just had its worst week since the April 2025 tariff crash. Yahoo Finance also reports odds of a December rate hike jumped to seventy-seven percent after a blowout jobs report. That fits the ten-year yield rising about half a percent on the day, to about four point eight six. Investing.com describes an AI stock selloff and spending worries, which matches the tech damage this week. The headlines don't clearly explain Friday's bounce itself.

Concept of the day: the variance premium and future returns. Researchers Bollerslev, Tauchen and Zhou measured it as implied minus realized variance. A higher premium has tended to go with higher stock returns over the following quarter, perhaps because it measures how much compensation investors demand for bearing volatility risk. Today the VIX is about twenty-five point six, against realized volatility near twenty, a gap of about five and a half points. For option sellers, that wide gap pays. In this research it has also gone with better forward returns on average, though one reading is noisy and not a signal on its own. Watch for the spread narrowing into the thin band.

AlphaThread

Nothing traded overnight, and nothing was halted or out of sync with the broker. The one thing to know is that flow levels and flow levels futures each restarted once in the past day. Both are running now. That's down from three restarts each yesterday.

Three research studies changed status. Your study of Instagram creators' stock calls stays open and active. The one creator tested so far doesn't predict direction. Your study of low relative volatility in a mega-cap now says it needs a better test, because the pattern looks like ordinary mean reversion. The follow-up on implied volatility also needs a better test. The low-volatility flag isn't supported as a trigger, though the data can't rule out a small edge. No new ideas came into the inbox, and the R eleven score didn't move.

Nothing is live yet. IBKR is your primary broker, but the account is still at options Level 1.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve has twelve of twenty trades toward going live, and twenty of ninety days. It's down seventy dollars realized, with one SPY put spread still open from Thursday afternoon. Your copy Mordy sleeve is running cleanly. It has no closed trades yet, zero of twenty, and twelve of ninety days. Flow levels has two closed trades, up eleven dollars, so two of twenty trades and eleven of ninety days. Flow levels futures has no trades yet and is eight days into the ninety. It's also marked as a research session, so it can't be promoted live as built. Paper profit and loss fills at mid-price, so treat it as an upper bound.

On the rest of the research, the study of copying a free Discord caller needs more data. It has nine calls against the forty required. R three is waiting on your review. R four needs your approval for one probe to close it out. R five, the capture universe and request budget question, needs a better test. R thirteen and R eighteen are pre-registered and blocked on data. R twenty-three is logging a forward record and has no result yet. The remaining studies are closed or parked.

R eleven, Vin's reversal levels, is still short of its bar. The real trades are four closed, averaging a quarter of a unit of risk gained per trade. The placebo trades are six closed, averaging about one and a third. The bar needs thirty closed real trades and a clear edge over the placebo, so it's far from met.

The inbox still holds sixty-six ideas, with thirty-eight queued.

item.title: pod — Sat, Nov 7
item.description:
School

Good morning. Physics Exam 2 shows as overdue, but it was an in-person exam with nothing to submit online. The watcher tried twice and was blocked both times. Just keep an eye out for the score.

Tomorrow night, Sunday at midnight, your Physics homework ten is due. It's worth ten points and isn't started. Monday at midnight, you have Quiz eleven in Prokaryotic Cell, worth fifteen points. There's also an extra credit assignment in Prokaryotic Cell due next Friday at midnight. It's worth no points, so it's optional.

The deadline watcher had a rough Friday. It couldn't log in to Canvas for about four and a half hours, from mid-afternoon until early evening, so deadlines weren't being watched during that stretch. It recovered in time, though. At about quarter to eight, it completed and submitted your Linear Algebra Homework nine, all graded problems. Your professor also posted a note that a few typos in that homework were fixed. If you already submitted, you don't need to redo anything.

Two new grades came in for Physics, both from iClicker. Your performance grade was twenty-seven out of fifty-four, and the extra credit was about three out of five. Together they nudged your Physics score down slightly, from about seventy-eight and a half to just over seventy-eight. That's still a B plus.

Two classes are worth a look. Linear Algebra is at seventy-five and a half, a C. Abstract Algebra is at about sixty-five, with no letter grade yet. Prokaryotic Cell is an A minus, and the physics lab is an A.

In email, the advising office wrote back Friday evening about your math double major plan. Three professors also replied Thursday and Friday about getting access to the WRDS and CRSP data for your study. All of those are already read. Still unread are Perusall reminders for the Module nine and Module ten assignments in Prokaryotic Cell, the sixty-four-oh-seven-only ones. If those apply to you, they're still open. Also unread is the Physics note with the Exam 2 review materials.

On registration, Spring registration is open now through late April. You have no holds and no to-dos, and your cumulative GPA is three point six eight.

The one thing that matters most today is getting started on Physics homework ten, since it's due tomorrow night and the Prokaryotic Cell quiz follows right behind it.

Projects

Here is what needs you today.

Start with AlphaThread. The watchdog found the signals ingest crashing three times yesterday afternoon, and the two flow-levels paper sessions were found down three times as well. The flow-levels runs later finished fine. For signals ingest, no later successful run is recorded. The runners are up and the paper log is fresh, but you need to find out why signals ingest keeps crashing before the market opens.

Two more AlphaThread items are yours. First, the NT8 auto-reconnect fix needs its Sim101 checks, outside market hours. Install and recompile the add-on from the fix branch, pull the network for at least three minutes, then try a manual disconnect. Merging to main and the Lucid redeploy are already approved once that passes. Second, for spec 027 you need to confirm the join to main and the go-live on Lucid. The first Lucid eval day replaces the old test task, so it counts as the operator-live success criterion and must be recorded.

Next, the Discord feed. The daily health check failed again on one unfilled gap in the listener, so deletes inside that gap are invisible.

For calculators, the PreProduct launch config still needs you in the browser for an admin session. On the trademark, you still owe one US attorney quote, the USPTO search, and the e-sign steps once the LLC exists. Claude drafts the quote requests next run.

Last, the kalq server hunt. Its status file is from November first, and the follow-ups due on the third and fourth have passed with no known outcome. Check the hunt.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread development moved on several branches. A composed sleeve can now take per-session overrides of its manifest parameters. The regime overlay branch now lets the candle import accept an exact list of sessions beyond the tolerance. In the copy-guru futures work, limit entries can now trigger on touch, but the option ships switched off. A separate fix lets the alert interpreter read the guru alert lines, with only its reading counting as a witness. Two new items joined the ready queue: closing the GEX data gap, and long-vol tooling from the IBKR gamma-scalping repo. The regime engine in spec 028 stays with an interactive session, so the queue loop will not take it. Spec 027 has six open tasks, including the deploy gate. Yesterday's shadow task install question no longer appears on your list. Health is a warning, which is the ingest problem already covered.

Calculators is now blocked rather than needing attention, because the trademark route was approved. The decisions were to take the lowest-cost quotes only, and Nathan gets the China quotes. The recheck of the FCC ruling found it still not in the Federal Register or on public inspection. Next is another recheck by Tuesday, then testing the cooked video editor once product footage exists.

Discord feed applied its watch list this morning. It now watches one hundred sixty-five channels across sixteen servers, up from one hundred fifty-three across fourteen. Thirteen channels were added and one removed. A fix also makes futures roots like NQ and ES count as futures instead of crypto. The health failure is the same one as yesterday.

IG ideas is healthy. The scrape worked on all four handles, and two new posts were analysed, but they produced no new ideas.

The kalq server hunt, the AlphaThread worktrees and the pod project are idle with nothing new. The hunt is still blocked on claiming the EpicNPC account.

Start with the signals ingest crash, since the market opens soon.

Markets

Stocks bounced on Friday after Thursday's rout, but the bounce was thin, and the Nasdaq still finished its fourth straight losing week.

The regime is stressed but easing. Volatility is high, with the VIX at about twenty-six, higher than on roughly ninety-five percent of days in the past year. That has held for two sessions. The term structure is in backwardation, meaning near-term fear is priced above three-month fear, also for two sessions. Trend is mixed, also two sessions, with the S&P 500 below its fifty-day average but just above its two-hundred-day. Implied volatility is rich against realized, with the VIX about five points above what the market actually delivered, and that has held for fifty-two sessions.

On the move itself, the S&P 500 rose about a third of a percent, the Nasdaq 100 gained about one point four percent, and small caps rose about one percent. The Dow slipped about four tenths of a percent. Tech led, up about one and a half percent on nearly double its normal volume, which suggests real buying rather than drift. But tech is still down more than eight percent on the week. Consumer staples fell about one point three percent, the weakest sector, a sign money rotated out of defensives. The ten-year yield rose to about four point eight six percent, and the dollar gained about three quarters of a percent. Oil is down nearly thirteen percent on the week, even after a small gain Friday.

Now the unusual parts. First, breadth disagreed with the index. Only about one hundred eighty-five S&P 500 stocks rose, against about three hundred seventeen that fell. When the index rises on a handful of winners, the rally is often narrow, and narrow rallies can be fragile. Second, the put to call ratio dropped to about point six, from about point nine the day before. Fewer traders are buying protection, which can mean fear is fading, though it can also mean complacency returning too quickly. Third, single stocks swung hard. Axon fell about eighteen percent on roughly five times normal volume, a heavy-conviction reaction, likely to news. Airbnb jumped about twelve percent and AMD about eleven percent, both on elevated volume.

Sentiment shifted for the Nasdaq 100. StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so changes against a ticker's own history matter more than the level. Bullish share there is about nineteen points below its thirty-day average, even as the index rose.

As for why, Investing.com says a tech swoon is roiling the market with inflation data coming. CNBC reported earlier in the week that the midterm results are making markets rethink the path of rates, and that Iran tension has kept oil volatile. The headlines do not clearly explain Friday's bounce, so that cause is unclear.

Concept of the day: why index skew is steeper than single-stock skew. Index option prices put more weight on a sharp drop than single-stock prices do, because index puts are the market's main insurance. With the VIX near twenty-six and the curve in backwardation, that demand is visible. The options angle is that out-of-the-money index puts carry higher implied volatility than equally distant calls, so put spreads that sell the further put recover part of that premium. Watch for the term structure returning to contango, which usually comes with put skew relaxing.

AlphaThread

Nothing traded overnight, but there is one health note. Your flow levels and flow levels futures sleeves each restarted three times in the last day, after the restarts yesterday afternoon. Both are running now. No halts, no reconciliation breaks, and no stale snapshots.

No trades opened or closed, so no profit or loss moved. No sleeve crossed a gate milestone or changed version, and the gate clocks each moved forward a day.

On research, three studies changed status. The study of whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is still open, and the one creator tested does not predict direction. R eight, on low relative volatility in a mega-cap, now says it needs a better test. R nine, on whether implied volatility underprices what follows that flag, also says it needs a better test. With fifty-six flags, the result is not distinguishable from chance. No new ideas landed in the inbox.

The R eleven score did not move. Your real trades have four closed, averaging a quarter of a unit of risk per trade. The placebo has six closed, averaging more than one and a third. The bar needs thirty closed real trades and a clear edge over placebo, so it is nowhere close.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. IBKR is your primary broker, but the account is still at options Level 1.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve is running cleanly. It has twelve closed trades and is down seventy dollars. That is twelve of twenty trades toward going live, and twenty of ninety days. One SPY put spread, opened Thursday afternoon, is still open. Paper results fill at the midpoint, so they are an upper bound on real trading.

Your copy Mordy sleeve is running cleanly with no restarts. It has no closed trades yet, so zero of twenty trades and twelve of ninety days.

item.content:encoded:
School

Good morning. Physics Exam 2 shows as overdue, but it was an in-person exam with nothing to submit online. The watcher tried twice and was blocked both times. Just keep an eye out for the score.

Tomorrow night, Sunday at midnight, your Physics homework ten is due. It's worth ten points and isn't started. Monday at midnight, you have Quiz eleven in Prokaryotic Cell, worth fifteen points. There's also an extra credit assignment in Prokaryotic Cell due next Friday at midnight. It's worth no points, so it's optional.

The deadline watcher had a rough Friday. It couldn't log in to Canvas for about four and a half hours, from mid-afternoon until early evening, so deadlines weren't being watched during that stretch. It recovered in time, though. At about quarter to eight, it completed and submitted your Linear Algebra Homework nine, all graded problems. Your professor also posted a note that a few typos in that homework were fixed. If you already submitted, you don't need to redo anything.

Two new grades came in for Physics, both from iClicker. Your performance grade was twenty-seven out of fifty-four, and the extra credit was about three out of five. Together they nudged your Physics score down slightly, from about seventy-eight and a half to just over seventy-eight. That's still a B plus.

Two classes are worth a look. Linear Algebra is at seventy-five and a half, a C. Abstract Algebra is at about sixty-five, with no letter grade yet. Prokaryotic Cell is an A minus, and the physics lab is an A.

In email, the advising office wrote back Friday evening about your math double major plan. Three professors also replied Thursday and Friday about getting access to the WRDS and CRSP data for your study. All of those are already read. Still unread are Perusall reminders for the Module nine and Module ten assignments in Prokaryotic Cell, the sixty-four-oh-seven-only ones. If those apply to you, they're still open. Also unread is the Physics note with the Exam 2 review materials.

On registration, Spring registration is open now through late April. You have no holds and no to-dos, and your cumulative GPA is three point six eight.

The one thing that matters most today is getting started on Physics homework ten, since it's due tomorrow night and the Prokaryotic Cell quiz follows right behind it.

Projects

Here is what needs you today.

Start with AlphaThread. The watchdog found the signals ingest crashing three times yesterday afternoon, and the two flow-levels paper sessions were found down three times as well. The flow-levels runs later finished fine. For signals ingest, no later successful run is recorded. The runners are up and the paper log is fresh, but you need to find out why signals ingest keeps crashing before the market opens.

Two more AlphaThread items are yours. First, the NT8 auto-reconnect fix needs its Sim101 checks, outside market hours. Install and recompile the add-on from the fix branch, pull the network for at least three minutes, then try a manual disconnect. Merging to main and the Lucid redeploy are already approved once that passes. Second, for spec 027 you need to confirm the join to main and the go-live on Lucid. The first Lucid eval day replaces the old test task, so it counts as the operator-live success criterion and must be recorded.

Next, the Discord feed. The daily health check failed again on one unfilled gap in the listener, so deletes inside that gap are invisible.

For calculators, the PreProduct launch config still needs you in the browser for an admin session. On the trademark, you still owe one US attorney quote, the USPTO search, and the e-sign steps once the LLC exists. Claude drafts the quote requests next run.

Last, the kalq server hunt. Its status file is from November first, and the follow-ups due on the third and fourth have passed with no known outcome. Check the hunt.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread development moved on several branches. A composed sleeve can now take per-session overrides of its manifest parameters. The regime overlay branch now lets the candle import accept an exact list of sessions beyond the tolerance. In the copy-guru futures work, limit entries can now trigger on touch, but the option ships switched off. A separate fix lets the alert interpreter read the guru alert lines, with only its reading counting as a witness. Two new items joined the ready queue: closing the GEX data gap, and long-vol tooling from the IBKR gamma-scalping repo. The regime engine in spec 028 stays with an interactive session, so the queue loop will not take it. Spec 027 has six open tasks, including the deploy gate. Yesterday's shadow task install question no longer appears on your list. Health is a warning, which is the ingest problem already covered.

Calculators is now blocked rather than needing attention, because the trademark route was approved. The decisions were to take the lowest-cost quotes only, and Nathan gets the China quotes. The recheck of the FCC ruling found it still not in the Federal Register or on public inspection. Next is another recheck by Tuesday, then testing the cooked video editor once product footage exists.

Discord feed applied its watch list this morning. It now watches one hundred sixty-five channels across sixteen servers, up from one hundred fifty-three across fourteen. Thirteen channels were added and one removed. A fix also makes futures roots like NQ and ES count as futures instead of crypto. The health failure is the same one as yesterday.

IG ideas is healthy. The scrape worked on all four handles, and two new posts were analysed, but they produced no new ideas.

The kalq server hunt, the AlphaThread worktrees and the pod project are idle with nothing new. The hunt is still blocked on claiming the EpicNPC account.

Start with the signals ingest crash, since the market opens soon.

Markets

Stocks bounced on Friday after Thursday's rout, but the bounce was thin, and the Nasdaq still finished its fourth straight losing week.

The regime is stressed but easing. Volatility is high, with the VIX at about twenty-six, higher than on roughly ninety-five percent of days in the past year. That has held for two sessions. The term structure is in backwardation, meaning near-term fear is priced above three-month fear, also for two sessions. Trend is mixed, also two sessions, with the S&P 500 below its fifty-day average but just above its two-hundred-day. Implied volatility is rich against realized, with the VIX about five points above what the market actually delivered, and that has held for fifty-two sessions.

On the move itself, the S&P 500 rose about a third of a percent, the Nasdaq 100 gained about one point four percent, and small caps rose about one percent. The Dow slipped about four tenths of a percent. Tech led, up about one and a half percent on nearly double its normal volume, which suggests real buying rather than drift. But tech is still down more than eight percent on the week. Consumer staples fell about one point three percent, the weakest sector, a sign money rotated out of defensives. The ten-year yield rose to about four point eight six percent, and the dollar gained about three quarters of a percent. Oil is down nearly thirteen percent on the week, even after a small gain Friday.

Now the unusual parts. First, breadth disagreed with the index. Only about one hundred eighty-five S&P 500 stocks rose, against about three hundred seventeen that fell. When the index rises on a handful of winners, the rally is often narrow, and narrow rallies can be fragile. Second, the put to call ratio dropped to about point six, from about point nine the day before. Fewer traders are buying protection, which can mean fear is fading, though it can also mean complacency returning too quickly. Third, single stocks swung hard. Axon fell about eighteen percent on roughly five times normal volume, a heavy-conviction reaction, likely to news. Airbnb jumped about twelve percent and AMD about eleven percent, both on elevated volume.

Sentiment shifted for the Nasdaq 100. StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so changes against a ticker's own history matter more than the level. Bullish share there is about nineteen points below its thirty-day average, even as the index rose.

As for why, Investing.com says a tech swoon is roiling the market with inflation data coming. CNBC reported earlier in the week that the midterm results are making markets rethink the path of rates, and that Iran tension has kept oil volatile. The headlines do not clearly explain Friday's bounce, so that cause is unclear.

Concept of the day: why index skew is steeper than single-stock skew. Index option prices put more weight on a sharp drop than single-stock prices do, because index puts are the market's main insurance. With the VIX near twenty-six and the curve in backwardation, that demand is visible. The options angle is that out-of-the-money index puts carry higher implied volatility than equally distant calls, so put spreads that sell the further put recover part of that premium. Watch for the term structure returning to contango, which usually comes with put skew relaxing.

AlphaThread

Nothing traded overnight, but there is one health note. Your flow levels and flow levels futures sleeves each restarted three times in the last day, after the restarts yesterday afternoon. Both are running now. No halts, no reconciliation breaks, and no stale snapshots.

No trades opened or closed, so no profit or loss moved. No sleeve crossed a gate milestone or changed version, and the gate clocks each moved forward a day.

On research, three studies changed status. The study of whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is still open, and the one creator tested does not predict direction. R eight, on low relative volatility in a mega-cap, now says it needs a better test. R nine, on whether implied volatility underprices what follows that flag, also says it needs a better test. With fifty-six flags, the result is not distinguishable from chance. No new ideas landed in the inbox.

The R eleven score did not move. Your real trades have four closed, averaging a quarter of a unit of risk per trade. The placebo has six closed, averaging more than one and a third. The bar needs thirty closed real trades and a clear edge over placebo, so it is nowhere close.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. IBKR is your primary broker, but the account is still at options Level 1.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve is running cleanly. It has twelve closed trades and is down seventy dollars. That is twelve of twenty trades toward going live, and twenty of ninety days. One SPY put spread, opened Thursday afternoon, is still open. Paper results fill at the midpoint, so they are an upper bound on real trading.

Your copy Mordy sleeve is running cleanly with no restarts. It has no closed trades yet, so zero of twenty trades and twelve of ninety days.

Your flow levels sleeve restarted, as covered above. It has two closed trades and is up eleven dollars. That is two of twenty trades and eleven of ninety days.

Your flow levels futures sleeve also restarted. It has no closed trades yet, so zero of twenty trades and eight of ninety days. It is a research session, which means it cannot be promoted live as configured.

R four, on the two odd RIVN timestamps, needs your approval for one probe to close it out. R ten, on copying a Discord caller, needs more data, and the paper forward test is how it gets answered. R thirteen and R eighteen are pre-registered and blocked on data. R twenty-three is logging calls going forward, with no result yet. R twenty-two found that one caller's futures calls clear its bar, but those are caller-reported prices, so treat them as an upper bound. The other studies are closed or parked.

item.description:
School

Your big one is tonight. Physics Exam 2 is due at eight twenty tonight, about fifteen hours from now. It's not submitted yet. The exam email says the room is split across four spots on campus, so check which room is yours.

Also tonight, your Linear Algebra Homework 9 is due at eleven fifty-nine. It's worth thirty points and not submitted.

Over the weekend, Physics Homework 10 is due Sunday at midnight. Then on Monday at midnight, you have Quiz 11 for Prokaryotic Cell. Nothing is overdue.

On the deadline watcher, it sent early warnings for the physics exam and Linear Algebra Homework 9. It says it starts doing work on its own at six hours left. It did not submit anything since yesterday. Its Duo helper also failed to start twenty-one times between early Thursday morning and Thursday afternoon. That means automatic login may not be reliable right now, so don't count on it for tonight's work.

No new grades posted in the last day. A couple of scores are worth knowing, though, compared with the last check on Monday. Abstract Algebra is at about sixty-five percent, down from seventy. Linear Algebra is holding at seventy-five and a half, a C. Physics is at about seventy-eight, still a B plus. Prokaryotic Cell is at ninety-four, an A minus, and the physics lab is at ninety-six.

On email, Alejandro Lopez Lira replied last night about your request for WRDS and CRSP sponsorship for your pre-registered study. You've already opened it. Your physics course also still has an unread exam review email from last week. Earlier this week, you were also reminded that Monday, November sixteenth is the last day to drop a course without penalty. That's worth keeping in mind with Abstract Algebra where it is.

For registration, Spring twenty twenty-seven is open now and stays open until April twenty-first. You have no holds, no to-dos, and no automatic registration plan.

The one thing today: get ready for Physics Exam 2 at eight twenty tonight, and find your room.

Projects

You have four things waiting today.

First, the Discord feed. The daily health check failed again, for the same reason as yesterday. The listener reports one unfilled gap, so deleted messages inside it are invisible. You need to fill the gap or confirm it can be ignored.

Second, AlphaThread. The shadow task install is blocked on four answers from you. Should it install now? Should it use its own dedicated worktree? Should it also register the second quote capture? And do you keep the indicative Alpaca quotes, or sign up for the options data feed?

Third, kalq has two asks. The trademark route needs your approval. The plan is to form the company first, at about three thousand dollars realistic at filing plus three hundred later. You would e-sign the trademark office declaration and the China agent power of attorney. Workers would then get two China agent quotes and one US attorney quote, and run the trademark search. The pre-order launch setup also needs you to open a founder admin session in the browser, for the pre-product and notifications pages.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread is in good shape on the development side. Six queue tasks finished overnight, and there were sixty commits across sixteen branches. Two more queue tasks merged. The dashboard now has a single Sleeves tab, and the earnings timeline hover bug is fixed. The edge-hunt triage is done. For spec twenty-eight, yesterday's decisions are recorded, and the regime exit is in version one. Spec twenty-seven still has eight open tasks, and one queue task is held by your interactive session. The runner has been up about twenty-seven hours with no alerts. The checkout is on the signal sleeve branch with two uncommitted entries.

Yesterday's blocked items on the minute-bar source and the reconnect add-on no longer appear in the report. Today the only block is your install answers.

kalq finished two tasks overnight. The trademark filing plan for China and the US is written, which is why it now waits on you. The federal rule recheck found the FCC order still not published in the Federal Register. A new research task is queued to test the free cooked editor next to the first one. Reel triage produced four notes, and the reel bot processed nine reels. The second reply to Wonderful went out yesterday, and your morning answers were applied. Next, you are waiting on Wonderful's revised quote and their answer on the screen.

New research ideas ran cleanly at six. The watcher found seven new posts and created two ideas, and both were queued. The inbox holds sixty-six ideas, with thirty-eight queued. As always, the creators' claims are untested.

Back to the Discord feed. Beyond the health failure, two commits landed on master. One adds an allowlist for channels and callers. The other drops the copy-mordy channel and its callers. The morning curation still watches one hundred fifty-three channels in fourteen servers. Seven entries are uncommitted in the working tree.

The remaining projects are quiet. Content bench has one commit, assessing the cooked editor as an edit bay. The AlphaThread worktrees only repeat the same work counted above. The kalq server hunt has no change. Its status file dates from November first, so it is unclear whether the follow-ups due on the third and fourth happened. Two threads still wait on claiming the EpicNPC account.

Start with the Discord gap and the four install answers. Those are the quickest ones to clear.

Markets

Stocks had a sharp, broad selloff yesterday, with technology leading it down, and the VIX jumped from the mid-teens to about twenty-eight.

The S&P 500 fell about four and a half percent. The Nasdaq 100 dropped about six and a half percent, and small caps lost about four and a half. The Dow slid about three and a half. Volume was roughly three times normal in the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100. That is heavy participation, which suggests real conviction behind the selling, not a thin drift lower. Tech was the worst sector, down about eight percent, and it is now about fourteen percent lower over five days. Energy fell about three percent. Meanwhile gold rose about one percent, and bitcoin fell about five and a half percent.

Now the unusual parts. First, breadth. Only seventy-three S&P 500 stocks rose, while four hundred thirty fell. Yet about sixty-three percent of the index is still above its fifty-day average, down only about three points in five days. That often means the damage is fresh and fast, not yet a long grind. One day does not make a trend.

Second, the rotation underneath. Consumer staples, health care, and financials all closed at one-year highs, even as they fell on the day. Dozens of defensive and financial names hit new highs, while only seven stocks hit new lows. One read is that money is moving out of the crowded trade and not out of stocks entirely.

Third, volatility. The VIX closed above the three-month VIX, a ratio of about one point one. Yesterday the ratio was about point eight eight. The equity put to call ratio rose to about point eight nine from about point four four. Investors are paying up for near-term protection, and that can mean stress is concentrated in the next few weeks.

Individual names were violent. AMD fell about seventeen percent and Sandisk about twenty-two percent, both on roughly three times normal volume. Applovin jumped about thirty-one percent on five times normal volume.

As for why, headlines point at artificial intelligence. Investing.com reports Susquehanna sees eight percent of AI data center projects at risk, and describes an AI rout. MarketWatch points to the Texas governor-elect's comments on data centers, after Tuesday's elections. CNBC reports Tesla and SpaceX lost over four hundred twenty billion dollars in combined market value after the midterms, and says a Democratic sweep gives markets a reason to rethink the path of interest rates. The ten-year yield eased to about four point eight four percent. Investing.com says Nasdaq futures are rising this morning as dip buyers step in. The exact trigger for the size of yesterday's drop is not clear from these headlines.

Concept of the day: the VIX term structure. The VIX measures expected volatility over the next thirty days, and the three-month VIX covers a longer window. Normally the shorter one sits lower, because the future is more uncertain than the present. Yesterday that flipped. Short-term fear exceeded longer-term fear, which is called backwardation. It usually signals investors want protection right now. Often it fades as the shock does, but it can persist if selling continues.

AlphaThread

Quiet on the health side. No halts, no reconciliation breaks, and none of your running sleeves restarted overnight.

The action was in demo put spread. It closed four trades yesterday, every one on its underlying stop, two winners and two losers. The sleeve's realized total fell about one hundred thirty-two dollars on the day. It also opened four new spreads, and one is still open from the close. None of your sleeves hit a gate milestone.

Research moved on three studies. The study on whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is still open, and you chose to keep it that way. The studies on low relative volatility in mega-caps, and on whether implied volatility underprices what follows, both landed on needs a better test.

Two new ideas came into the inbox. One is that QQQ rebounds after an extreme one-day jump in the VIX. The other is that broad all-sector down days lead to deeper short-term SPY drawdowns.

The R eleven score moved too. Two more real trades and two more placebo trades closed.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. IBKR is your primary broker, but the account is still at options Level 1.

On paper, demo put spread has twelve closed trades and is down seventy dollars in total. It is twelve of twenty trades toward going live, and nineteen of ninety days. Paper results fill at the midpoint price, so treat all profit and loss here as an upper bound.

Copy Mordy is running cleanly with no closed trades. It is zero of twenty trades and eleven of ninety days.

Flow levels is running cleanly with two closed trades, up eleven dollars. It is two of twenty trades and ten of ninety days.

Flow levels futures is running cleanly with no closed trades, zero of twenty and seven of ninety days. Its latest research session allowed uncovered short legs, so it cannot go live as it stands.

On research, the R eleven study of Vin's reversal levels is being scored against its bar. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, a mean of at least fifteen hundredths of a point of risk per trade, and a clear lead over the placebo. Today you have four real trades averaging about a quarter of a point. The placebo has six trades averaging about one and four tenths, so the placebo is ahead. The real sample is far too small to read anything into.

Other open studies are mostly waiting on you or on data. The R three calendar findings need your review. The R four timestamp probe needs your approval. R ten, copying a Discord caller, is collecting data through the paper test. R thirteen and R eighteen are pre-registered but blocked on missing data. R twenty-three is logging calls with no result yet.

The rest of the studies are closed, parked, or built and need nothing from you.

Of the ideas in the inbox, thirty-eight are queued out of sixty-six total.

item.description:
