This school data is from Monday, November 2, not today, so some of it may be out of date.

Here is what it showed was coming up. The Prokaryotic Cell Quiz 9 and Quiz 10 were due Monday at midnight. Neither was submitted at that point, and the data can't say whether they went in afterward. Check Canvas to make sure they didn't slip.

Physics Exam 2 is due tomorrow, Friday, at eight twenty in the evening. It's worth twenty points and wasn't submitted as of Monday. There's also an unread email from your physics class with exam review material. After that, Physics homework ten is due Sunday at midnight, worth ten points.

On the deadline watcher: on Sunday afternoon, it failed to log in to Canvas five times between about twelve fifty and two fifty. During that stretch, deadlines weren't being watched. It recovered by Monday and sent due-soon warnings for both quizzes, noting that auto-submit starts at six hours left. The data doesn't show whether it submitted anything.

There were no new grades. Two classes are sitting below a B. Linear Algebra is at seventy-five and a half percent, a C. Abstract Algebra is at seventy percent. Prokaryotic Cell is your strongest at an A minus, and the physics lab is an A.

In email, one date matters. Monday, November sixteenth, is the last day to drop a course without penalty. If you've been weighing that for Linear Algebra or Abstract Algebra, you have about eleven days.

On registration, Spring 2027 has been open since October thirtieth. You're eligible, with no holds and no to-dos. No automatic registration plan is set up, so you'd need to add classes yourself. Your cumulative GPA is three point six eight.

The most important thing today is Physics Exam 2, due tomorrow evening, plus confirming those two quizzes actually got turned in.

Projects

Here is what needs you today.

Start with AlphaThread. The watchdog found three paper sessions down around ten to three this morning, close to the live deploy. No later healthy run is recorded and the cause is unconfirmed, so check that they are running. Two work items are also blocked on you. First, the one-minute index futures data. The recommendation is the free NinjaTrader export of four quarters of micro contracts, about ten minutes. Only if that fails, say whether a worker may spend up to ten dollars on a Databento key. Second, the NinjaTrader auto-reconnect add-on has four questions. Should it be installed and tested on the simulator outside market hours? Should it retry every five minutes or stop after a number of failed logons? After the tests pass, should it be merged and redeployed on Lucid? And should attempts be added to the broker unavailable message? The worker suggests yes, keep five minutes, yes, and no.

Two things failed in ops. Yesterday's daily report did not run, so this briefing is the next one. And the reel bot ended ten runs as failed yesterday, the last mid-afternoon, with no healthy run since.

For kalq, nine questions are waiting in this morning's overnight report. They cover subscription ordering and labels, hiding quick-buy on European pack pages only, post-launch pricing of two hundred thirty-nine dollars for a two-pack and nineteen ninety for a spare battery, cuts in the reel formats, stand-in calculators, and a dev-theme trial of the consent box. The Wonderful reply is on hold until trademark research is done. That task is queued as ready.

Discord feed: the health step failed at four this morning with one unfilled gap. The listener itself is running. It is the same gap as two days ago.

The kalq server hunt status file is four days old, and two follow-up dates have passed. Check the threads and update it. Two listings still need the EpicNPC account claimed.

Now the projects, compared with the last report we have, from two days ago.

AlphaThread development: the work queue cleared thirteen tasks overnight. Two fixes, the relay echo and the discordscrape gap handling, were merged to main and went live with your approval. Other finished work includes a VIX control for the day-after-Thanksgiving research, new calendar signals, an entry filter, and updated futures holiday hours for twenty twenty-seven. Several research studies closed with pre-registered results. One idea was marked dead, and a Turnaround Tuesday test advanced on two of three funds. There were thirty-two commits in the day. Next up are the auto-reconnect work and a rerun of the trailing stop study once minute data exists. Spec twenty-seven still has open tasks, including a dry-run reconcile and your go-live merge on Lucid.

kalq: the overnight run finished five tasks across twenty-six commits. The backend now records the European order and consent basis per purchase, and the consent columns are in the privacy export. Also done are the pack-page consent box with policy and email drafts, bundle research, an agreement draft for Wonderful, and ten reel formats. A recheck found the new FCC rule still unpublished. CalcAI notes show the partner is CALCAI LLC in New Jersey, not SolverNow. Tests pass, but the branch is not pushed. Still ahead is the pre-order launch setup, which needs your PreProduct admin session.

New research ideas is healthy. The watcher found eight new posts and one new idea, about SPY after a midterm election day. It was not queued.

On the Discord feed, curation added two alert channels, and one fix means guru alerts feed signals again.

The AlphaThread worktrees are idle, showing only shared commits.

Start with the paper sessions.

Markets

Stocks rallied broadly on Tuesday, with the Dow up about three percent, its best day in eighteen months according to MarketWatch.

The S&P 500 rose about one point six percent on about one and a half times normal volume. Heavy volume suggests real buying rather than a drift higher. The Dow led, small caps gained about one and a half percent, and the Nasdaq 100 rose about one percent. That matters because the Nasdaq is still down about four and a half percent over five days and nine percent below its high. Tech was flat on the day and remains thirteen percent below its peak.

The sector story was a wide spread. Consumer discretionary rose over four percent on about two and a half times normal volume, the heaviest of any sector. Financials, staples, health care and communication services each gained over three percent. Energy fell nearly five percent on more than double normal volume, as oil dropped about eight percent. Gold rose about three percent, the ten-year yield slipped to about four point nine percent, and bitcoin gained about four percent.

Now the unusual stuff. First, breadth. About three hundred seventy-six S&P stocks rose against one hundred twenty-seven that fell, and the share above their fifty-day average climbed about thirteen points in five days to about seventy-two percent. When breadth improves along with the index, the rally is often healthier than one carried by a few big names. Financials, staples and health care all closed at one-year highs, along with dozens of other stocks.

Second, the sector gap of about nine points between consumer discretionary and energy. A wide gap like that can mean money is rotating between themes rather than simply rising together. One day is not a trend.

Third, single-stock shocks. FIS fell nearly twenty-four percent on over six times normal volume and hit a one-year low. Trimble and Datadog each dropped over fourteen percent on heavy volume. A big gap at the open on huge volume usually means news arrived overnight, often earnings, and that large holders repriced all at once. The headlines here do not say what hit FIS.

One sentiment note. StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so only shifts against a ticker's own history count. Bullishness on the Dow fund was about thirty points above its own thirty-day average.

As for why, MarketWatch ties the rally to relief after Democrats swept to power in Congress. CNBC reported on the election results the day before. Why oil fell so hard is unclear from the headlines, and the energy drop is not explained by the election news alone.

Concept of the day: the VIX term structure. The VIX, the market's expected volatility over the next month, fell to about sixteen point six from about twenty point eight. The three-month VIX sits higher, at about eighteen point eight. The ratio of the two is about point eight eight, down from about point nine eight the day before. When the near-term measure sits below the longer one, the market is calm now and pricing more uncertainty later. When the near-term reading rises above the longer one, it signals stress right now. Yesterday the two were nearly equal, so the curve moved from flat toward calm. For an options trader, that shifts what protection costs: nearby options got cheaper.

AlphaThread

Here's what changed since yesterday. Health first. Your copy Mordy, flow levels and flow levels futures processes each restarted once in the last day, the latest around three this morning. All three are running now. No halts, no reconciliation breaks, and no stale snapshots.

No trades opened or closed anywhere. One oddity in the demo put spread sleeve: its realized profit is up fifty-four dollars, to sixty-two, even though its closed trade count didn't move. Its open SPY spread also shows three contracts, where yesterday it showed six. That's worth a look. As always, paper profit uses mid-price fills, so it's an upper bound on what real trading would have done.

No gate milestones and no version changes.

On research, three studies changed status. R seven, whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything, is still open. The one creator tested so far doesn't predict direction. R eight, on whether low relative volatility in a mega-cap reverts upward, needs a better test, since it looks like ordinary mean reversion. R nine, on whether options underprice the volatility that follows, also needs a better test. The result can't be told apart from chance.

One new idea landed in the inbox: whether SPY after a midterm election day outruns random windows. The R eleven score didn't move.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. Your broker account is still at options level one, which limits what can trade.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve is running in the main store. It has eight closed trades and sixty-two dollars of realized profit. That's eight of twenty trades and eighteen of ninety days toward going live.

Copy Mordy restarted once but is running cleanly. It has no closed trades yet, so zero of twenty trades and ten of ninety days.

Flow levels also restarted once and is running. It has two closed trades and eleven dollars of profit. That's two of twenty trades and nine of ninety days.

Flow levels futures restarted once and is running. It has no closed trades, so zero of twenty and six of ninety days. Its latest research session allows uncovered short legs, so it can't be promoted live as it stands.

On the other studies: R eleven, Vin's reversal levels, is pre-registered and being scored. Real trades have two closed at an average of about a third of a risk unit. Placebo trades have four closed, averaging nearly two. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, so there's no verdict yet, and the placebo is ahead. R ten, copying a Discord caller, needs more data. It has nine calls against the forty required. R thirteen and R eighteen are pre-registered and blocked on data. R twenty-three is logging calls with no result yet. R three is waiting on your review, and R four is waiting on your approval for one probe. R twelve is parked. The other studies are closed.

The ideas inbox holds sixty-four ideas, thirty-six of them queued.

item.title: pod — Tue, Nov 3
item.description:
School

This briefing is built from data collected yesterday, November second, because the early morning school check had not finished. Treat everything here as possibly out of date.

The most urgent item is the two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes, Quiz 9 and Quiz 10, worth fifteen points each. As of the last check they were not submitted, and both were due last night at midnight. They may now be overdue, so check Canvas first thing.

Next is your physics Exam 2, due Friday at eight twenty in the evening. Your Physics homework 10 is due Sunday night at midnight. Nothing else is due this week.

The deadline watcher had a rough stretch on Sunday. It could not log in to Canvas for five checks between about noon and three in the afternoon, so deadlines were not being watched then. It recovered, and it sent due-soon warnings about both quizzes, at about twenty-four hours and again at twelve. It said automatic completion would start at six hours left. The data stops before that point, and no submission was recorded, so you can't count on the quizzes being done.

No new grades have posted. Compared with the last check, Linear Algebra rose from sixty-seven and a half to seventy-five and a half, which is a C. That is up, but still below a B. Abstract Algebra sits at seventy, with no letter grade yet. Physics is up slightly, to a B plus, about seventy-nine percent. Prokaryotic Cell is an A minus and the physics lab is an A.

In email, the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences advisor reminds you that November sixteenth is the last day to drop a course without penalty. That is two weeks away. Perusall also has unread notices that you have not completed Assignments 9 and 10 in Prokaryotic Cell, but those are marked for the graduate section only, so they may not apply to you. And there is an unread email from your Physics course with Exam 2 review material, which is worth opening before Friday.

On registration, the Spring 2027 window opened Friday afternoon and stays open through April. You have no holds and no to-dos. Last week's data showed an automatic registration plan for six classes set to fire when the window opened. Yesterday's data lists no plan, and nothing confirms the classes were added, so check your Spring schedule in ONE.UF. The Fall window closes December second. Your cumulative GPA is three point six eight.

The one thing that matters today is confirming that the two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes went in. If they did not, contact your instructor right away.

Projects

You have a few things today, mostly in AlphaThread.

In AlphaThread, the watchdog found four runner sessions down between about twelve forty-one and twelve forty-three this morning, including the signals ingest. They appear to have been restarted, but the cause is unknown, so check they stay up. There's also an operator step: change the role links on one Discord channel to alerts, then restart the listener. And you still need to verify the seven declared 2026 Globex holiday and early-close times against the CME tables before November twenty-sixth.

For calculators, kalq, there are seven open questions in today's report, and one needs your admin session.

On the Discord feed, the listener health check failed on one unfilled gap. Deletes inside that gap are invisible.

And for the kalq server hunt, the last follow-up with the first lead is due today, then you drop it. The owner nudge on the fourth lead is due tomorrow.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread development. Seven queue tasks finished overnight. An eighth, the futures calendar fix for 2027, is committed on its own branch but not marked done. There were also commits on the research docs branch, the layer six work, and the first phase of spec twenty-seven. Next up are the five open follow-ups on spec twenty-three and the ready queue. One task is still blocked on data and needs you. The Alpaca key file and the prop-firm sleeve item no longer appear on your list, and the report doesn't say why. Health shows a warning from the restarts, with no alert lines in the last day.

Calculators, kalq. The overnight run finished, and the project is blocked on your answers. That's up from four questions yesterday to seven. The unit economics work landed. Break-even customer acquisition cost is about seventy dollars forty-six cents, and the three-to-one target is about twenty-three dollars forty-nine cents. The final wording for the European paragraph in the order confirmation is done. The consent design for the European pack is done too, and two follow-on tasks are queued behind it. Those two wait on questions three through six. The second reply to the partner is approved to send. The F C C ruling is still not in the Federal Register, and the recheck is due by November tenth. Three reel notes were triaged.

IG ideas. The watcher ran at five this morning and found one new idea. It's a down Friday followed by a down Monday, which precedes a larger than usual S P Y move. It scored three and is live-executable, but it wasn't queued. Eight new posts were analysed, none waiting on a transcript. The inbox holds sixty-three ideas, thirty-six of them queued. As always, the creator claims are untested hypotheses.

Discord feed. The big change is the gap count, down from two hundred seventeen to one. The health check no longer fails on four-oh-three gaps, and notification titles with emoji or curly quotes now send. The watch list was refreshed to one hundred seventy channels across fifteen servers, one fewer than before. The listener is running and connected. The next step is to fill or acknowledge that last gap.

Kalq server hunt. Nothing has moved since Sunday, when the status file was last updated. Two leads are blocked on claiming the EpicNPC account, and one is waiting on a staff reply.

The remaining worktrees are all AlphaThread branches and are idle. They only show shared history from the sixty commits in the last day.

That's the picture. The restarts and the one Discord gap are the items to watch.

Markets

Tech sold off again on heavy volume, but most stocks actually rose, so the market's weakness was narrow.

The S&P 500 fell about half a percent. The Nasdaq 100 dropped about one point four percent, on roughly one and a half times normal volume. Heavy volume suggests real selling, not a drift lower. The Dow rose about half a percent, and small caps were basically flat.

The sector gap tells the story. Tech fell almost three percent on about one and two-thirds times normal volume. Energy fell about four percent. On the other side, consumer discretionary rose about two and a half percent, financials about one point nine, and materials about one point eight. Materials and consumer staples both closed at one-year highs. Oil dropped more than seven percent to about ninety-six dollars. The ten-year yield slipped to about four point nine percent, gold rose about one point eight percent, and bitcoin fell about two percent.

Now the unusual part. Breadth disagreed with the index. Three hundred forty-seven S&P 500 stocks rose and only one hundred fifty-five fell. The share above their fifty-day average climbed to about sixty-seven percent, up about six and a half points in five days. One read is that big tech dragged a cap-weighted index down while the average stock did fine. That can be a rotation, not a broad retreat. It is one session, though.

Individual names were wild. Lumentum fell about nineteen percent on nearly three times normal volume, and Marvell fell about thirteen percent on more than two and a half times normal. Oracle dropped about nine percent. Idexx jumped about twenty-two percent after opening up thirteen percent, on three and a half times normal volume. A gap that holds or extends on that volume often means big funds repositioned, not just day traders.

Sentiment also shifted. StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so changes against a ticker's own normal matter more than levels. Bullishness on small caps fell far below its thirty-day average, while it rose above average for the Nasdaq 100, even on a down day.

For the why: CNBC reported that crude fell below one hundred dollars amid reports of U.S.-Iran diplomatic efforts. That fits the energy drop. Airlines rose, with United up about five percent and Delta about four, which makes sense when fuel gets cheaper. Lufthansa cutting its outlook on a huge fuel bill, per Investing.com, shows how much that matters. For tech, the cause is unclear. Investing.com has been analyzing an October dive in AI-related shares, which may be part of it. Midterm elections are today, and Citi and Morgan Stanley, per MarketWatch, are both talking up outcomes, so some caution is plausible.

Concept of the day: the VIX term structure. The VIX, at about twenty-one, measures expected swings over the next month. The three-month version was about twenty-one point six. Normally the longer one is higher, since more time means more uncertainty. Their ratio rose to about point nine eight from about point nine four on Friday. As it approaches one, traders are paying nearly as much to insure against the next month as the next three. When it rises above one, near-term fear dominates, which has often shown up in real stress. We are close, not there.

AlphaThread

Three of your paper processes restarted overnight. Copy Mordy, flow levels, and flow levels futures each restarted once, early this morning. All three are running now. School

This briefing is built from data collected yesterday, November second, because the early morning school check had not finished. Treat everything here as possibly out of date.

The most urgent item is the two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes, Quiz 9 and Quiz 10, worth fifteen points each. As of the last check they were not submitted, and both were due last night at midnight. They may now be overdue, so check Canvas first thing.

Next is your physics Exam 2, due Friday at eight twenty in the evening. Your Physics homework 10 is due Sunday night at midnight. Nothing else is due this week.

The deadline watcher had a rough stretch on Sunday. It could not log in to Canvas for five checks between about noon and three in the afternoon, so deadlines were not being watched then. It recovered, and it sent due-soon warnings about both quizzes, at about twenty-four hours and again at twelve. It said automatic completion would start at six hours left. The data stops before that point, and no submission was recorded, so you can't count on the quizzes being done.

No new grades have posted. Compared with the last check, Linear Algebra rose from sixty-seven and a half to seventy-five and a half, which is a C. That is up, but still below a B. Abstract Algebra sits at seventy, with no letter grade yet. Physics is up slightly, to a B plus, about seventy-nine percent. Prokaryotic Cell is an A minus and the physics lab is an A.

In email, the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences advisor reminds you that November sixteenth is the last day to drop a course without penalty. That is two weeks away. Perusall also has unread notices that you have not completed Assignments 9 and 10 in Prokaryotic Cell, but those are marked for the graduate section only, so they may not apply to you. And there is an unread email from your Physics course with Exam 2 review material, which is worth opening before Friday.

On registration, the Spring 2027 window opened Friday afternoon and stays open through April. You have no holds and no to-dos. Last week's data showed an automatic registration plan for six classes set to fire when the window opened. Yesterday's data lists no plan, and nothing confirms the classes were added, so check your Spring schedule in ONE.UF. The Fall window closes December second. Your cumulative GPA is three point six eight.

The one thing that matters today is confirming that the two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes went in. If they did not, contact your instructor right away.

Projects

You have a few things today, mostly in AlphaThread.

In AlphaThread, the watchdog found four runner sessions down between about twelve forty-one and twelve forty-three this morning, including the signals ingest. They appear to have been restarted, but the cause is unknown, so check they stay up. There's also an operator step: change the role links on one Discord channel to alerts, then restart the listener. And you still need to verify the seven declared 2026 Globex holiday and early-close times against the CME tables before November twenty-sixth.

For calculators, kalq, there are seven open questions in today's report, and one needs your admin session.

On the Discord feed, the listener health check failed on one unfilled gap. Deletes inside that gap are invisible.

And for the kalq server hunt, the last follow-up with the first lead is due today, then you drop it. The owner nudge on the fourth lead is due tomorrow.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread development. Seven queue tasks finished overnight. An eighth, the futures calendar fix for 2027, is committed on its own branch but not marked done. There were also commits on the research docs branch, the layer six work, and the first phase of spec twenty-seven. Next up are the five open follow-ups on spec twenty-three and the ready queue. One task is still blocked on data and needs you. The Alpaca key file and the prop-firm sleeve item no longer appear on your list, and the report doesn't say why. Health shows a warning from the restarts, with no alert lines in the last day.

Calculators, kalq. The overnight run finished, and the project is blocked on your answers. That's up from four questions yesterday to seven. The unit economics work landed. Break-even customer acquisition cost is about seventy dollars forty-six cents, and the three-to-one target is about twenty-three dollars forty-nine cents. The final wording for the European paragraph in the order confirmation is done. The consent design for the European pack is done too, and two follow-on tasks are queued behind it. Those two wait on questions three through six. The second reply to the partner is approved to send. The F C C ruling is still not in the Federal Register, and the recheck is due by November tenth. Three reel notes were triaged.

IG ideas. The watcher ran at five this morning and found one new idea. It's a down Friday followed by a down Monday, which precedes a larger than usual S P Y move. It scored three and is live-executable, but it wasn't queued. Eight new posts were analysed, none waiting on a transcript. The inbox holds sixty-three ideas, thirty-six of them queued. As always, the creator claims are untested hypotheses.

Discord feed. The big change is the gap count, down from two hundred seventeen to one. The health check no longer fails on four-oh-three gaps, and notification titles with emoji or curly quotes now send. The watch list was refreshed to one hundred seventy channels across fifteen servers, one fewer than before. The listener is running and connected. The next step is to fill or acknowledge that last gap.

Kalq server hunt. Nothing has moved since Sunday, when the status file was last updated. Two leads are blocked on claiming the EpicNPC account, and one is waiting on a staff reply.

The remaining worktrees are all AlphaThread branches and are idle. They only show shared history from the sixty commits in the last day.

That's the picture. The restarts and the one Discord gap are the items to watch.

Markets

Tech sold off again on heavy volume, but most stocks actually rose, so the market's weakness was narrow.

The S&P 500 fell about half a percent. The Nasdaq 100 dropped about one point four percent, on roughly one and a half times normal volume. Heavy volume suggests real selling, not a drift lower. The Dow rose about half a percent, and small caps were basically flat.

The sector gap tells the story. Tech fell almost three percent on about one and two-thirds times normal volume. Energy fell about four percent. On the other side, consumer discretionary rose about two and a half percent, financials about one point nine, and materials about one point eight. Materials and consumer staples both closed at one-year highs. Oil dropped more than seven percent to about ninety-six dollars. The ten-year yield slipped to about four point nine percent, gold rose about one point eight percent, and bitcoin fell about two percent.

Now the unusual part. Breadth disagreed with the index. Three hundred forty-seven S&P 500 stocks rose and only one hundred fifty-five fell. The share above their fifty-day average climbed to about sixty-seven percent, up about six and a half points in five days. One read is that big tech dragged a cap-weighted index down while the average stock did fine. That can be a rotation, not a broad retreat. It is one session, though.

Individual names were wild. Lumentum fell about nineteen percent on nearly three times normal volume, and Marvell fell about thirteen percent on more than two and a half times normal. Oracle dropped about nine percent. Idexx jumped about twenty-two percent after opening up thirteen percent, on three and a half times normal volume. A gap that holds or extends on that volume often means big funds repositioned, not just day traders.

Sentiment also shifted. StockTwits skews bullish and retail, so changes against a ticker's own normal matter more than levels. Bullishness on small caps fell far below its thirty-day average, while it rose above average for the Nasdaq 100, even on a down day.

For the why: CNBC reported that crude fell below one hundred dollars amid reports of U.S.-Iran diplomatic efforts. That fits the energy drop. Airlines rose, with United up about five percent and Delta about four, which makes sense when fuel gets cheaper. Lufthansa cutting its outlook on a huge fuel bill, per Investing.com, shows how much that matters. For tech, the cause is unclear. Investing.com has been analyzing an October dive in AI-related shares, which may be part of it. Midterm elections are today, and Citi and Morgan Stanley, per MarketWatch, are both talking up outcomes, so some caution is plausible.

Concept of the day: the VIX term structure. The VIX, at about twenty-one, measures expected swings over the next month. The three-month version was about twenty-one point six. Normally the longer one is higher, since more time means more uncertainty. Their ratio rose to about point nine eight from about point nine four on Friday. As it approaches one, traders are paying nearly as much to insure against the next month as the next three. When it rises above one, near-term fear dominates, which has often shown up in real stress. We are close, not there.

item.description:
School

This briefing runs on school data from Thursday, because the early morning check had not finished, so treat everything here as possibly out of date.

As of Thursday, two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes were still unsubmitted: Module nine and Module ten, fifteen points each. Both are due tonight at midnight. Physics homework nine was due Saturday night at midnight and was also unsubmitted on Thursday, so check that it went in. Nothing was overdue at the time.

The deadline watcher did two things. Early Thursday morning it completed and submitted the physics lab prelab on Impulse and Momentum, which was about seventeen hours overdue. It scored four out of five, with every answer correct and a late penalty. Before that, the watcher could not log in to Canvas for about forty-five checks in a row, from early Wednesday until just after midnight Thursday. Deadlines were not being watched during that stretch, and the data does not show whether the login was fixed.

For grades, the physics lab Simple Harmonic Motion prelab came back four and a half out of five. Abstract Algebra posted a score of three on the chapter one homework. Your lowest overall score was Linear Algebra at sixty-seven and a half percent, a D plus. Abstract Algebra sat at seventy percent with no letter grade yet.

In email, Denise Dixon wrote about the FLATS exam. The exam you had scheduled for Thursday was apparently not going to happen, and she says to register again with BYU and the proctoring service when you are ready. Perusall also sent several unread reminders about the Module nine assignment for Prokaryotic Cell, the graduate-only one.

Two dates fall today. The FAFSA Extravaganza runs from ten to two at the Reitz Union, with help on financial aid. Florida Undergraduate Research Conference abstracts are also due today. The Emerging Scholars applications were due yesterday.

On registration, Spring registration opened Friday at two in the afternoon. An automatic plan was set to try adding six classes the moment it opened. This data predates that, so it cannot say whether the classes landed. Open OneUF and confirm your schedule. You had no holds or to-dos as of Thursday.

The most important thing today is finishing both Prokaryotic Cell quizzes before midnight, and checking that your spring schedule went through.

Projects

Good morning. Here is what needs you today.

Start with calculators. Four questions are waiting for the morning questions run. They cover how to read the billing country rule, where to move the setup control on the device, the counsel wording for the European pack paragraph, and the one-time engineering charge for the second supplier reply, forty-five thousand yen. That last answer matters most, because the reply is due Saturday. Also, the PreProduct launch needs your Shopify admin session, and everything to paste is ready. The F C C ruling recheck is due by next Tuesday. The morning questions run shows no recorded end, so it is unclear whether it finished.

Next, Discord feed. The health step failed again, and the listener reports two hundred seventeen unfilled gaps. Deletes inside those gaps are invisible. The listener itself is running and connected.

For AlphaThread, two things are open. The free Alpaca key file is still needed by two queued tasks, and it is unclear whether you have created it. And before November twenty-sixth, check the seven declared Globex holiday and early-close times against the CME's final tables. The futures prop-firm task is also still marked blocked, though you answered its questions yesterday and bought the Lucid account, which is copied by hand for now.

For the server hunt, the last follow-up to the first lead is tomorrow, then drop it.

Now the projects, starting with calculators. The overnight run finished four tasks. It applied your recent decisions to the device interface pack and the second supplier reply, updated the drafts, redid the weekly report by product type, and rechecked the F C C ruling. That ruling is still not in the Federal Register. The run made ten commits, tests are passing, and the branch is not pushed. One change landed in the wrong commit and was left as is. Next, send the second reply with the updated interface pack and spec once the engineering charge is answered. After the billing country answer, the order confirmation gets re-rendered. Yesterday you had eleven founder questions. Now it is four.

AlphaThread development moved well. The queue worker finished two tasks overnight. One added seven futures prop-firm rule profiles and a way to compare them. The follow-up ran that comparison on the patched Guru futures trades, and the ranking held at every account size. A spec for the prop-firm futures copy work was started, with a webhook route to Lucid through Tradovate. A spec for a Telegram approval loop was written. The robustness record for the earlier spec was merged. Still blocked is the first real backtest run for the rule-set tool, which needs a read-only copy of the operator database or a run in the main checkout. Open work on the main spec includes live acceptance and several follow-ups, one of which must happen before any promotion. The runner is healthy.

IG ideas is fine. The daily scrape analysed three new posts and produced no new ideas. Nothing is waiting for a transcript.

On Discord feed, the watch list was refreshed. It now covers one hundred seventy-one channels across fifteen servers, up from one hundred six across twelve yesterday. Four servers had nothing worth watching. The config change is uncommitted, with an untracked backup beside it. The health failure is the one you heard earlier.

On the server hunt, the two leads you were asked about yesterday are settled. Both were vetted and passed. A message went to a moderator on the Embedded Engineering server, while the other server has still not replied. If the moderator stays quiet, nudge the owner on Wednesday. Two EpicNPC leads remain blocked until that account is claimed.

The other AlphaThread worktrees are idle. Two carry small leftovers, some modified cache files and a stray cache folder.

That is everything. The Discord health step is the one carryover that has not moved.

Markets

Friday was a rough day for tech: the Nasdaq 100 fell about three and a half percent, its worst of the group, while energy, staples and health care held up.

The S&P 500 dropped about one point eight percent. The Dow lost about one percent, and small caps fell about one and a half percent. Volume tells you how much conviction was behind it. The S&P traded at about twice normal volume and the Nasdaq 100 at more than twice normal. Heavy volume on a drop suggests real selling, not just thin trading, so it is harder to dismiss as noise.

Within the market, the tech sector fell nearly five percent on more than twice normal volume. Energy rose almost two percent and closed at a one-year high. Staples rose about one and a half percent, also at a one-year high, and health care closed at a high too. Gold fell about three percent and sits at a one-year low. Oil rose about two percent to just over one hundred four dollars. The ten-year yield slipped to about four point nine percent.

Now the unusual part. Several big names gapped down hard at the open. Intel opened down about twenty-six percent and closed down about twenty-nine percent, on more than four times normal volume. Reddit fell about twenty-nine percent on nearly seven times normal volume. Gaps that big on heavy volume usually mean an earnings report or guidance reset that forced a fast repricing. And when the close is near or below the open, as with Intel, buyers did not step in to rescue the price.

Second, rotation. Money moved out of tech and into defensive and energy names. The gap between the best and worst sector was about seven points. Dozens of stocks hit new one-year highs, mostly in energy, health care and staples. One read is investors are not leaving stocks altogether, but moving toward safer, cash-generating businesses.

Third, the VIX rose to about nineteen, but it still sits below the three-month VIX. That is the normal pattern, and it suggests traders see this as a shock, not full panic. Breadth also held up better than the index. About sixty-one percent of S&P 500 stocks are above their fifty-day average, slightly higher than five days ago. The damage was concentrated in tech.

As for the cause, the data does not give a single clear reason. Reuters, via Investing.com, wrote about an October dive in AI-related shares testing the broader market. The Wall Street Journal reported that AI investors have been rushing to hedge against a tech downturn. That fits the picture, though it does not prove the cause of Friday's drop. CNBC also reported that crude fell below one hundred dollars on reports of diplomatic efforts between the U.S. and Iran.

Concept of the day: the VIX term structure. The VIX measures expected swings over the next thirty days, and the three-month VIX does the same over a longer window. Normally the longer one is higher, because more time means more uncertainty. When the short-term number rises above the longer one, it signals acute stress. Friday the VIX stayed below the three-month, so options traders were pricing a bump, not a crisis.

AlphaThread

Quiet weekend on the trading side. No trades opened or closed, no gate milestones, and no sleeve changed version. Nothing is halted, and there are no reconciliation breaks. Your three running paper stores show a fresh start time from Friday afternoon, but none counted a restart in the last day, and all three are running.

Three research studies changed status. The one on whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is now marked active, and you chose to keep it open. The one on low relative volatility in mega-caps and the one on whether implied volatility underprices what follows both landed on needs a better test. No new ideas came into the inbox. Your R eleven score did not move.

Nothing is live yet. Your Interactive Brokers account is set as primary, but it is only approved for the most basic options level.

On paper, the demo put spread sleeve has eight closed trades and is up eight dollars. That is eight of twenty trades toward going live, and thirteen of ninety days. One position is still open. Paper profit uses mid-price fills, so treat it as an upper bound.

Your copy Mordy sleeve has no closed trades yet. That is zero of twenty trades and five of ninety days.

Flow levels has two closed trades and is up eleven dollars. That is two of twenty trades and four of ninety days.

Flow levels futures has no trades and sits at one of ninety days. Its latest research session allowed uncovered short legs, so it cannot go live as it stands.

On research, the creator-calls study stays open and the two volatility studies need better tests. Beyond those, a few are waiting on you. The data gap study is waiting on your review. The odd RIVN timestamps study needs your approval for one probe. The insider buying study needs an approved contact string for the SEC before it can run. The capture universe study needs live spikes to settle its request budget. The Discord copy study is collecting data, with nine calls against the forty it needs. Six other studies are settled.

On R eleven, Vin's reversal levels, you have two closed real trades averaging about a third of an R. The placebo has four closed trades averaging nearly two R, so the placebo is ahead. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, a mean of at least fifteen hundredths of an R, and a clear edge over the placebo. You are far from that.

The ideas inbox holds sixty-two ideas, thirty-six of them queued. Discord had fifteen new caller alerts, mostly closes. They are unscored, so treat them as noise for now.

Friday the VIX stayed below the three-month, so options traders were pricing a bump, not a crisis.

AlphaThread

Quiet weekend on the trading side. No trades opened or closed, no gate milestones, and no sleeve changed version. Nothing is halted, and there are no reconciliation breaks. Your three running paper stores show a fresh start time from Friday afternoon, but none counted a restart in the last day, and all three are running.

Three research studies changed status. The one on whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is now marked active, and you chose to keep it open. The one on low relative volatility in mega-caps and the one on whether implied volatility underprices what follows both landed on needs a better test. No new ideas came into the inbox. Your R eleven score did not move.

Nothing is live yet. Your Interactive Brokers account is set as primary, but it is only approved for the most basic options level.

On paper, the demo put spread sleeve has eight closed trades and is up eight dollars. That is eight of twenty trades toward going live, and thirteen of ninety days. One position is still open. Paper profit uses mid-price fills, so treat it as an upper bound.

Your copy Mordy sleeve has no closed trades yet. That is zero of twenty trades and five of ninety days.

Flow levels has two closed trades and is up eleven dollars. That is two of twenty trades and four of ninety days.

Flow levels futures has no trades and sits at one of ninety days. Its latest research session allowed uncovered short legs, so it cannot go live as it stands.

On research, the creator-calls study stays open and the two volatility studies need better tests. Beyond those, a few are waiting on you. The data gap study is waiting on your review. The odd RIVN timestamps study needs your approval for one probe. The insider buying study needs an approved contact string for the SEC before it can run. item.title: pod — Sun, Nov 1
item.description:
School

This morning's school check hadn't finished, so everything here is from Thursday, October twenty-ninth, and may be out of date.

As of then, nothing was overdue. Your physics homework, HW nine, was due Saturday night at midnight. That has passed, and the data can't tell you whether it went in, so check Canvas. Two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes, Module nine and Module ten, are due tomorrow, Monday, at midnight. Each is worth fifteen points, and neither had been submitted.

The deadline watcher had a rough stretch. It couldn't log in to Canvas for forty-five checks in a row, from early Wednesday morning until just after midnight Thursday. Deadlines weren't being watched during that time. Right after that, it found the physics lab prelab on Impulse and Momentum about eighteen hours overdue and submitted it. All answers were correct, but the late penalty left you with four out of five.

On grades, the physics lab Simple Harmonic Motion prelab came back four and a half out of five. Abstract Algebra posted your chapter one homework, scored three, though the points possible showed as zero. Your overall scores then were Prokaryotic Cell at an A minus, the physics lab at an A, and Physics at a B plus. Abstract Algebra sat at seventy percent with no letter yet. Linear Algebra was the weak spot at sixty-seven and a half, a D plus.

Your Physics professor was away at a conference that week. The learning assistant, Neerav, covered office hours near room twenty-one eighty. Wait for the next announcement before counting on that again.

In email, there are a few dates. The Emerging Scholars Program applications are due today, Sunday, around noon. Florida Undergraduate Research Conference abstracts are due tomorrow. A financial aid event, the FAFSA Extravaganza, runs tomorrow from ten to two in the Reitz Union. There was also a note from the FLATS exam office about re-registering with the proctoring service if you skipped your scheduled exam. Reply if you still need to take it. Perusall reminders for the graduate-only assignments keep piling up, so ignore those unless they apply to you.

For registration, Spring twenty twenty-seven opened Friday at two in the afternoon. An automatic plan was set to try adding six classes the moment it opened. The data doesn't show whether it worked, so check your schedule in OneUF. You had no holds and no to-dos.

The most important thing today is to confirm your physics homework went in, then finish both Prokaryotic Cell quizzes before tomorrow's midnight deadline.

Projects

You have a full list this morning, with the calculators project first.

For calculators, the overnight run left eleven founder questions. Start with the first: paste the interim privacy policy now, because it's ready. The launch setup for the pre-product page also needs your admin session. And the second reply to the supplier is due by November seventh, with the F C C recheck due by November tenth.

For the kalq server hunt, you need to join the two screened leads with the burner account. Log the okbudi account back into Discord in Chrome. And approve or edit the holding reply to Huva22.

For the Discord feed, the daily health step failed again, with two hundred sixteen unfilled gaps. Check today's Discord log.

For AlphaThread, create the Alpaca key file if you haven't. Two confirmatory runs are waiting on it. Also verify the seven Globex holiday times against the C M E tables before November twenty-sixth.

Now the projects, starting with calculators. The overnight run finished seven tasks. The privacy policy is ready to paste. The device display pack for Wonderful PCB is done, as a document and a PDF, and the supplier reply attaches it with the latest spec. There's also a draft of the order confirmation and a copy and paste order for the pre-product template. The server change that shapes AI answers to the device display exists locally only and isn't deployed. The F C C ruling isn't in the Federal Register yet. Tests pass, with three hundred three on functions and two hundred seventy-three on the database. Thirteen commits sit on the overnight branch, not pushed. Next, confirm the twenty by eleven text grid with the supplier, and deploy the server change with the next dev gateway deploy. The F C C recheck starts tomorrow. One more thing: the Meta ad account setup from yesterday no longer appears on your list. The report doesn't say whether it was finished.

AlphaThread, on development. The research worker finished the geopolitical risk jump-flag test on the Cboe put index, and both variants failed. It also committed the pre-registration and a sixty-day pilot for another study, with no completion event, so that one's status is unclear. The IG watcher queued a batch screen of seven ideas. Four commits landed on the worker branch. Next are the two confirmatory runs once the key file exists, a first run of the Vest Markets rule set on a real backtest, and that batch screen. Spec twenty-three still has five open tasks. One must land before any promotion, and the holiday check is due before November twenty-sixth. The runner looks healthy, with no alerts.

Discord feed. Curation still covers a hundred six channels across twelve servers, and the config change is uncommitted. The listener is running and connected, with event counts rising. But the gap count hasn't moved since yesterday, and deletes inside those gaps are invisible.

Kalq server hunt. Both leads replied with invites and passed screening. They're discoverable, Russian, and off-topic. A holding reply is drafted for one of them. The first lead didn't answer the day-two follow-up. One last follow-up goes out November third, then drop it. Two other leads are blocked until the EpicNPC account is claimed. One waits on the okbudi login, and one waits on staff.

IG ideas. The watcher ran fine and found eleven new posts, with no new ideas. No posts are waiting on transcripts, down from seven yesterday.

The other three AlphaThread checkouts are quiet. They show only the shared worker commits, and one still has two modified bars-cache files.

That's the full list. The privacy policy is the one to do first.

Markets

Stocks fell hard on Friday, led by a sharp selloff in technology on heavy volume.

The S&P 500 dropped about one point eight percent, with volume roughly double normal. The Nasdaq 100 fell about three and a half percent on more than twice normal volume. The Dow lost about one percent and small caps slid about one and a half percent. A drop on double volume shows real conviction. Lots of people were selling, not just a thin market drifting lower.

Tech was the center of it. The tech sector fell nearly five percent, again on more than twice normal volume. Meanwhile energy rose almost two percent to a one-year high, and consumer staples and health care both closed at one-year highs. That is a rotation, with money leaving growth and moving toward defensive and commodity names. Oil rose about two percent to just above a hundred and four dollars a barrel.

Gold fell about three percent to a one-year low, which is unusual. It is often a safe haven, but it fell while the ten-year yield eased to about four point nine percent. Bitcoin slipped under one percent.

Now the unusual stuff. First, the single-stock gaps. Intel opened down about twenty-six percent and closed down nearly twenty-nine percent on more than four times normal volume. Reddit fell about twenty-nine percent on nearly seven times normal volume. When a stock gaps down at the open and keeps falling all day, it often means the news reset expectations and holders kept selling into it, rather than buying the dip. Second, breadth. Only about sixty-one percent of S&P 500 stocks sit above their fifty-day average, and that is slightly higher than five days ago. So the damage was concentrated in a narrow group of big tech names, not a broad collapse. Third, the VIX closed near nineteen, up about two points. It sits below the three-month VIX, so traders are not pricing near-term panic. The put to call ratio of about zero point six six is on the low side, which suggests options traders were not rushing into protection.

Why it happened. Investing.com reported that Wall Street closed sharply lower as fears over AI cash burn sparked a tech selloff. CNBC reported that S&P revised Meta's outlook downward on cash flow and capex concerns. MarketWatch wrote about Intel's worst day in decades, a roughly one hundred forty billion dollar wipeout, and Reddit's biggest one-day drop ever. The Wall Street Journal, via Investing.com, said AI investors are rushing to hedge against a possible tech downturn. Why gold fell so far is less clear from the data alone.

Concept of the day: the VIX term structure. The VIX measures expected stock market swings over the next thirty days, and the three-month VIX measures the same thing further out. Normally the longer one is higher, because there is more time for surprises. When the near-term VIX jumps above the longer one, that signals acute stress. Friday's ratio was below one, about point nine four, even after a big tech drop. That says traders saw this as a sharp sector selloff, not a market-wide emergency. One day does not make a trend, but a flip above one would be worth watching.

AlphaThread

Nothing changed in your trading since yesterday. No halts, no reconciliation breaks, no restarts, and no new trades or gate milestones. The paper numbers are from Friday's close, and the weekend adds nothing. The research side has movement: three studies are flagged as updated, covered below. No new ideas landed in the inbox, and the R eleven score is unchanged.

Nothing is live yet. Your broker account is only approved for the most basic level of options trading, so real money can't trade spreads.

On paper, the demo put spread sleeve has eight of twenty trades toward going live, and thirteen of ninety days. It's up about eight dollars in realized profit, with one spread still open. Paper fills happen at the midpoint, so that profit is an upper bound, and it doesn't count as evidence for going live. The same caveat applies to every sleeve here.

Your copy Mordy sleeve is running cleanly. It has made no trades yet, so it's at zero of twenty trades and five of ninety days.

Flow levels is running cleanly too. It has two closed trades, up about eleven dollars, so two of twenty trades and four of ninety days.

Flow levels futures is also running cleanly, with no trades, zero of twenty and one of ninety days. It can't be promoted live as it stands, because its latest research session allowed uncovered short positions.

On research, three studies have updated status. The question of whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is still open. The one creator tested doesn't predict direction, and you've asked to keep it going across more creators. The question of whether low relative volatility in a mega-cap reverts upward needs a better test, since on prices alone it's ordinary mean reversion. The follow-up on whether implied volatility underprices what comes next also needs a better test. The gap it found is indistinguishable from chance.

Two studies are waiting on you. The market calendar gap review needs your approval before it earns a spec, and the odd Rivian timestamps need one approved probe to close.

The Schwab request budget study is a planning question that needs a better test. The Discord copy-trading study needs more data, with nine calls against the forty required. The insider buying study is pre-registered and waiting on an approved contact string for the SEC before it can run.

On R eleven, the reversal levels study, your real trades have closed two, averaging about a third of a unit of risk. The placebo has closed four, averaging nearly two. The bar needs thirty real trades and a clear lead over placebo, so it's far from being met.

Six other studies are closed or answered. The ideas inbox holds sixty-two ideas, none new.

item.title: pod — Sat, Oct 31
item.description:
School

This school check is from Thursday morning, two days old, so some of this may have changed.

As of then, your Physics homework, HW nine, was due tonight, Saturday, at eleven fifty-nine. It's worth ten points, and it showed as not submitted. Two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes, Module nine and Module ten, are due Monday night at the same time. Each is worth fifteen points. Nothing was overdue.

The deadline watcher had a rough stretch. From early Wednesday morning until just after midnight Thursday, it failed to log in to Canvas forty-five times in a row. Deadlines weren't being watched during that time. Once it recovered, it found your physics lab prelab on Impulse and Momentum, nearly eighteen hours overdue. It completed and submitted it on its own. Every answer was correct, but the late penalty left you with four out of five.

On grades, the physics lab also posted a four and a half out of five on the Simple Harmonic Motion prelab, and it sits at an A. Abstract Algebra posted a score of three on the chapter one homework. The one score to watch is Linear Algebra, at sixty-seven and a half percent, a D plus. Prokaryotic Cell is at an A minus, and Physics is a B plus.

In your email, Physics put out a note that the professor was away at a conference, and a learning assistant named Neerav covered office hours near room twenty-one eighty. That's past now, but it's worth knowing if you need help with homework nine.

Your language department wrote about the FLATS exam. They assumed you didn't want to take the one scheduled for Thursday. When you're ready, you'll need to register again with the proctoring service. A few dates are coming up. Emerging Scholars applications are due Sunday, and Florida Undergraduate Research Conference abstracts are due Monday. On Monday from ten to two, the financial aid office hosts a FAFSA help event in the Reitz Union.

Spring registration opened Friday at two in the afternoon. The automatic plan was set to try adding six classes the moment it opened. This data can't confirm whether that worked, so check your schedule.

The most important thing today is Physics homework nine, due tonight, if it isn't already in.

Projects

You have six things today. The most time-sensitive is for calculators, also called kalq. You answered that the Meta Business Manager and ad account should be set up now, so the account builds history before any conversion ads. There's no conversion spend yet. Also for kalq, the launch configuration for PreProduct needs your browser admin access, for the PreProduct and Notifications screens. And the privacy policy still needs a publish date from you.

For AlphaThread, you still need to create the free Alpaca market-data key file in your secrets folder. Two research tasks are waiting on it, and it's unclear whether the file exists yet.

For the Discord feed, the daily health step failed again. The listener is running and connected, but it reports two hundred sixteen unfilled gaps, so deletes inside those gaps are invisible. Yesterday it was one gap.

Two deadlines. The device interface pack promised to Wonderful PCB is due Saturday, November seventh. And you need to verify the seven Globex holiday and early-close times against CME's final tables before November twenty-sixth.

Now the projects. AlphaThread development had a productive night. The overnight queue finished five items. The robustness battery is now wired into the backtest record. The plan for the first two stories of the robustness spec is done, along with its review leftovers. The trend and regime overlay for the premium-selling strategies is finished, and the third story, a robustness gate criterion, landed too. Separately, the Vest one-step presets and sleeve-budget rules are committed. That's thirteen commits in a day, mostly on the robustness branch. The main checkout sits on the signal sleeve branch, clean. The decisions you were asked about yesterday no longer show up as open, so work moved past them. Still blocked are the opening-range breakout study and the SPY momentum study, both on the Alpaca key. The Vest presets still need a route to copy a real backtest database before a first real run. On the earlier spec, five tasks stay open, and one of them must land before any promotion. The runner is healthy, with no alerts.

For calculators, the overnight run ended fine with six tasks done. It applied your founder answers to the security page and the product page, finished a working first-hour checklist, added official EU legal sources, followed up on the European security standard, and added a security-updates question to the product FAQ. Your answers are recorded, and the order-confirmation draft is now ready to start. A reply went to Wonderful PCB with your choices, and the device pack is queued. Fourteen commits sit on the overnight branch, not pushed. The overnight guard denied two shell commands that touched its own guardrails. The run report says nothing was lost. At launch, you'll need a security thank-you page and an acknowledgments entry in the security file.

The Discord feed did its curation. The watch list is down to one hundred six channels across twelve servers, thirty-four fewer than yesterday, including several alert channels. Gold Squad, Odd Lots, TPE's School and Quanted still have nothing worth watching. The config file has uncommitted changes. Next step is finding out why health failed and whether those gaps can be filled.

IG ideas is fine. The watcher ran at six this morning, analysed fourteen new posts, and produced no new ideas. Seven posts are still waiting on transcripts, five from velocity options and two from rp dot profits.

The other three AlphaThread checkouts are idle, with nothing new. One has two uncommitted price cache files.

That's the picture. The Meta account and the Alpaca key are the quickest wins today.

Markets

Friday was a sharp, tech-led selloff. The Nasdaq 100 fell about three and a half percent, and money moved into energy, health care and staples.

The S&P 500 dropped about one point eight percent. The Dow lost about one percent. Small caps fell about one point six percent. The big indexes traded at roughly twice normal volume, which shows real conviction. Sellers were committed, not just drifting. Small caps traded on normal volume, so that drop is less convincing.

Tech did the damage. The sector fell nearly five percent on more than double normal volume. Energy rose almost two percent and closed at a one-year high. Staples gained about one and a half percent, also at a high. Gold fell about three percent to a one-year low, roughly thirty percent below its peak. Oil rose about two percent to around one hundred and four dollars. The ten-year yield slipped to about four point nine percent.

Now the unusual parts. First, the single-stock wreckage. Intel fell nearly thirty percent on about four and a half times normal volume, after opening about twenty-six percent lower. Reddit fell about the same, on nearly seven times normal volume. A gap down that holds all day on that much volume usually means big institutions were selling, not just retail traders.

Second, rotation. Forty-five S&P stocks hit one-year highs, many in energy, health care and staples, against five at lows. When money flees one corner and piles into defensive ones, it can mean investors are repositioning, not abandoning stocks altogether.

Third, breadth. Decliners beat advancers, two hundred seventy-five to two hundred twenty-eight. That is a fairly mild split for an index down nearly two percent. The share of stocks above their fifty-day average actually edged up, to about sixty-one percent. One read is that the pain was concentrated in a few huge tech names, not broad. One day is not a trend.

The VIX rose about two points to roughly nineteen. Its three-month cousin sits a bit higher, which is still the calm arrangement. The put to call ratio rose to about point six six.

Why? Investing.com says Wall Street closed sharply lower as fears over AI cash burn sparked a tech selloff. MarketWatch reports Intel had its worst day in decades, a one hundred forty billion dollar wipeout. CNBC reports S&P revised its outlook on Meta downward over cash flow and capital spending concerns. MarketWatch also says Reddit logged its biggest one-day drop ever. Why gold fell is less clear, though MarketWatch notes it dropped to its lowest in a year despite renewed Iran jitters.

Today the market moved in that direction, without getting there.

AlphaThread

Those stops pushed its total realized profit down fifteen dollars, to about eight dollars. One of the new trades is still open. That sleeve is now at eight of twenty trades toward going live. Paper profit uses mid-price fills, so treat it as an upper bound.

On health, nothing halted and no reconciliation breaks. Your three running sleeves had no restarts in the last day. Your flow levels futures sleeve no longer shows a version, because no build manifest was found for it. It was version zero point one yesterday.

On research, three studies changed status. The question of whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is still active, and the one creator tested so far does not predict direction. The low relative volatility study and the follow-up on whether implied vol underprices what comes next both say they need a better test. No new ideas came into the inbox.

For R eleven, the score did not move. You have two closed real trades, averaging plus zero point three two R. Four placebo trades average plus one point nine three. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, a mean of at least plus zero point one five, and a lead over the placebo. So it is far from either.

Now the roll call.

Nothing is live yet. Your broker is Interactive Brokers, but the account is only approved for the simplest options level.

On paper, your put spread sleeve is running in the main store. It has eight closed trades and is up about eight dollars. It is at thirteen of ninety days.

Your copy Mordy sleeve is running cleanly with no trades yet. It is at zero of twenty trades and five of ninety days.

Your flow levels sleeve is running cleanly with two closed trades, up eleven dollars. It is at two of twenty trades and four of ninety days.

Your flow levels futures sleeve is running with no trades yet. It is at zero of twenty trades and one of ninety days. Its latest research session allows uncovered short legs, so it cannot go live as it stands.

School

This school check is from Thursday morning, two days old, so some of this may have changed.

As of then, your Physics homework, HW nine, was due tonight, Saturday, at eleven fifty-nine. It's worth ten points, and it showed as not submitted. Two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes, Module nine and Module ten, are due Monday night at the same time. Each is worth fifteen points. Nothing was overdue.

The deadline watcher had a rough stretch. From early Wednesday morning until just after midnight Thursday, it failed to log in to Canvas forty-five times in a row. Deadlines weren't being watched during that time. Once it recovered, it found your physics lab prelab on Impulse and Momentum, nearly eighteen hours overdue. It completed and submitted it on its own. Every answer was correct, but the late penalty left you with four out of five.

On grades, the physics lab also posted a four and a half out of five on the Simple Harmonic Motion prelab, and it sits at an A. Abstract Algebra posted a score of three on the chapter one homework. The one score to watch is Linear Algebra, at sixty-seven and a half percent, a D plus. Prokaryotic Cell is at an A minus, and Physics is a B plus.

In your email, Physics put out a note that the professor was away at a conference, and a learning assistant named Neerav covered office hours near room twenty-one eighty. That's past now, but it's worth knowing if you need help with homework nine.

Your language department wrote about the FLATS exam. They assumed you didn't want to take the one scheduled for Thursday. When you're ready, you'll need to register again with the proctoring service. A few dates are coming up. Emerging Scholars applications are due Sunday, and Florida Undergraduate Research Conference abstracts are due Monday. On Monday from ten to two, the financial aid office hosts a FAFSA help event in the Reitz Union.

Spring registration opened Friday at two in the afternoon. The automatic plan was set to try adding six classes the moment it opened. This data can't confirm whether that worked, so check your schedule.

The most important thing today is Physics homework nine, due tonight, if it isn't already in.

Projects

You have six things today. The most time-sensitive is for calculators, also called kalq. You answered that the Meta Business Manager and ad account should be set up now, so the account builds history before any conversion ads. There's no conversion spend yet. Also for kalq, the launch configuration for PreProduct needs your browser admin access, for the PreProduct and Notifications screens. And the privacy policy still needs a publish date from you.

For AlphaThread, you still need to create the free Alpaca market-data key file in your secrets folder. Two research tasks are waiting on it, and it's unclear whether the file exists yet.

For the Discord feed, the daily health step failed again. The listener is running and connected, but it reports two hundred sixteen unfilled gaps, so deletes inside those gaps are invisible. Yesterday it was one gap.

Two deadlines. The device interface pack promised to Wonderful PCB is due Saturday, November seventh. And you need to verify the seven Globex holiday and early-close times against CME's final tables before November twenty-sixth.

Now the projects. AlphaThread development had a productive night. The overnight queue finished five items. The robustness battery is now wired into the backtest record. The plan for the first two stories of the robustness spec is done, along with its review leftovers. The trend and regime overlay for the premium-selling strategies is finished, and the third story, a robustness gate criterion, landed too. Separately, the Vest one-step presets and sleeve-budget rules are committed. That's thirteen commits in a day, mostly on the robustness branch. The main checkout sits on the signal sleeve branch, clean. The decisions you were asked about yesterday no longer show up as open, so work moved past them. Still blocked are the opening-range breakout study and the SPY momentum study, both on the Alpaca key. The Vest presets still need a route to copy a real backtest database before a first real run. On the earlier spec, five tasks stay open, and one of them must land before any promotion. The runner is healthy, with no alerts.

For calculators, the overnight run ended fine with six tasks done. It applied your founder answers to the security page and the product page, finished a working first-hour checklist, added official EU legal sources, followed up on the European security standard, and added a security-updates question to the product FAQ. Your answers are recorded, and the order-confirmation draft is now ready to start. A reply went to Wonderful PCB with your choices, and the device pack is queued. Fourteen commits sit on the overnight branch, not pushed. The overnight guard denied two shell commands that touched its own guardrails. The run report says nothing was lost. At launch, you'll need a security thank-you page and an acknowledgments entry in the security file.

The Discord feed did its curation. The watch list is down to one hundred six channels across twelve servers, thirty-four fewer than yesterday, including several alert channels. Gold Squad, Odd Lots, TPE's School and Quanted still have nothing worth watching. The config file has uncommitted changes. Next step is finding out why health failed and whether those gaps can be filled.

IG ideas is fine. The watcher ran at six this morning, analysed fourteen new posts, and produced no new ideas. Seven posts are still waiting on transcripts, five from velocity options and two from rp dot profits.

The other three AlphaThread checkouts are idle, with nothing new. One has two uncommitted price cache files.

That's the picture. The Meta account and the Alpaca key are the quickest wins today.

Markets

Friday was a sharp, tech-led selloff. The Nasdaq 100 fell about three and a half percent, and money moved into energy, health care and staples.

The S&P 500 dropped about one point eight percent. The Dow lost about one percent. Small caps fell about one point six percent. The big indexes traded at roughly twice normal volume, which shows real conviction. Sellers were committed, not just drifting. Small caps traded on normal volume, so that drop is less convincing.

Tech did the damage. The sector fell nearly five percent on more than double normal volume. Energy rose almost two percent and closed at a one-year high. Staples gained about one and a half percent, also at a high. Gold fell about three percent to a one-year low, roughly thirty percent below its peak. Oil rose about two percent to around one hundred and four dollars. The ten-year yield slipped to about four point nine percent.

Now the unusual parts. First, the single-stock wreckage. Intel fell nearly thirty percent on about four and a half times normal volume, after opening about twenty-six percent lower.
