item.description:
School

Heads up: this briefing runs on data collected yesterday, October 29, because the early morning school check had not finished. Treat everything as possibly out of date.

Nothing was overdue in that data. Your physics homework, HW nine, is due tomorrow night, Saturday at midnight. It's worth ten points. Your two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes, Module nine and Module ten, are due Monday night at midnight. Each is worth fifteen points.

The deadline watcher had a rough stretch. It could not log in to Canvas for forty-five checks in a row, from early Wednesday morning until just after midnight Thursday. Deadlines were not being watched during that time. Once it recovered, it found the physics lab prelab on Impulse and Momentum about seventeen hours overdue, and submitted it. All the answers were correct, but the late penalty left you with four out of five.

On grades, the physics lab prelab on Simple Harmonic Motion came back four and a half out of five. Abstract Algebra posted your chapter one homework with a score of three, with no point total listed. Your physics lab is at ninety-six percent, an A. Linear Algebra is the one to watch. It sits at sixty-seven and a half percent, a D plus, unchanged from the day before. Abstract Algebra is at seventy percent with no letter grade yet.

In email, the FLATS exam office wrote that, assuming you did not want to take the exam scheduled for Thursday, you will need to register again with BYU and the proctoring service when you are ready. If you still need that exam, that is your next step.

Perusall has been sending reminders that the Module nine assignment is not complete in Prokaryotic Cell. It is marked for the graduate section only, so ignore it if that does not apply to you.

A few dates are coming up. Emerging Scholars Program applications are due Sunday. Abstracts for the Florida Undergraduate Research Conference are due Monday. Also on Monday, from ten to two at the Reitz Union, financial aid is hosting a FAFSA help event.

Registration is the big one. Spring registration opens today at two in the afternoon. You have no holds and no to-dos, and you're eligible. Your automatic registration plan is set to fire the moment the window opens, and it will try to add the six classes you picked.

The most important thing today is spring registration at two, so make sure your plan is ready, and then get started on that physics homework.

Projects

Here is what needs you today.

Discord feed first. The health check failed again this morning, and the listener still has one unfilled gap. Deletes inside that gap are invisible, so it's worth investigating.

AlphaThread has the most decisions. First, whether to put a free Alpaca data key in your secrets folder. That unblocks two research studies. Second, whether to buy minute history for NQ futures. The recommendation is no. Third, whether a failed robustness battery should block a promotion from research to paper. The recommendation is no, just record it. Fourth, how a real backtest reaches the survival command, and which strategy and rule set it should use. There is also a deadline. Before November twenty-sixth, check the seven Globex holiday and early-close times for 2026 against the final CME tables.

For kalq, the open founder items are a Judge.me login or token, setting up forwarding for the security address, and a capped key for the photo test.

For kalq-discord, you need to claim the EpicNPC account. It blocks two outreach messages, and one other target has no contact route.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread development moved a lot. Seven tasks are done, and the big merge landed in main, bringing in specs twenty-two and twenty-three plus the earlier research work. The test suite shows over five thousand passing and none failing. A read-only paper snapshot command and a weekday afternoon task also merged. That was forty-eight commits in a day. Four research tasks are built but blocked on your decisions. Spec twenty-four, the robustness record, is drafted and clarified. Next is planning its first two user stories, and the third waits on your promotion answer. Five items on spec twenty-three are still open. The project stays marked blocked, as it was yesterday.

Calculators, kalq. The overnight run finished three queued tasks and added the belief-brief fields. The FCC re-check could start today, and part of it is done, using the FCC order and the Sunshine notice. The rest waits for the adopted FCC order, and is pencilled in from November sixth. Your founder answers from today are recorded. The overnight branch has eighteen commits and has not been pushed. Next are small document cleanups in the security, product data, and comment filter files. Still blocked are one task needing a publish date, and one needing your browser admin access.

IG ideas ran fine. The watcher found thirteen new ideas from three hundred and four posts, a big jump from none yesterday. The inbox now holds sixty-two ideas, with twenty-nine queued. The six visible new ideas all scored three and can be executed live, but none is queued. Eleven posts are waiting for transcripts, six from one creator and five from another.

Discord feed. Curation added seven channels, so you now watch one hundred and forty channels across twelve servers. Four servers were judged not worth watching, same as yesterday. The listener is connected with about forty-four hundred events logged. The health failure is the one thing to chase, and it's the second day running.

Kalq-discord. You approved five outreach messages and a track of directory targets, capped at one hundred. Three messages went out, one directory was pitched through a moderator channel, two were skipped, and one is on hold. The rest wait on the blocks mentioned earlier.

The pod project is fine. It gained Markets, AlphaThread, and School segments, the research roll call now covers only open or changed findings, and yesterday's episode published without trouble.

Two AlphaThread worktrees are idle. The IBKR one is clean on main, and the research one has uncommitted changes but no commits of its own.

That's the picture. The Discord health check is the quickest thing to look at, and the AlphaThread decisions are the most valuable.

Markets

Wall Street had a lopsided Thursday session: a handful of giant tech and software names fell hard, while most of the market quietly went up.

The S&P 500 slipped about point four percent on roughly normal volume. The Nasdaq 100 fell about one point four percent, also on normal volume. The Dow lost about point four percent. Small caps went the other way, up about one percent, though on lighter volume than usual, so that move is easier to reverse.

The sector picture shows the split. Health care rose about two point four percent on nearly one and three-quarters times normal volume, and closed at a one-year high. Heavy volume on a high shows real buying. Real estate, staples and utilities each rose about one and a half percent or more. Communication services fell about one point nine percent on over one and a half times normal volume, and closed at a one-year low. Tech fell about one point two percent.

Now the unusual part. Google's two share classes each dropped about twelve percent on more than five times normal volume. ServiceNow fell about twenty-seven percent on six times normal volume, and Fortinet fell about twenty percent. All of these gapped down at the open. A gap on volume like that usually means new information arrived overnight, often earnings, and big holders repriced all at once instead of selling gradually. The headlines here don't say what triggered it, so the cause is unclear.

Second, breadth. About four hundred and six stocks in the S&P 500 rose, against ninety-seven that fell. The share above their fifty-day average improved to about sixty-six percent, from about sixty-one percent five days ago. So the index decline came from a few large stocks, not broad weakness.

Third, fear gauges stayed calm. The VIX sat at about seventeen, below the three-month VIX at about nineteen. That is the normal shape, and it suggests no near-term panic. The equity put to call ratio was about point five eight, which means traders were leaning toward calls.

Elsewhere, the ten-year yield eased about one percent to just under five percent. Bitcoin fell about four percent on nearly one and three-quarters times normal volume. CNBC reports Binance suffered a hack of about six point three billion dollars, which plausibly explains the selling. Oil settled around one hundred and two dollars, and energy edged up. CNBC reports Exxon and Chevron beat earnings expectations on strong refining profits.

Looking ahead, CNBC reports Amazon was down about seven percent and Intel down about twenty-five percent in premarket trading after earnings, and Investing.com says European shares dipped on AI cash-burn fears. That is a possible follow-through for tech, but it's one morning.

Concept of the day: the S&P 500 is weighted by company size, so a few huge stocks can pull the index down even when most members rise. Yesterday showed it clearly. About four hundred stocks advanced, yet the index fell, because Alphabet and other heavyweights dropped sharply. When the index and breadth disagree, ask whether the move is concentrated in a few names or genuinely broad. Here it was concentrated, which is often less worrying than a decline led by many stocks.

AlphaThread

Health first. Three of your paper stores each restarted three times in the last day: copy Mordy, flow levels, and flow levels futures. All three are running now, after restarting early this morning. None is halted, and there were no reconciliation breaks. Snapshots are fresh.

No trades opened or closed in the last day.

Some research moved. Your free options data survey now has MarketData.app adopted as a one-year backfill. The study of Instagram creators' stock calls is active, as you asked. The put spread study is dead as a premium edge, since the profit was just market beta. The variance premium study survives narrowly, but its straddle can never trade live. The iron butterfly follow-up is dead, because the wings cost more than the premium. And the insider cluster buys study is pre-registered, waiting on you to approve a contact string for the SEC before it can run.

Thirteen new ideas landed in the inbox, mostly about index drawdowns, end-of-October seasonality into year-end, and FOMC day behavior. The inbox holds sixty-two ideas, twenty-nine of them queued.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. Your broker account is still at the lowest options permission level, so live trading is blocked.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve has five closed trades and is up about twenty-three dollars. One position is still open. It sits at five of twenty trades and twelve of ninety days toward going live, and its research gate is not met.

Copy Mordy, version zero point three, has no trades yet. It is four days in, so zero of twenty trades and four of ninety days.

Flow levels, version zero point three, has two closed trades and is up about eleven dollars. That is two of twenty trades and three of ninety days.

Flow levels futures, version zero point one, started yesterday with no trades. It is zero of ninety days. It also cannot be promoted live as it stands, because its research session allowed uncovered short legs.

One honest note: paper profit is filled at mid-price, so treat it as an upper bound, not evidence for going live.

On research, a few items are waiting. The gap detection findings are waiting on your review. The Rivian timestamp question needs your approval for one probe to close it. The Discord copy-trading study has nine calls against the forty it needs, with no hint of an edge, so the paper forward test will answer it. Discord had twenty-six new alerts from twelve callers, but those are unscored.

R eleven, the Vin reversal levels study, is being scored. Real trades have two closed at an average of about a third of a risk unit. The placebo has four closed at nearly two. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, and the real trades must beat the placebo by at least about a seventh of a risk unit. So the placebo is ahead, and the sample is far too small to mean anything.

Five other studies are answered or need a better test.

CNBC reports Binance suffered a hack of about six point three billion dollars, which plausibly explains the selling. Oil settled around one hundred and two dollars, and energy edged up. CNBC reports Exxon and Chevron beat earnings expectations on strong refining profits.

Looking ahead, CNBC reports Amazon was down about seven percent and Intel down about twenty-five percent in premarket trading after earnings, and Investing.com says European shares dipped on AI cash-burn fears. That is a possible follow-through for tech, but it's one morning.

Concept of the day: the S&P 500 is weighted by company size, so a few huge stocks can pull the index down even when most members rise. Yesterday showed it clearly. About four hundred stocks advanced, yet the index fell, because Alphabet and other heavyweights dropped sharply. When the index and breadth disagree, ask whether the move is concentrated in a few names or genuinely broad. Here it was concentrated, which is often less worrying than a decline led by many stocks.

AlphaThread

Health first. Three of your paper stores each restarted three times in the last day: copy Mordy, flow levels, and flow levels futures. All three are running now, after restarting early this morning. None is halted, and there were no reconciliation breaks. Snapshots are fresh.

No trades opened or closed in the last day.

Some research moved. Your free options data survey now has MarketData.app adopted as a one-year backfill. The study of Instagram creators' stock calls is active, as you asked. The put spread study is dead as a premium edge, since the profit was just market beta. The variance premium study survives narrowly, but its straddle can never trade live. The iron butterfly follow-up is dead, because the wings cost more than the premium. And the insider cluster buys study is pre-registered, waiting on you to approve a contact string for the SEC before it can run.

Thirteen new ideas landed in the inbox, mostly about index drawdowns, end-of-October seasonality into year-end, and FOMC day behavior. The inbox holds sixty-two ideas, twenty-nine of them queued.

Now the roll call. Nothing is live yet. Your broker account is still at the lowest options permission level, so live trading is blocked.

On paper, your demo put spread sleeve has five closed trades and is up about twenty-three dollars. One position is still open. It sits at five of twenty trades and twelve of ninety days toward going live, and its research gate is not met.

Copy Mordy, version zero point three, has no trades yet. It is four days in, so zero of twenty trades and four of ninety days.

Flow levels, version zero point three, has two closed trades and is up about eleven dollars. That is two of twenty trades and three of ninety days.

Flow levels futures, version zero point one, started yesterday with no trades. It is zero of ninety days. It also cannot be promoted live as it stands, because its research session allowed uncovered short legs.

One honest note: paper profit is filled at mid-price, so treat it as an upper bound, not evidence for going live.

On research, a few items are waiting. The gap detection findings are waiting on your review. The Rivian timestamp question needs your approval for one probe to close it. The Discord copy-trading study has nine calls against the forty it needs, with no hint of an edge, so the paper forward test will answer it. Discord had twenty-six new alerts from twelve callers, but those are unscored.

R eleven, the Vin reversal levels study, is being scored. Real trades have two closed at an average of about a third of a risk unit. The placebo has four closed at nearly two. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, and the real trades must beat the placebo by at least about a seventh of a risk unit. So the placebo is ahead, and the sample is far too small to mean anything.

Five other studies are answered or need a better test.

item.title: pod — Thu, Oct 29
item.description:
School

Nothing is overdue, and nothing is due today or tomorrow. The next deadline is your Physics homework, HW nine, due Saturday night at eleven fifty-nine. That's about seventy hours from now, and it's worth ten points.

Then on Monday night at midnight, you have two Prokaryotic Cell quizzes, Quiz nine and Quiz ten. Each is worth fifteen points.

One physics note: your professor is away at a conference, so office hours today are covered by Neerav, the learning assistant. He'll be in the interaction area near room twenty-one eighty.

The deadline watcher had a rough stretch. It couldn't log in to Canvas for forty-five checks in a row, from early Wednesday morning until just after midnight, so deadlines weren't being watched during that time. After it recovered, it found the physics lab prelab on Impulse and Momentum about eighteen hours overdue. It completed and submitted it at about quarter to one. All answers were correct, but with the late penalty you got four out of five.

On grades, the Simple Harmonic Motion prelab came back at four and a half out of five. Your Abstract Algebra chapter one homework was graded too, showing a score of three with no points listed, so that one is hard to read. The physics lab sits at an A.

Two classes are below a B. Linear Algebra is at sixty-seven and a half percent, a D plus. Abstract Algebra is at seventy percent. Prokaryotic Cell is an A minus, and Physics is a B plus.

In email, Denise Dixon wrote about your FLATS exam. She says she's assuming you don't want to take the exam scheduled for today, and that when you're ready, you'll need to register again with BYU and the proctoring service. If you do plan to take it, you'll want to sort that out right away.

Perusall has also sent repeated reminders that Assignment nine in Prokaryotic Cell isn't complete. It's labeled for the graduate section only, so it may not apply to you.

Coming up, Emerging Scholars applications are due Sunday, and Florida Undergraduate Research Conference abstracts are due Monday. Monday from ten to two at the Reitz Union, there's a financial aid help event for the next year's FAFSA.

For registration, Spring registration opens tomorrow at two in the afternoon, and you have no holds. Your automatic registration plan is set up with six classes, and it will try to add them the moment the window opens.

The most important thing today is to sort out your FLATS exam status, since that email says the exam was scheduled for today.

Projects

Four things need you today, and one more is just a date.

Discord feed first, because it is the one flagged as a problem. The five a.m. health step failed again, the second morning in a row. The listener is running and connected, but it still reports one unfilled gap. You need to read today's Discord log to see why the health step failed.

AlphaThread is still blocked on the same two tasks. For the insider cluster-buy backtest, you need to give the contact email for the SEC user agent. You also need to decide whether phase two runs on yfinance prices, which are survivor-biased. For the task of finding more handles, four questions remain. Who adds the profits handle to the handles file? Do you want velocity options added? Should its Discord invite go to the invite scraper? And do you want any more discovery profile reads?

For kalq, there are five founder questions from the overnight report. Should AI mode require a PIN? How does PIN recovery work? What is the fallback quote from a Notified Body? How long is the security update period? And what is the security email address? A later commit records founder answers, so some of these may already be settled. That was not checked. The publish date task and the PreProduct admin work also still wait on you. Separately, the F C C re-check cannot run before tomorrow. The overnight run picks it up, so nothing is needed from you there.

Now the projects, starting with AlphaThread. Your runner has been up about sixty-three hours, and the paper database was written to about an hour ago. There are no alerts. Yesterday had no commits, but today there are fifteen. The broker decision was accepted and merged: Interactive Brokers is primary, gated on spreads permission, with Alpaca second. On the futures simulation, the launcher template and a proposed watchdog block landed, and one success criterion flipped to done. On the lane sleeve, a futures version of the flow levels strategy was built and registered in the hosts, and another success criterion flipped. The flow levels strategy now sizes positions by estimated loss at the stop, and the research note records results from Tuesday. The copy, flow levels and scoring paper runs all finished fine, and one reel note was filed. Next up is the live acceptance for the sizing work, which you run yourself, then fixing a flaky paper-fallback test. The many auto-discovered AlphaThread worktrees all show the same fifteen commits. One of them has uncommitted changes.

Calculators, also called kalq, had a better night. Yesterday's run timed out, but this one finished fine. Seven queued tasks are done, across twelve commits on tonight's branch, which is not pushed. The function, database and key guard tests all pass. A new task was queued to add belief-shift fields to the creative briefs, from a reel, and two reel notes were triaged. Three ready tasks are still blocked. Yesterday's attorney search, shell look and Wonderful PCB reply questions no longer appear in the needs list, but the report does not say whether they were answered. Next are the F C C re-check tomorrow, re-exporting the external firmware P D F before sharing it, and a browser check of the EUR-Lex texts the tools could not read.

IG ideas is fine. The watcher ran at six and analysed three new posts, from the trading fraternity and delta trend trading accounts. That produced two call rows and no new ideas. The inbox holds forty-nine ideas, one queued. As always, creator claims are untested hypotheses.

Back to Discord feed. The overnight curate step applied a new watch list: one hundred thirty-three channels across eleven servers. That change is uncommitted. Four servers were judged not worth watching.

Reel-bot, which had failures yesterday, does not appear in today's report.

The one problem repeating two days running is the Discord health failure, so start there.

item.title: pod — Wed, Oct 28
item.description:
Projects

Several things need you today, mostly on calculators.

First, the overnight run timed out after six hours and was stopped at seven. Four tasks were finished and reported at ten past one, so check nothing was lost after that. Second, there are blocking questions. You need to decide when to run the attorney clearance search for the 82MS look, which shell look to use, and what the fallback is if the attorney flags the stock shell. You also need to decide whether to send the first reply to Wonderful PCB. It's drafted and unsent, with the FCC line narrowed to Part 15B. Third, the PreProduct launch needs you in the PreProduct and Notifications admin screens, and the Judge.me login or token is still missing. The FCC vote is tomorrow, and the re-check can't run before Friday.

On AlphaThread, two tasks are still blocked on you, unchanged since yesterday. For the insider cluster-buy backtest, you need to say whether your email can be the SEC contact, and whether to run phase two now on the survivor-biased prices. Yesterday's recommendation was yes to both. For the handle search, you need to decide who adds rp dot profits to the handles file, whether to add velocity options, whether to feed its Discord invite to the scraper, and whether to allow more profile reads. Yesterday's recommendation was an interactive session adds the line, yes, yes, no.

On Discord feed, the health check failed again at five this morning, with one unfilled listener gap. Deletes inside the gap are invisible. The listener is running and connected.

One note, no action needed. Reel-bot had eight failed runs yesterday afternoon on three reels. A later run succeeded at four this morning and filed all three.

Now the projects. AlphaThread is quiet compared with yesterday's big merges. There are no new commits, and the branch is clean. Three paper runs finished fine, and reel-bot filed three notes. Next up is the live acceptance for the signal sleeve, the one open task in that spec, which you run yourself. After that, someone needs to fix the flaky paper-fallback test. Health is good. The runner has been up about thirty-nine hours, and there were no alerts in the last day.

Calculators has an overnight branch with the four finished tasks, not yet pushed. Yesterday, the supplier quote work, including the quote breakdown, a draft reply and the firmware spec, was merged on the remote. Research turned up two findings. The old Casio design patents from two thousand three to two thousand five have expired, but a family filed in twenty nineteen runs to about twenty thirty-five, which is an inference. And the Espressif S3 modules have a single modular FCC grant, though a handheld likely needs a SAR step. Reel-bot filed one note, and two files are uncommitted. The referral and review-hold questions from yesterday no longer appear. Next, the FCC re-check waits until Friday. The browser session for the FCC exhibits and the design search is still pending, and the landed cost gets rerun once Sunny answers. The privacy recheck still needs a publish date.

IG ideas is fine. The watcher ran at six, analysed one new post and created no new ideas. The newest idea is still the cyber ETF fade. The inbox holds forty-nine ideas, and one is queued.

Discord feed updated its watch list. It's now one hundred thirty-three channels across eleven servers, down from one hundred thirty-five. Two were removed, daily charting and getting started on whop, and none were added. The change is uncommitted. Next is looking at that gap.

The biggest clock is the FCC vote tomorrow, so the calculators decisions come first.

item.title: pod — Tue, Oct 27
item.description:
Projects

You have items waiting on AlphaThread, the Discord feed, and kalq.

Starting with AlphaThread. Two work items have been blocked on you since yesterday morning. The first is the search for more people to follow. It has four questions. Someone needs to add one profile handle to the handles file, because the worker is blocked from editing it. A second handle needs adding too. The Discord invite for the first handle needs to go to the scraper on the burner account. And it asks whether it may read more profiles beyond the original ten. The worker recommends an interactive session adds the line, then yes, yes, and no.

The second blocked item is the research pre-registration. It asks whether your email can be the contact in the S E C download header. The worker already used it for the test probe without approval. It also asks whether to run the second download phase now on the free price data, which is survivor biased. The recommendation is yes to both.

One more note. A worker run yesterday morning ended failed, with no log line added and a dirty worktree. Both tasks it touched are recorded as done, and later runs ended fine, the latest early this morning.

On the Discord feed, it's the same problem as yesterday. The listener is running and connected, but it has one unfilled gap, and the five o'clock health check failed again. Deletes inside that gap are invisible until it's filled.

For kalq, there are four founder questions. First, the referral limit per referrer. The recommendation is ten for life, for now. Second, friend bonus credits. Recommended: none at launch. Third, the review hold buffer. Recommended: add seven days for shipping. Fourth, when to promote the short video experiment. Recommended: once product footage exists. You also still need to provide the Judge.me login or token to finish the review check. Separately, the reel bot failed three times yesterday afternoon on one video. That video was filed unanalysed, and later runs were fine.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread had a big night. The paper broker running on live market data is merged to main, and its validation passed all fifty-three checks. The futures simulation work finished all five lanes and merged into its branch. The flow levels strategy is built, with its research pre-registered. Two queue tasks finished. A new reel note was filed on a noise band intraday momentum strategy on SPY. The creator claims a Sharpe of one point three three, but that's untested. Next up is fixing a flaky paper fallback test. The only open task in the flow levels spec is the live acceptance run, which only you can do. Health is fine. The paper runner is up and there were no alerts. Two worktrees now have uncommitted files, nine in the sleeve lane and two in the flow research branch. Yesterday all were clean.

On kalq, the overnight run finished on its own branch, which is not pushed. It added referral codes, held review credits until the return window ends, put an encrypted key copy step into the over the air update runbook, and added tests for hidden reviews and referral concurrency. Posts making claims now get a clear reject reason. The database changes are local only. Tests are up to two hundred eighty-six for functions, two hundred seventy-three for the database, and twenty-five for the key guard. Once you answer the buffer question, the shipping buffer goes into the config. With your okay in an interactive session, the four new database changes can be applied to the dev project, four functions deployed, and a smoke test run. The F C C re-check can't start before Friday.

Instagram ideas is fine. The watcher found one new post and no new ideas. There are forty-nine ideas in the inbox, and one is queued so far.

On the Discord feed, the watch list refreshed to one hundred thirty-five channels across eleven servers, with no change in visible channels.

In roblox-workbench, one new commit adds a multi-client testing harness.

That's the picture. The two AlphaThread unblocks and the kalq answers are the quickest wins.

item.title: pod — Mon, Oct 26
item.description:
Projects

You have a lot waiting this morning, and two of the items are failures.

First, Discord feed. The health check failed in the five o'clock run, and the listener has one unfilled gap. Deletes inside that gap are invisible. The listener itself is connected and running. You need to look at the failure and decide how to fill the gap.

Second, ops. The morning questions run failed again yesterday at nine because it could not start the Claude session. That is the second day in a row, and no later run is recorded in the last twenty-four hours.

For AlphaThread, three blocked queue items still wait on your answers. One is the route for the second parity result. One is the approach for detecting and deleting partial daily candles. One is the handle discovery that found no dated callers. The final live acceptance task for spec twenty-two is also yours to run, and merging to main needs your confirmation.

For kalq, two overnight questions. Check the Instagram brand professional account for the Trial toggle, the follower count, and the three-second view rate. Then run the git hooks path setting on your PC clone. The photo test is due this week and needs a key with a provider-side cap of fifteen dollars or less. The FCC re-check cannot start before October thirtieth, and the vote is October twenty-ninth.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread is blocked on those answers, but the paper runner is healthy. It has been up about seven hours, with no alerts in the last day. Two commits landed. The interpreter prompt is now version two, so a list of price levels no longer counts as a trade statement. A research note also pre-registers Vin's free reversal levels as a reaction trade. The copy-mordy paper run and signals ingest each recorded a start with no end yet. Yesterday's worry about signals ingest no longer appears in your list. Next is running paper sessions until you have ten fresh regular-hours sessions. After that, the roadmap points to the pricing ladder.

Calculators, or kalq, had a good overnight run. Six tasks finished on the overnight branch, with all tests passing, and nothing was applied to Supabase. item.title: pod — Sun, Oct 25
item.description:
Projects

Three things need you today, and the first two are about overnight failures.

First, AlphaThread. The watchdog found the signals ingest down and restarted it twice, around one in the morning. No end is recorded for those runs, so it is unclear whether it is running now. Check it.

Second, the Instagram watcher. Instagram locked it out until three thirty-three this afternoon, and the six o'clock run stopped. You were notified. Do nothing until the lockout ends. Never bypass a challenge. If Instagram shows one, clear it by hand with a headed browser session. Then rerun the ideas script.

Third, the morning questions run failed yesterday at nine because it could not start the Claude session. No later run is recorded. Today's nine o'clock run is the check.

Also for AlphaThread, one blocked task needs a choice. It is the parity run result with settlement prices. Route A adds the settlement scoring as a fourth permitted cause in the manifest test and rewrites one capture. Route B rewrites the realized profit and loss in four fixtures, with a pinning test. Route C closes it as won't-do. There are two side questions. The suggestion is yes to the test comment naming the three causes plus settlement scoring, and no to adding a settlement prices table to the fixtures.

For kalq, create the two Shopify pages, the photo math solver and the AI calculator with chat. The calculator page should wait for the keyword call. Both still show placeholder price and credit text until that decision is made. The photo test is due this week. Create the dedicated key with a hard provider-side cap of fifteen dollars or less, then run it with friends. The FCC vote is Thursday. The recheck of the FCC rules cannot start before Friday.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread is on attention. The live paper run is healthy. The runner is up, the paper database was written to this morning, and there were no alerts in runner logs. A lot landed since yesterday. The copy trading tool reached version point three, which pins the allowed channels and skips signals from channels not on the list. Version point two added skipping of late, already-known signals and an optional label in alert titles. A new decision record says a sleeve's policies run only at its own wakeups. All five user stories of the signal sleeve are delivered, plus the backfill import and ingest launcher, and the final analysis pass is done. Go-live notes for the first session are written. The market was closed, so no entries yet. The backfill study verdict is that it needs more data, nine of forty. A reel note was filed. It judged the hedge-fund reverse-engineering claims as hype, keeping only a generic backtest validation checklist. Next, you run paper sessions until ten fresh regular-hours entries. Two other queue tasks stay blocked. One is repairing partial daily candles. The other is finding more handles, which needs your approval before any scraping.

Calculators, kalq, is on attention. The overnight run finished seven tasks. They cover the short-form video stack, the keyword page draft and templates, the over the air update runbook with a key rotation plan, the free credits research, scripts for the students organic test, and supplier signing questions. Your founder answers are recorded, with three new decisions and one reworded. Functions tests pass at two hundred fifty-eight, database tests at two hundred forty-two. Twelve commits sit on the overnight branch, not pushed. Next are the free credits backend, free hook testing before a thousand followers, and key storage with the keyword map. The pre-order launch setup still needs your browser admin access. Open founder items remain on counsel, supplier samples, landed cost, compliance, and AI provider accounts.

IG ideas moved from fine to blocked because of the lockout. There are no new ideas today. The inbox holds forty-eight, one queued.

Discord feed is healthy. The listener is connected, with no unfilled gaps. The watch list now covers a hundred and one channels across eleven servers. Joining servers is by hand now.

Roblox workbench has five new commits on main and twenty-one uncommitted files.

The remaining AlphaThread worktrees are clean, with nothing of their own.

Start with the ingest check, then let the lockout run out.

item.title: pod — Sat, Oct 24
item.description:
Projects

You have a few things waiting today. Most urgent is the calculators project.

For calculators, the photo test is due this week. You need to create a dedicated AI key with a provider-side spending cap of fifteen dollars or less, then run the test with two or three friends. The pre-order launch setup also needs you in the PreProduct and Notifications admin screens before the first real listing. You're also asked whether to reword the decision record so three items don't read as confirmed. And the federal communications check can't start before October thirtieth, since the vote is October twenty-ninth.

For AlphaThread, three blocked queue tasks need your answers, with recommended answers already filled in. They cover the scale route for the parity results, repair of partial daily candles, and handle discovery. Also, the fifth and last live paper session is Monday. After that, the final validation run is yours to start, and it closes out the run.

Now the projects. Starting with AlphaThread, which moved from blocked to attention. Session four of five is done. The underlying stopped at the open and there was one open. The books agreed all day, with twenty-five checkpoints, no breaks and no faults. Your runner has been up about eighty-six hours, the database was written to this morning, and there have been no alerts. On the operator interface branch, the live success criterion now passes, and the authentication page offers re-authentication before the refresh token expires. One oddity: no task completion events were recorded for the work queue. Next is Monday's session, then final validation.

Calculators had a good overnight run, with seven tasks done. There was research on the trademark position for the ChatGPT calculator keyword page, and the low-credit rule is built. The emailed export link is built too. The drafts now treat pre-order and waitlist together, and the theme has a waitlist form next to pre-order. There was also research on short-form editing and scheduling tools for the Instagram and TikTok pipeline, plus the over the air update check and a firmware spec catch-up. That's seventeen commits on the overnight branch, not yet pushed. Tests pass, two hundred fifty-eight for functions and two hundred sixteen for the database. The five new database migrations exist only locally. Queued next are research on a free-first short-form stack, a draft keyword page for the AI calculator with chat, and a publishing runbook with a signing-key rotation plan. With your okay, the migrations can go to the dev project and the changed functions can roll out. Two things are stuck. The export confirmation page needs a Supabase custom domain, and the price is still to be checked. The privacy recheck still needs a publish date. The AI provider retention questions from yesterday no longer appear on your list.

IG ideas ran fine at six. It found no new posts, so no ideas today. The inbox holds forty-eight ideas, with one queued.

Discordscrape has fifteen commits on master. Live signals now come with phone alerts and a hook, along with new commands to watch, peek, follow, and capture live chat. There's also a way to search and read the collected corpus. Free channels from Invest With Mordy and The Flow Project were added.

Pod now records run start, run end and publish events to the shared operations log. Reel-inbox does the same for ingested, filed and finished items, and it now marks notes as requested when you send a queue-this message.

The remaining AlphaThread worktrees are idle and clean, covering pricing ladder, charts, health, recorder, runner, interface, docs, and the worker.

Overall, the live run is steady, and what's holding things up is mostly your answers and admin steps.

item.title: pod — Fri, Oct 23
item.description:
Projects

Here's what needs you today.

Start with AlphaThread. Today is session four of five in the live paper run. Check the watchdog report at four forty-seven this afternoon. The final validation can only run after session five. Three queued tasks are also still waiting on you. One needs a route chosen for the parity result scale in the second test set. One needs a decision on detecting partial daily candles and deleting them through the Runner. The last is handle discovery, where the proposal is to add none and park that research item.

Next, calculators, kalq. Six yes or no questions on AI provider retention are in the overnight report. They include requesting zero data retention and applying the latest migration to dev. Until you answer, the privacy wording stays blocked. The pre-order launch setup also needs your admin access in the PreProduct and Notifications screens before the first real listing. And keep a date in mind. The FCC vote is next Thursday, October twenty-ninth, so the re-check can't start before Friday, October thirtieth.

Now the projects.

AlphaThread has moved from attention to blocked, because of those three queue tasks. The paper run is healthy. Session three was recorded with twenty-four instants, no breaks, and no faults. The operator interface screenshot review passed, and validation came back with seventy-two passes, no failures, and six skipped. There was also a new commit with the backtest robustness scoping docs. Your runner has been up about sixty-two hours with no alerts in the last day. The quiet logs are just because the market is closed, not a fault. After sessions four and five comes the final validation. The pricing ladder and operator interface branches are still unmerged, with no dates given.

Calculators, kalq, had eighteen commits. The pre-order trial is done, which clears yesterday's Shopify Payments blocker. The migration that drops the old rate limiter is applied to dev, and smoke tests passed sixteen out of sixteen. Guide articles now have breadcrumbs. The Klaviyo outbox is deployed to dev, and privacy tests one through four pass on the unpublished dev theme. A research pass on AI provider retention was done, which produced your six questions. There's also a new idea queued for an Instagram and TikTok content pipeline, with reel inbox folders added. Still ahead are the browser privacy signal test and the UK and EU VPN test. The final privacy recheck waits on a publish date. Many founder items remain open, including supplier samples, compliance, landed cost, the product page, policies, and the weekly report app.

IG ideas is fine. The watcher ran at six this morning and analysed one new post, but produced no new ideas. Yesterday's four newest ideas are still unqueued. The inbox holds forty-eight ideas, with one queued in total. As always, the creator claims are untested hypotheses.

Reel inbox has one new commit, adding a local Whisper speech engine and routing into project inboxes.

The remaining AlphaThread worktrees, including the pricing ladder, are clean and idle, with nothing new.

The one thing that can't slip today is the afternoon watchdog check.

item.title: pod — Thu, Oct 22
item.description:
Projects

You have two projects waiting on you today.

First, AlphaThread. You still need to pick a route for the blocked parity result scale. The queue suggests adding an earlier queued fix as a fourth permitted cause. Two other answers are also waiting. One is whether to build a detector for partial daily candles, which you would run with no live session. The other is the handles question, where the queue suggests adding none and parking that research item.

Second, the calculators project. Turn on Shopify Payments under Settings, then Payments. It still blocks the pre-order trial. Then create the read-only Dev Dashboard app for the weekly report, and put its three Shopify settings, store, client ID and client secret, in the repo env file. Shopify no longer allows new admin custom apps. You also have six overnight questions in today's report, including how long to keep the Klaviyo outbox and where dead-row alerts should go. Lastly, the overnight work sits on an unpushed branch. The new Klaviyo migration needs an interactive session to apply and redeploy.

One date to keep in mind. The F C C re-check cannot start before October thirtieth, because the vote is October twenty-ninth.

Now the projects. AlphaThread first. Session two of the five-session paper run is done, and it was clean. It had thirty instants, twenty-three reconciliations agreed, no breaks and no faults. The trim policy closed three of nine spreads, and the books agreed all day. The Runner has been up about thirty-eight hours with no alerts, so yesterday's worry about duplicate runners has not recurred. Commits dropped from one hundred thirteen to one hundred five, almost all operator interface work. Next is three more sessions, then the final validation script, which must exit clean with nothing skipped or failed.

On the calculators project, the overnight run finished four tasks and one partly. The Klaviyo outbox is built, with retries, backoff, dead-row alerts and privacy deletion. Tests passed: two hundred fifteen for functions and one hundred ninety-six for the database, up from one hundred sixty-four and one hundred seventy. The keyword pages now soften the photo claim, and the privacy and AI terms wording matches the code. The weekly report token setup is also done. The pre-order trial is only partly done, with docs and install steps, and none of it is verified. Yesterday's photo test and pre-order questions no longer appear on your list. Work merged to main yesterday includes the shared rate limiter, the scheduled jobs, the Anthropic adapter, and pair-claim sign-in. The dev smoke test passed fifteen of fifteen, and AI is on under a two dollar daily cap. Still blocked are the pre-order trial, the deploy, and one task waiting on a publish date. In your interactive session, also fix the flaky Klaviyo test and create the guides blog in the dev theme.

IG ideas is healthy. The watcher ran at six and found three new idea cards that are readable, though its status says four. The top one scored three. It says that when the S and P five hundred fund runs far ahead of equal weight, the gap tends to close. The other two scored two. One covers deep drawdowns after large retail I P Os. The other covers beaten-down laggers after a volatility spike. None were queued today, and there are forty-eight in the inbox. Remember that the creators' claims are untested. Two new posts were found, and none wait for a transcript.

The remaining AlphaThread worktrees are idle and clean. The pod repo is idle too, with one commit pinning the publishing git login.

Nothing is failing this morning. The open items are your decisions and the Shopify setup.

AlphaThread comes first. The second of five live paper run sessions is due today. Check that the Runner stays up through market hours, since the first session had a duplicate Runner incident. Three queue questions are also still blocked on you. One needs a route pick, a, b, or c, and the suggestion is a. One asks whether to write a read-only partial candle detector. The suggestion is yes, then delete mismatches through a Runner command while no session is live. The last needs your answers on handles, and the suggestion is to add none and park that research item.

For calculators, you need to turn on Shopify Payments. PreProduct and pre-orders depend on it, and the next install step waits on it. You also need to create the capped API key, fifteen dollars maximum, and take the three trial photos for the photo test. Finally, three pre-order questions are open. Should credit packs share a cart? Should delay emails go through an app or Klaviyo? And which launch sale mode do you want?

Now the projects. AlphaThread first. The first paper session is recorded. It passed its success criterion with a position open, but the duplicate Runner incident is the caution. Four more consecutive trading sessions remain. The Runner is healthy, up almost fourteen hours, with no alerts in the last day. Last night's log shows two heartbeat ping timeouts, which are not a fault on their own. The pricing ladder spec also passed its final gate: forty-two passes, no failures, one skip, across more than four thousand tests. Two final tasks there are left for you. IG ideas is healthy. The watcher ran at about six this morning and found nine new ideas, none queued to AlphaThread today. Four score three and two score two, all defined and executable live. There are forty-four ideas in total, with one queued overall. No posts are waiting for a transcript, down from four yesterday. The repo has three uncommitted items.

The pricing ladder, operator interface, and worker branches are clean and just share AlphaThread's history.

Today mostly comes down to the Runner staying up and the Shopify Payments switch.

item.title: pod — Tue, Oct 20
item.description:
Projects

You have items on two projects today, and one is time-sensitive.

Start with AlphaThread. The five-session paper count begins tomorrow. It was pushed back from yesterday because the runner was restarted just after midnight onto the merged code. The final validation steps stay with you. There are also three questions waiting. First, four parity fixtures differ only in the decimal scale of realized profit and loss. You can add the settlement price change as a fourth permitted cause, rewrite the fixtures, or close it as won't do. The queue default is to add the cause. Second, approve a read-only detector for partial daily candles in the operator price candles. The suggestion is yes, with any mismatches deleted by a command you run when no session is live. Third, no candidate Instagram handle makes dated calls. The suggestion is to add none and park that research item.

Now calculators. First, the photo quality test. Say whether about eight to twelve dollars is fine for a first live pass, and who creates a dedicated key with a spending cap set by the provider. The live run needs an interactive session. Second, the pre-order switch. You need to define what counts as a sample passing, and who signs it off. The delay notice is queued before the product page switches. Third, turn on the customer privacy setting in your Shopify settings. The dev theme push was approved today and also needs an interactive session. Finally, the F C C vote is October twenty-ninth, and the re-check can't start before October thirtieth.

On AlphaThread, yesterday's health warning is gone. The runner is up, has been running about six hours, and the paper database was written to this morning. There were no alerts in the last day. Overnight, nearly all the queued work finished, including settlement prices, the netted lot fix, the login state and security check, and the runner stop and heartbeat. The review fixes and worker branch merged into the main spec branch, and the test baseline is three thousand eight hundred twenty-six passing. On the pricing ladder spec, the first twenty-one tasks are done, and work continues from the twenty-second.

On calculators, the overnight run finished eight tasks across twelve commits, none pushed yet. The firmware spec task that was blocked yesterday is done, and the firmware and privacy questions from yesterday no longer need you. Four new decisions were recorded. Function tests show one hundred thirty-seven passing, and database tests one hundred sixty-two. One flaky database test could not be reproduced. Next up are answer replay with an alert digest, an email alert sink, photo size wording, the pre-order delay notice, and a keyword merge for the planner. Still blocked are the privacy policy, which needs a publish date and open items resolved, and the F C C re-check.

IG ideas is healthy. The watcher ran at about six this morning with no errors and found eleven new ideas, bringing the inbox to thirty-five. Six are visible, all scored three and live-executable. They cover high yield bonds at a low and later stock drawdowns, long Treasuries bouncing after a record losing streak, silver catching up to chips, July strength in the S and P ETF, bond volatility ahead of drawdowns, and utilities and staples beating after a software selloff. The creators' claims are untested. None of those were queued to AlphaThread. Five new posts were found, four of them waiting for transcripts.

The other three AlphaThread worktrees and the pod project have nothing new to report.

The one clock running is tomorrow's session count.

item.title: TEST A — Clean (af_heart)
item.description:
TEST A — Clean (af_heart)

New script format (cold open, signposting, closing recap) in af_heart with natural sentence and paragraph pauses, an intro sting, chimes between segments and an outro. No background music, no think pauses; a decision marker becomes a short silence.

Script

Today: four things need you, and the biggest is the AlphaThread paper run that is supposed to start counting today.

First, AlphaThread. You need to start the five-session paper run today. It needs five consecutive trading sessions beginning this Monday, with at least one open and close. After that comes a repeat with a position open, and then the final validation. The Schwab token was assumed to lapse on Sunday, and it is unclear whether you renewed it.

Second, still AlphaThread. You need to check that the runner is really active. The process has been up for about forty-three hours. But the newest log, written sixteen hours ago, says only that the runner finished. The data does not say whether that is normal.

Third, kalq. You need to answer the privacy follow-ups. They cover which ad pixel events and hashed email go to ad partners, and pixels on by default in the US but only after accept in the EU and UK. They also cover the thirteen-plus and under-sixteen position, the split between eighteen-plus in the Terms of Sale and thirteen-plus for accounts, and export through the account page only.

[[think]]

Fourth, also kalq, three smaller asks. Answer the firmware questions: whether over the air updates are a launch requirement, the signing key, the api address, and the photo limit. Tell the briefing what came out of Sunday's Shenzhen meeting, since the outcome isn't recorded. Then give the alert email address and sender, and say whether to push to the dev theme and turn on the customer privacy setting.

[[think]]

Now, what changed.

AlphaThread is flagged for attention. On Sunday afternoon, three commits landed on main. The OptionsDX importer is merged, and that roadmap item is marked done. No tasks changed. Seventy-one are done, and two remain open, both of which only you can close. Next is the five-session run, then the validation run and recording the counts. After the merge, the next spec will be number twenty, the pricing ladder. Health shows a warning, the runner oddity you just heard about. No alerts went out in the last day, and there were no collection errors.

kalq is blocked. The overnight run finished six tasks. The privacy policy now reflects the four new decisions. The backend has the thirteen-plus check, consent purge, and an alert stub. Data retention purges are in, along with a test for parallel sessions against account deletion, and a closer for stuck credit reservations that records spend before making the call. Footer privacy links are built in local theme files, not pushed. Sunday also brought the four decisions, a supplier log update, and research on four G and SIM feasibility. Tests pass: one hundred twenty-nine for functions and one hundred fifty-two for the database.

Still unverified: real Supabase behaviour, the scheduled jobs, and the theme links in a browser. Next up is a run-through on the Supabase dev project and a spend-reserve test with concurrency. The firmware work waits on your answers, and the privacy page still needs a publish date. The FCC vote is October twenty-ninth, and that re-check can't start before October thirtieth. Nothing to do on that today.

If you remember one thing, start the AlphaThread paper run today, after confirming the runner is really active.

They also cover the thirteen-plus and under-sixteen position, the split between eighteen-plus in the Terms of Sale and thirteen-plus for accounts, and export through the account page only.

[[think]]

Fourth, also kalq, three smaller asks. Answer the firmware questions: whether over the air updates are a launch requirement, the signing key, the api address, and the photo limit. Tell the briefing what came out of Sunday's Shenzhen meeting, since the outcome isn't recorded. Then give the alert email address and sender, and say whether to push to the dev theme and turn on the customer privacy setting.

[[think]]

Now, what changed.

AlphaThread is flagged for attention. On Sunday afternoon, three commits landed on main. The OptionsDX importer is merged, and that roadmap item is marked done. No tasks changed. Seventy-one are done, and two remain open, both of which only you can close. Next is the five-session run, then the validation run and recording the counts. After the merge, the next spec will be number twenty, the pricing ladder. Health shows a warning, the runner oddity you just heard about. No alerts went out in the last day, and there were no collection errors.

kalq is blocked. The overnight run finished six tasks. The privacy policy now reflects the four new decisions. The backend has the thirteen-plus check, consent purge, and an alert stub. Data retention purges are in, along with a test for parallel sessions against account deletion, and a closer for stuck credit reservations that records spend before making the call. Footer privacy links are built in local theme files, not pushed. Sunday also brought the four decisions, a supplier log update, and research on four G and SIM feasibility. Tests pass: one hundred twenty-nine for functions and one hundred fifty-two for the database.

Still unverified: real Supabase behaviour, the scheduled jobs, and the theme links in a browser. Next up is a run-through on the Supabase dev project and a spend-reserve test with concurrency. The firmware work waits on your answers, and the privacy page still needs a publish date. The FCC vote is October twenty-ninth, and that re-check can't start before October thirtieth. Nothing to do on that today.

If you remember one thing, start the AlphaThread paper run today, after confirming the runner is really active.
